data:
Runink FACE: Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine. Logistics and fulfilment teams lose money and hours to shortages, damaged loads, missed claim windows and carrier invoices that don’t match the contract. Finding each case means reading across the warehouse system, the telematics feed and the paperwork by hand. FACE does that reading: it connects to the systems you already run, finds the cases, and drafts the claim, the evidence and the next step for a person to approve.
These docs are organised by what you are trying to do.
OverviewWhat FACE is, how it is built, and the vocabulary. Using FACEOne page per page in the app: Ask, Briefs, Options, Why, Actionable Twins, Settings. Data sourcesConnections, runners, and every supported connector. Analysis & evidenceHow findings, decisions and evidence documents are produced. Agent model cardsEach agent’s job, inputs, model and human oversight. Security & trustThe controls, how they work, and the scope of each. Operating FACEDeploying, configuring and troubleshooting an instance. gRPC API referenceEvery service and method, for integrators.
data.conventions-in-these-docs#Conventions in: Names of settings, environment variables, RPCs and error messages are copied from the product exactly. If a page and the product disagree, the product is right. Please tell us. Every analysis page ends with a Reading the results note, and every security page with the scope of its controls. Read those notes as carefully as the rest.

data:
You ask a question on Ask. FACE reads your connected sources and answers it, shows what you could do about it on Options, the rules and sources behind it on Why, and the actions it drafted on Actionable Twins, where a named person approves or rejects each one. This section explains how each of those results is produced and how to read it.
It is written for evaluators who need to decide whether those outputs can be trusted, so every statement here is taken from the backend code and its protobuf contract (semantics.v1), and names the RPC, field or variable it describes.
data.pages-in-this-section#Pages in this sect: Fetch pipelineWhat runs when you ask on Ask: phases, traces, SOPs, suggested questions and briefs. Sovereign modelsThe in-cluster model plane and ModelService. Structured outputTOON parsing into typed structs, and the one JSON exception. GroundingPer-tenant Direct Corpus Interaction over your own corpus. Evidence documents17 closed document kinds, each built from cited records. Action cards & moneyThe cards on Actionable Twins, options sent for approval, money and the decision trail. Statistics & MLEvery AnalysisService method and the ml library under it. Posture & maturityHealth scores, the domain graph and estate causal analysis. Simulation & twinsThe services behind Options and Actionable Twins, claims and returns. Twin ontology & graphEPCIS 2.0 + CBV classes, relations, identifiers and the device registry. Compliance, finance, operationsFindings, remediation orders and routing. Vision & CCTVFrame grading, class-conditioned detection, coordinates. Agents & oversightRalph loop, guardrails, judging ladder, human approval.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results:
Every page ends with a Reading the results note: what a result shows, and what stays with the person who acts on it. Throughout the contract, FACE puts the difference between “measured zero” and “not measured” on the wire, not in prose. You’ll see this in fields such as EvaluationMetrics.unmeasured_reason, FetchAnalysisResult.hypothesis_swarm_ran, AbsentFigure.reason, IngestSurveillanceFeedResponse.detection_note and AnalyzeEstateCausalResponse.answered. A client that shows a number should read its companion field first.
Connecting sources is covered in Data sources. Transport, identity and at-rest encryption are covered in Security. Full message definitions are in the API reference.
data.the-pipeline-at-a-glance#The pipeline at: flowchart LR A[Connected sources] -->|allowlisted reads| B[Extract & profile] B --> C[Cluster & EDAHDBSCAN · Prophet/ARIMA] C --> D[Phase 1posture + rules] D --> E[Phase 2hypothesis swarm] E --> F[Phase 3twins decision] F --> G[Judging ladder] G --> H[Action cards +evidence documents] H --> I{Actionable Twinsapprove / reject} I -->|approve| J[Seal chained intoappend-only lineage log] K[(Tenant corpusplain text, DCI)] -.grounding.-> D & E & F
data.two-rules-that-shape-everything-here#Two:
Sovereign inference only. Every text, vision and voice call goes to an OpenAI-compatible model plane served inside the FACE deployment’s own cluster (Runink’s shared machines on Lite, your own cloud or servers on Dedicated and Enterprise). FACE never calls an outside AI service on any plan, and it ships no model server of its own. If the plane is not configured, FACE refuses to start instead of running with nothing behind it. See Sovereign models.
Determination is separate from expression. Any output that a third party might act on, such as an evidence document or a remediation order, is built in two layers:
Determination is fixed arithmetic over cited records. No model is involved. Expression is optional prose that a model may draft, but only after the determination is frozen. The contract states it in one line: the model never decides what is true; it only phrases what was decided. See Evidence documents.

data:
An action card (ActionCard) is a recommended action waiting for a person to approve or reject it. You decide cards on Actionable Twins, where they sit in three lanes:
Waiting for you: cards that still need a decision. In flight: approved, with no final outcome recorded yet. Back: a final outcome is recorded (recovered in full or in part, or denied). Each lane’s heading counts its items and adds up the money its cards state. Cards that state no amount are counted apart, never as $0. The same cards appear at their place on the page’s Map view. Play chips filter the list (claims, disruptions, routes, fulfilment and the other plays).
Cards come from three places:
Deterministic derivers over the tenant’s records. These produce the twin cards and the evidence documents. The twins agent’s TOON output. An option a person sent for approval from Options (see Options sent for approval). Every card is served through TwinsService.
data.anatomy-of-a-card#Anatomy of a card: Field Meaning type The business domain and routing key. The derivers and handlers emit Compliance, Finance, Operations, Procurement and S&OP. Model-produced cards may carry another string, which clients treat as uncategorised. priority, impact, status status is Approved or Rejected once decided. Empty means pending. transaction_value The card’s contribution to the dollar headline (see below). Artifact fields One typed payload per artifact family: route_card, email_draft, calendar_invite, erp_update, claims_card, cold_chain_card, customs_clearance_card, and others. evidence_document One field for the whole evidence-document family. See Evidence documents. origin (ActionOrigin) Which stage produced the card, as the wire spells it (reconcile, fetch or simulate), with a run_id and a label. If it’s absent, the stage wasn’t recorded. It’s never inferred. judgement The judging ladder’s verdict, reached before the card was accepted. See Agents & oversight. authority (ActionAuthority) The approval the decision-authority policy requires: its tier, how many distinct named approvals, the rule that decided it and why. See Auditability & lineage. execution (ActionExecution) What approving will do on this instance, step by step, before anyone approves. records_only=true means approving records the decision and nothing else runs. decision_option Set on a card that is an option sent for approval from Options (see below). decision_trail Who decided the card, when, which way and why (see below). recovery_trail, latest_outcome What happened after the approval, as named people recorded it, and the last outcome in the decision log. These move a card from In flight to Back. GetActionQueue returns the pending queue by default. Pass status="Approved" or status="Rejected" to read back decided cards, and use workflow_type to filter on type.
data.deciding-a-card#Deciding a card:
ExecuteAction is the one place a person decides a card:
The decider is identified from the verified session. An approval is refused unless the session token’s subject can be verified. A rejection is recorded whatever the attribution says. A reason is required on rejection and optional on approval. Whitespace-only counts as empty. The limit is 2000 characters, and a longer reason is refused rather than truncated. On approval, the evidence document is sealed (see Sealing), and any executable artifacts run. The response reports what happened: decision_recorded: the decision was durably written. success: false only when an approval executed nothing. transaction_id: minted only on success. not_executed: tokens such as email:no_google_connector, calendar:not_implemented, erp:not_implemented or billing:charge_failed, one for each artifact that didn’t run. How a client should read the response. decision_recorded=true with success=false means the card is decided but nothing was executable. The client should stop, and must not retry. Genuine failures arrive as gRPC status errors instead.
data.money-one-headline-disjoint-buckets#Mone:
The money a lane’s heading shows on Actionable Twins is a sum of what its cards state. A sum can’t tell what the money is for, so FACE enforces a rule instead: two cards must never charge the same dollars.
A card contributes to a money total only if all three of these hold:
It has not been rejected. A rejection is a decision not to take the saving. Approved and pending cards both count. It carries a dollar value. An emissions card sets its value in kilograms of CO2e, so it contributes nothing to a money total. It is in a named charging bucket. A test (TestOnlyTheNamedCardFamiliesChargeTheHeadline) lists the closed set of buckets allowed to charge and says why each one owns its money. A new producer that charges without being added to that list fails the build. Adding it is where someone has to write down whose dollars they are.
data.options-sent-for-approval#Options sent f:
On Options, FACE compares the what-if options for one decision behind the selected run’s checks (HypothesisService.CompareOptions). Every option is scored on one shared measure with a 95% range. FACE marks one Recommended only when its range sits wholly below the next option’s and below the figure as measured. Otherwise it says No clear winner on this data and why. An option with no baseline is Not measured and is never ranked.
Send for approval calls SendToTwins with the decision, the option and the run. The server compares the options again and queues the option with the figures it computed itself. The card lands in Waiting for you on Actionable Twins and carries decision_option: the decision, the option’s lever and change, what it was measured to do, the figure as measured, and whether it was the recommended one. The response names the approval it needs: one named person, or two different named people.
Approving it records the decision and changes nothing by itself. It is never automatic.
Estimated and assumed effects are labelled apart. A lead-time option (for example, moving shipments to air) has its effect estimated from the shipments that took it, by regression adjustment, with its interval. A temperature option’s effect is the option’s own assumption: every reading is moved by the full change and checked again against its own limits, and the card states that how far the change really moves the readings is not estimated. An option the rows never took is Not measured, naming the data it needs.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: The headline is a sum of claims about money, not money received. It’s only as good as the cited records behind each card. decided_by doesn’t prove a human pressed a button. A person’s token driven by a script looks the same. decided_by_role separates a service account from a person’s session. The trail is a verified attribution, not a signature. It is written by the instance into a store the instance owns. A required reason proves someone typed something, not that it’s true or complete. An approval is not an execution receipt. Read transaction_id and not_executed. A recommended option is the clear winner on the rows read, not a guarantee. Read whether its effect was estimated or assumed before approving it.
data.savings-summary#Savings summary:
GetSavingsSummary returns two separate figures:
total_savings_usd: the pipeline. It counts savings on cards nobody has rejected. approved_savings_usd: the subset the operator has committed to. It’s always less than or equal to the total. Neither figure is “realised.” These figures do not record whether an approved action was carried out in the world, so no client may label either figure that way. What a person recorded after an approval is in the card’s recovery_trail and shows in the Back lane. The FACE app does not display GetSavingsSummary today; it is an API call.
data.the-charging-buckets#The charging bucket:
Four evidence-document kinds charge:
Kind The money it owns OSD_REPORT The cargo itself: units short plus units damaged, at the cited unit price. This is a loss already incurred. FNOL The reserve on a newly reported loss, only for claim numbers no claims card already charges. RATE_CON_ACCESSORIAL_AUDIT Accessorials invoiced above the signed rate confirmation. MSA_SLA_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT Service credits owed back under an SLA clause. Five twin-card families charge:
Card family The money it owns cold_chain_card Value at risk of the load on a reefer whose own readings broke a stated band. claims_card The reserve on an open claim. For billing alerts, the invoice amount due on an account. customs_clearance_card Demurrage or per-diem accrued by a hold. Never the duty and never the cargo. importer_of_record_card Duty and tax with no accountable party. cross_border_trucking_card Detention accrued at a crossing.
data.the-decision-trail#The decision trail:
ActionCard.decision_trail is a list of ActionDecision entries, and the last entry is the current decision. Each entry records:
decision: Approved or Rejected. decided_at: the server’s clock when the decision was recorded. decided_by: the verified sub claim of the deciding session, never a value the caller supplied. attribution (DeciderAttribution): how well the decider could be named. decided_by_role: the verified role. reason. A retried decision with the same content doesn’t add a new entry. The original entry is kept, including its original time. An operator who changes their mind gets a second entry.
data.value-ledger#Value ledger:
TwinsService.GetValueLedger returns, for the tenant and a period, the money FACE identified, what people approved and filed, what was recovered, and what expired unfiled. Recovered money is kept in two figures: what people entered, and what the operator’s own claims system states. Every figure names its basis, and a figure with no basis is “not measured”, never zero. The ledger bills nothing.
Where you see it: the line above the lanes on Actionable Twins (recovered this quarter against FACE’s fee, with the full ledger folded under it), and the money line at the top of Ask (owed to you, claim windows closing, waiting for your approval, recovered this quarter).
data.why-other-documents-keep-their-money-out:
Most evidence documents are about money another bucket already owns. A cargo loss survey, a notice of intent, a statement of position and a subrogation demand all concern the same cargo the OS&D report charges. A temperature excursion and a warranty audit concern the same load the cold-chain card charges. If they charged too, one loss would be counted several times, and the error would look like better news.
So those documents state their money in claimed_amount (what the document asks for) or exposure_amount (value at risk, not yet lost), and no total reads those fields. The reader still sees the figure; the headline just doesn’t add it up twice.

data:
FACE’s agents draft; a person decides. Nothing an agent proposes is sent, filed or paid until a named person approves it on Actionable Twins, and FACE recommends an option only when it is the clear winner on the data.
The agents are prompt templates driven by one orchestrator, the Ralph loop. What an agent may do is bounded in four places:
the guardrails on its input, an authorisation gate on its tools, a judging ladder on the actions it proposes, a human decision before anything is adopted.
data.agent-templates#Agent templates:
The loop serves these agent templates: twins, hypothesis, rules_recon, ai_posture, compliance, finance, claims, claims_leakage, fraud_detection, fulfilment, reverse_logistics, route_twin, predictive_maintenance, telemetry, documentation, vision, voice, cop and self_healing.
Five more templates are refused by the loop on purpose, because they only phrase figures already computed in Go and must not get the loop’s tools: edge_recon_narrative (a field-reader walk), and freight_market, counterparty_check, counterparty_reviews and customer_analysis (the market and due-diligence passes). Each is guarded where it runs.
Templates are sent to the model verbatim. Nothing renders Jinja. Everything in a template file, including comments, is text the model reads. A template describes the role the model is asked to play. It is not a statement of the platform’s capabilities; for those, read the pages in this section.
data.agents-that-run-on-their-own#Agents that:
No one picks an agent and presses Run. The server runs the agents a change makes stale, for the tenant it happened in:
A rule’s enforcement posture is saved (RulesService.UpdateRulePolicy, from the policy drawer on Why): compliance and twins run. A scenario is simulated (SimulateScenario or InteractiveSimulate): twins runs, to turn the outcome into proposals. A burst of changes becomes one run per agent: each change inside a quiet window pushes the window out, at most one run per agent is in flight, and a change during a run queues exactly one follow-up. These runs are named auto:, and Options shows the ones in flight in one line (nothing at all when none is running). What they propose still waits for a person on Actionable Twins.
data.guardrails-openbias#Guardrails (OpenBias:
Before a prompt reaches the model, an OpenBias judge evaluates it against rule sets from the OpenBias rule sets that ship with the backend:
A global baseline is prepended to every judge. Each service adds its own rules (TwinsService, ComplianceService, HypothesisService, VisionService and others). The guardrails are wired and checked in three ways:
The agent lookup fails closed. Every agent id is mapped to its service’s guardrails. An agent with a template but no mapping is refused with FailedPrecondition, and the message describes a server configuration defect, not a user error. Other entry points are guarded too. GenerateSOP, GenerateRoadmap, TriageReturnItem and camera-feed grading (IngestSurveillanceFeed) each consult the matching judge. The documents are checked against the code. A parity test compares every rule in the rule documents with what the judges compile. Another test pins which judges are actually consulted. How the rules change. Rules are versioned, tested against the code before they land, and every refusal is audited.
data.human-in-the-loop-points#Human-in-the-lo:
A person makes these decisions. The server records who made each one, from the verified session:
Decision Where RPC What’s recorded Send an option for approval Options HypothesisService.SendToTwins The option, its figures as the server computed them, and the approval it needs. Sending decides nothing. Approve or reject an action card Actionable Twins TwinsService.ExecuteAction decision_trail. A reason is required on rejection. Approval seals the evidence document. A two-person card needs two different named people. Make an approved decision a standing rule Actionable Twins, on an approved card TwinsService.ProposeStandingRule / ApproveStandingRule Proposer and approver; the approver must be an org admin who is not the proposer. Address a remediation order Actionable Twins and its remediation views ComplianceService.AssignRemediation assigned_by and assigned_at_unix Standing routing rule The remediation views SetRemediationRoute set_by and set_at_unix Decide a remediation order Actionable Twins and its remediation views DecideRemediation decided_by and decided_at_unix Set a rule’s enforcement posture Why, the rule’s policy drawer RulesService.UpdateRulePolicy The operator-owned half only. It can’t change findings. Read actual customer rows API only; the FACE app does not call it ConfigService.SampleConnectionDataset A separate, bounded call. Exploring a source never samples it. See Data sources. Nothing FACE derives is sent, filed or settled without one of these decisions. Where an action does execute, for example an email draft through a connected account, its outcome is reported per artifact in not_executed. See Action cards & money.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: Guardrails make misuse harder; they don’t make it impossible. A prompt fence makes injection harder, and it does not solve it. Judging is a second opinion. A concurring verdict means the judge found the action supported by the evidence the run gathered. It doesn’t show the action is right. The tool gate authorises the tool, not the arguments. A caller permitted to use run_sql may still see the model choose a query they would not have written. Tenant scoping and the read-only shape check bound what that query can reach. Recording a human decision is not enforcing it. The recorded decision shows who approved what. It doesn’t show that they reviewed it carefully.
data.the-fast-path#The fast path:
In front of the model-based judge sits a pinned tree model from ml/decide, running through judgefast. It’s controlled by FACE_FAST_JUDGEMENT, which is on by default.
It answers only at the ladder’s final gate, and the deterministic gates run first. It never answers with no evidence. It leaves sensitive domains to the model-based judge. It abstains on anything it can’t answer, and that goes to the model exactly as before. Each model-based verdict records which model judged it in judged_by: either the fast model with its full sha256 digest, or llm.
data.the-judging-ladder#The judging ladder:
Every logistics action a loop’s final answer proposes is judged before it’s accepted. That covers the twins orchestrator’s decisions and action_cards, other agents’ recommendations, and the fetch’s Phase 3 twins decision. The judge is the shared Runink judging ladder (inference/judgement), which Runink TIDE also uses.
What counts as evidence. The evidence is what the run gathered: its context and its successful tool observations. The claim judged is the action alone, never the orchestrator’s rationale for it. Dissent removes the action. When the ladder dissents, the loop may be sent back to revise. An action still dissented from is removed. It survives only as accepted=false in FetchAnalysisResult.action_judgements or ExecuteLoopResponse.judgements. Unable-to-judge is never concurrence. An action that was not judged is kept as unable-to-judge, never as accepted. Verdicts can’t be forged by the model. Verdicts travel out of band in the shared runink.ui.judgement.v1 shape (Judgement on Decision and ActionCard). Any verdict key the model writes into its own output is stripped. Configuration. FACE_RALPH_JUDGEMENT controls judging, and FACE_RALPH_JUDGE_MAX_ACTIONS and FACE_RALPH_JUDGE_REVISIONS bound its cost.
data.the-ralph-orchestrator#The Ralph orchest:
RalphOrchestratorService.ExecuteLoop runs a ReAct loop (thought, then action, then observation) and streams each step back as an ExecuteLoopResponse:
agent_id picks the template, for example twins, hypothesis or rules_recon. The id is reduced to a base name before any filesystem use. max_iterations bounds the loop. The default is 5. LoopStatus reports progress: WORKING, EXECUTING, OBSERVING, DONE, FAILED or MAX_REACHED. Each turn is TOON: current_thought, has_action, action, action_input, is_final_answer, and on the final turn a nested final_result_json. On DONE, judgements carries the judging ladder’s verdicts. The same loop drives the scenario simulations behind Options and the interactive twin (StreamTwins).
data.tools#Tools:
The loop can dispatch three tools. Each passes a fail-closed authorisation gate (ralphToolGate) that checks the caller’s verified identity against the tool’s tier:
Tool Tier What it does read_file read Reads a file from a confined path. Output is truncated. run_sql write Runs a query through SqlService.ExecuteSelect, which refuses statements that fail its read-only shape check, against the connection the loop was started with. delegate_to_claims invoke Hands a sub-task to the claims agent. No subject, no tool. A call with no authenticated subject is denied, not skipped. When a tool has no working configuration for the run, the loop tells the model up front and treats the first failure as final.

data:
You open the Compliance, Finance and Operations views from the Remediation links on Actionable Twins. Each runs its own analysis and lists what it found, with a remediation order for each finding. You address an order to a department, set a standing route for a category, and record the decision. Orders still waiting for a decision are also listed in the Waiting for you lane on Actionable Twins. The business rules behind the findings, and the policy you set on each, are on Why.
Three services share one request and response shape:
Service RPC ComplianceService AnalyzeCompliance FinanceService AnalyzeFinance OperationsService AnalyzeOperations Each takes an AnalyzeComplianceRequest (system_context) and returns an AnalyzeComplianceResponse with these fields:
compliance_status: Pass, Warning, Fail, or Unable to Assess. violations (ComplianceViolation): the category, severity, description, related rule and remediation for each finding. audit_trail. spoken_response. orders: remediation orders (see below). live_data_note.
data.how-a-verdict-is-produced#How a verdict:
The compliance agent reads its system prompt from the compliance.jinja template. It then assembles the system state for the model, and the model answers in TOON. See Structured output.
Configuration values are labelled as declarations. Environment values such as ENFORCE_AUDIT_LOGGING, REQUIRE_HITL, DATABASE_ENGINE and PRIMARY_SERVER_URL go to the model marked OPERATOR DECLARATION, followed by a NOTE TO THE ASSESSOR: a declaration is what an operator asserted, not evidence that a control is implemented. Facts the code can establish for itself are marked OBSERVED. One example is that audit logging runs on every call and no code path disables it.
No usable answer means no verdict. With no model plane, or when generation times out or fails, the status is Unable to Assess with the reason, and the failure is audit-logged. It is never a pass, and never an invented finding.
live_data_note says which live data was read. A current server always sets it. The verdict rests on the session context sent with the request and on the instance’s own configuration, and the note tells the reader so.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A Pass is the model’s reading of the context it was given. Read live_data_note for what that context was. Operator declarations are claims about the environment, not controls the system has verified. An order with an assignment has not necessarily been sent. Only a recorded SENT dispatch says a person sent it.
data.remediation-orders-and-the-workflow#Reme:
A RemediationOrder is the dispatchable form of a finding. It’s shaped like an evidence document: a subject, facts read from records (specifications), coded determinations, citations, deadlines, ordered steps, and a seal written at approval.
An order may not contain any of the following:
A step whose parameters weren’t read from a record. A step that needs an unmeasured figure is not emitted. A department FACE inferred. FACE receives no org chart. An external service_provider, such as a carrier named on the cited record, may be derived. A deadline with no authority. A date appears only when a cited contract clause, SLA or statute supplies it. Order ids are stable (the rule id plus the subject), so an operator’s routing and decision survive the next analysis. The operator’s half of an order is stored apart from the derived half and merged when the order is read:
flowchart LR A[Derived orderNOT_ROUTED] --> B{Operator addressedthis order?} B -- AssignRemediation --> C[OPERATOR_ASSIGNED] B -- no --> D{Routing rule forthis category?} D -- SetRemediationRoute --> E[OPERATOR_ROUTING_RULE] D -- no --> F[stays NOT_ROUTED] C & E & F --> G[DecideRemediationDRAFT / APPROVED / REJECTED / SENT] AssignRemediation addresses one order to a department and contact. The server records assigned_by from the verified session, and ignores any author fields the client sends. SetRemediationRoute, ListRemediationRoutes and DeleteRemediationRoute manage a standing table. The table maps a finding category, matched exactly, to a department. An order routed by the table says so (OPERATOR_ROUTING_RULE), which is distinct from a person addressing that particular order. A person’s assignment always takes precedence over a rule. DecideRemediation records the human decision (RemediationDispatch). An empty state means nobody has decided yet, which is not the same as DRAFT. decided_by is the verified subject. FACE sends nothing by itself. SENT records something a human did outside the platform, and channel records how. RemediationAssignment.basis takes one of these values:
basis Meaning DERIVED_FROM_RECORD The provider was named on a cited record. OPERATOR_ASSIGNED A person addressed this order. OPERATOR_ROUTING_RULE A standing category rule addressed it. NOT_ROUTED The default. An unaddressed order is addressed to nobody, not to everybody. An empty orders list is a valid response. The overlay and routing apply to whatever orders the analysis produced.
data.rules#Rules:
RulesService serves the rules that the rules-reconciliation agent recognises in the data. You see them on Why, each with its policy drawer:
ListRules, AnalyzeCode and CheckCode read. UpdateRulePolicy sets only the operator-owned enforcement posture (RulePolicy), from the policy drawer. It can’t edit the agent’s findings (name, logic, proposed code or reconciliation_status). An operator who could overwrite a finding could make FACE agree with them. Saving a posture also re-runs the compliance and twins agents (see Agents & oversight).

data:
An evidence document (EvidenceDocument) is a document a third party acts on, such as an adjuster, a carrier’s claims desk or a court. FACE attaches one to an ActionCard in evidence_document. You read it on the card on Actionable Twins, and in full through the card’s View full decision artifact. It is sealed when a person approves the card. The contract is strict about what these documents are and are not:
These documents assemble a file, show what was read, and propose one next step for a person entitled to take it. They do not underwrite, bind, settle, or satisfy an obligation on anyone’s behalf.
data.citations#Citations:
A Citation has everything a reader needs to go and check a figure:
source_kind, source_id (the record’s id in the customer’s system), and the field read. value: the value exactly as read, never reformatted. This makes “no invented figures” something a test can check: every headline figure is either a cited value or documented arithmetic over cited values. connection_id, plus lineage_record_id pointing at the extraction record in the append-only lineage log. observed_at: taken from the lineage record, never from the wall clock, so re-deriving a document produces the same bytes. perception: set only when a model read the value off a scanned document image. It records an outcome (READ, NOT_PRESENT_ON_DOCUMENT, ILLEGIBLE or EXTRACTION_FAILED) and the model’s own confidence. That confidence is never used as a truth threshold. If perception is absent, the value came from a structured record.
data.determination-then-expression#Determinat:
Every field above narrative is determination. Derivers compute it as fixed, testable arithmetic over cited records, and no model is involved. narrative is expression. A model may draft it, but only after the determination is frozen, and only using figures that are already set.
Field What it holds kind One value from the closed EvidenceDocumentKind vocabulary (below). subject_id The customer’s own identifier for the shipment, claim or entry. It is also the key for the seal chain. facts (DocumentFact) What the records say. Every fact carries at least one citation id. findings (DocumentFinding) What was determined, as stable codes such as OSD_SHORT or SLA_BREACH_CONFIRMED, with a severity and the operands used. Never empty of citations. citations (Citation) Where each figure came from (see below). deadlines (DocumentDeadline) A date computed from a record date by a named rule (for example CARMACK_NOTICE_9M, COGSA_SUIT_1Y) with its authority, and the citation that supplied the start date. claimed_amount, exposure_amount, units_short, units_damaged Headline figures. These are optional, so a measured zero and “not measured” are different on the wire. absent (AbsentFigure) Why a figure is missing, from a closed set: NO_BACKING_RECORD, NOT_STATED_ON_DOCUMENT, ILLEGIBLE, EXTRACTION_FAILED, NOT_YET_DETERMINABLE, CURRENCY_NOT_STATED (a figure stated with no currency: not money, so not measured). narrative (DocumentNarrative) Optional prose. authored_by is deterministic-template or the model id, and figure_ids lists every figure the prose mentions. seal (DocumentSeal) Set at approval. Never set at derivation.
data.names-chosen-to-avoid-over-claiming#Name:
EQUIPMENT_LIMIT_APPROACH is deliberately not called “predictive maintenance”. The deriver measures a channel’s trend against a limit the feed itself states, and reports when a straight line through the first and last readings reaches that limit. Nothing is fitted and nothing is forecast, so no failure probability is ever produced.
CHAIN_OF_CUSTODY_AUDIT keeps one rule: an unrecorded handoff is not a break in custody. Every finding is a statement about the record, never about the goods or the people handling them.
The underwriting documents never decide coverage. No finding code says VOID, DECLINED, REPUDIATED or anything like it. Those are an underwriter’s words.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A document is a file, not a decision. It proposes one next step for a person entitled to take it. It doesn’t serve notice, file a claim or settle anything. A computed deadline is an input, not legal advice. It doesn’t preserve a right on anyone’s behalf. The document carries due_unix and no “days remaining” figure; the client computes the countdown at render time. A citation proves provenance, not correctness. It shows exactly which record a figure came from. It doesn’t show that the record was right. A seal proves the bytes haven’t changed since approval. It doesn’t prove who approved them. For that, see the decision trail on Action cards & money. Each deriver has its own tests for correctness. The coverage test checks that every emitted kind has a producer.
data.sealing#Sealing:
A seal (sha256-chain-v1) is written when an operator approves the card, never before:
content_hash covers the canonical bytes of fields 1 to 14. prev_hash chains the seal to the previous seal for the same subject_id. The seal record goes into the append-only lineage log. It carries hashes and ids only, never document content. signature and key_id are filled in only when a signing key is configured. A rejected card is deliberately left unsealed, because sealing a refused document would assert a state nobody adopted. If the seal can’t be written, the approval still stands, and the document is recorded as approved and unsealed.
data.the-vocabulary-17-document-kinds#The voc:
EvidenceDocumentKind is a closed vocabulary. Nothing on the model path can invent a new kind, and a build-time test checks that every kind FACE emits is constructed by its own deriver over cited records.
Kind Charges the headline? Paralegal and claims recovery STATEMENT_OF_POSITION No. States claimed_amount. OSD_REPORT Yes: the cargo value short or damaged. NOTICE_OF_INTENT_TO_CLAIM No. States exposure_amount. SUBROGATION_DEMAND No. States claimed_amount. Cargo insurance and underwriting FNOL Yes: the reserve, only for claims no claims card already charges. CARGO_LOSS_SURVEY No. States exposure_amount. WARRANTY_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT No. States exposure_amount. Shipper contracts and liability RATE_CON_ACCESSORIAL_AUDIT Yes: accessorials billed above the rate confirmation. MSA_SLA_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT Yes: service credits owed under an SLA clause. Field operations and cold chain TEMPERATURE_EXCURSION No. States exposure_amount only when the readings state load_value WITH a load_value_currency; otherwise it is absent as CURRENCY_NOT_STATED (“Not measured”). The cold-chain twin prices nothing. CHAIN_OF_CUSTODY_AUDIT No. Exposure is declared absent. CUSTOMS_MANIFEST_EXCEPTION No. The customs twin owns the delay’s cost. Reverse, reactive and equipment RETURN_DISPOSITION No. SERVICE_DISRUPTION No. EQUIPMENT_LIMIT_APPROACH No. An approaching limit is not a loss. Recovery leakage and indicator review CLAIMS_LEAKAGE No. States exposure_amount; the recovery card it points to owns the money. FRAUD_INDICATOR_REVIEW No. An indicator is not savings. States exposure_amount. The kind names above drop the EVIDENCE_DOCUMENT_KIND_ prefix. The charging rule is explained on Action cards & money.

data:
You ask a question on Ask, and FACE answers it from your own connected sources. That answer is one fetch: one run of FACE’s analysis. A fetch reads the data, profiles and clusters it, runs the analysis agents, and returns a FetchAnalysisResult with decisions, action cards and evidence documents. A brief on the Briefs page runs the same fetch on a clock or when new data arrives.
Where you see the result:
Ask shows the answer first, with its confidence chips. Each run is kept at /fetch/run/. Options shows what you could do about it, and Why shows the rules and sources behind it. Actionable Twins shows the action cards the run drafted, waiting for a person. All of this is served by FetchService.
RPC What it does RunFetch Runs a fetch and returns one RunFetchResponse. RunFetchStream Runs the same fetch and streams RunFetchUpdate events as each phase finishes. The last event carries the full result. ListTraces / GetTraceDetails Read back the recorded execution history. GenerateSOP Drafts a Standard Operating Procedure as markdown. ListFetchStarters Returns the suggested questions shown on Ask. Briefs are a separate service, SchedulesService, and are covered below.
data.briefs#Briefs:
A brief is a scheduled question, and you manage briefs on the Briefs page. Each brief is written for one persona and reads the sources picked for it. With none picked, it reads every connection the instance has when the run fires. Its runs open on Ask like any other run, and the cards they draft wait on Actionable Twins.
SchedulesService provides ListSchedules, CreateSchedule, UpdateSchedule, SetScheduleActive and DeleteSchedule. A brief fires on one of two triggers:
Time. A free-text frequency maps to an interval: hourly, every 6 hours, daily, weekly or monthly. Unrecognised text maps to hourly. Event. A connection’s data listener sees the events the trigger asks for. The brief fires when enough matching events are pending, the first has waited its debounce time, the cooldown since its last run has passed, and its previous run has finished. The run is marked TRIGGER_TYPE_EVENT. How briefs behave:
Execution is opt-in. A due brief runs a real fetch only when SCHEDULE_EXECUTE_FETCH=true on the server. Otherwise it is recorded as skipped, not as a success, and run_count does not increase. Briefs run as a service account. A scheduled fetch runs under a short-lived service-account session (ROLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT) minted for the scheduler. A picked source that is gone is named. At fire time a picked connection that no longer exists is dropped, and the run’s last-run line names it. When none is left, the run is refused with that reason. A brief can tell someone. Its notify setting (WhatsApp, call or email, and a condition) sends a notice once the run’s background phases end, to the numbers and mailbox on Settings › Integrations (Channels). The outcome is recorded in last_notify: sent, not needed, not sent (with the reason), or waiting. Outcomes are recorded as they happened. last_run_success reflects what the fetch actually returned. A fetch declined by the pipeline, for example for budget, is recorded as a failure. A brief whose previous run hasn’t finished skips that interval instead of stacking.
data.phases#Phases:
sequenceDiagram participant C as FACE app participant CP as FACE server participant R as Runner participant M as Model plane C->>CP: RunFetchStream(RunFetchRequest) CP->>CP: compute-unit budget check CP->>R: forward (records + sealed credentials) R-->>C: phase=data_health (done=false) R->>R: read sources, profile, cluster, EDA par Phase 1 R->>M: posture agent (TOON) and R->>M: rules reconciliation (TOON) end R-->>C: phase=data_health (done=true) R->>M: Phase 2 hypothesis swarm R-->>C: phase=scenarios R->>M: Phase 3 twins decision R->>R: judging ladder on proposed actions R-->>C: phase=recommendations R-->>C: phase=final + RunFetchResponse RunFetchUpdate.phase names the stage an event reports. The contract lists data_health, rules, scenarios, recommendations, final and model_text (the text a model call is producing, as it is produced), plus denied for a budget refusal. The server also sends progress labels such as sources and data_prep while a stage runs, so a client should not treat the list as closed. done=false means a stage is still running. The terminal event always has phase="final", done=true, and a result.
The runner’s pipeline (runContextEngineeringPipeline) has three phases:
Phase 1, data alignment. The posture agent and the rules-reconciliation agent run in parallel over the fetched context. Before they run, the pipeline clusters the samples (HDBSCAN through AnalysisService.ClusterRefinement) and runs a per-domain time-series EDA (runDomainTimeSeriesEDA, backed by ml/prophet). When two data domains are correlated with |r| at or above RunFetchRequest.synapse_threshold (default 0.5), the EDA records a measured CORRELATED_WITH edge between them. Phase 2, hypothesis swarm. A bounded-parallel swarm runs one agent per scenario the estate proposes. The swarm has a cap, and its census travels in FetchAnalysisResult. The scenarios appear on Options. See Simulation & twins. Phase 3, twins decision. The twins orchestrator turns the grounded findings and simulations into decisions and action cards. Each proposed action goes through the judging ladder before it’s accepted. The accepted cards appear on Actionable Twins. See Agents & oversight. A Phase-1-only fetch. When session_eda is set, the fetch runs Phase 1 only: data domains, maturity, rules and the knowledge graph. It never runs the hypothesis or twins agents. The FACE app does not set it; a question on Ask, a brief and an API call without it run the full pipeline.
Unary RunFetch returns early. When Phase 1 completes, RunFetch returns the core result, and Phases 2 and 3 keep running in the background. RunFetchStream waits until the recommendations are ready.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A completed fetch is not a complete fetch. Read source_notices and the swarm census before treating the result as covering every selected source and scenario. Progress events report pipeline stages, not answer quality. A final event with success=true means the pipeline finished. It doesn’t mean the model’s answer is correct. EvaluationMetrics is not a quality score while unmeasured_reason is set. A cached result is a replay of an earlier run. Its provenance.computed_at says when it was produced.
data.sop-generation#SOP generation:
GenerateSOP takes a topic, a process_name and optional steps. The prompt is screened before it reaches the model. A refused prompt returns InvalidArgument, and the refusal is audit-logged.
The response carries markdown in sop_content and an sop_id. If the model call fails after the prompt is accepted, the content is the literal SOP Generation Failed.
data.suggested-questions-on-ask#Suggested que:
ListFetchStarters returns up to four FetchStarter questions, each with an icon, a title, a subtitle and prompt_text. They come from the caller’s own data, newest findings first:
The newest fetch. The newest run in the caller’s history that succeeded, or the newest with an analysis: its broken measured rules, its flagged routes and its scenario verdicts. Run history is scoped as ListFetchRuns is. A quick sample of the sources. A bounded read of each active source, with no model and no fetch run, so a question can name a figure before any fetch has run. A question built this way carries sample_rows and sampled_at_unix_ms. The connections. What each source’s last Explore described: its tables, row counts and topics. Each question names its play (claims, disruptions, routes, fulfilment, cold_chain, maintenance, inventory or fleet), which Ask’s play chips filter on. The call reads no store: it answers with the set built in the background, says it is still being prepared (loading), or says why it could not be read.
data.traces#Traces:
ListTraces and GetTraceDetails read the session records that each fetch saves to the durable record store. A Trace from these RPCs carries the transaction id, the command, the analysis text and the drafted SQL. If the process has no session store, ListTraces answers FailedPrecondition instead of returning an empty list, because “never read” and “nothing recorded” are different answers.
Observed data lineage, meaning which source was read when and where the rows went, is a different record. It’s served by LineageService.GetSourceActivity. See Posture & maturity.
data.what-the-result-carries#What the result:
FetchAnalysisResult includes the following fields, among others:
decisions and action_cards: the structured twin output. See Action cards & money. graph_nodes and graph_edges: the knowledge graph for the fetched domains. hypothesis_scenarios, hypothesis_impacts, hypothesis_traces, hypothesis_forecasts and hypothesis_anomalies: the swarm’s union of answers. It is a union, not a consensus. Nothing votes on or reconciles the agents. hypothesis_scenarios_inferred, hypothesis_agents_dispatched and hypothesis_agents_succeeded: the swarm census. These counts are only meaningful when hypothesis_swarm_ran is true. source_notices: sentences about sources that could not be read, or about where a source’s SQL actually ran. An empty list does not mean every source was fine. action_judgements: the judging ladder’s verdict on every proposed action, whether accepted or rejected. A rejected action appears nowhere else. provenance: how the answer was produced, fresh or exact-cache, set by the server. metrics (EvaluationMetrics): these scores are not filled in by the fetch. The response sets unmeasured_reason to “no evaluation harness ran for this fetch — these scores are absent, not zero”. A client must not render the scores as percentages when that field is set. sql_generated: SQL text drafted by the model from the fetched schemas. It’s informational output, not a record of what was executed. Repeat fetches can be served from cache. A recent identical fetch (same connection_id and command) can be replayed from cache. The cache entry must be younger than FETCH_CACHE_TTL (default 10 minutes) and at least FETCH_CACHE_MIN_CONFIDENCE (default 0.7) confident. A cached answer is marked in provenance. A run whose analysis phases all failed is never cached.
data.where-a-fetch-runs#Where a fetch runs:
The FACE server (the control plane) never runs the pipeline itself. RunFetchStream forwards the request to a dedicated runner and relays that runner’s stream back. If no runner can be dialled, the stream ends with a terminal final event that says the fetch did not run: “dedicated runner unavailable — fetch does not run on the control plane”. It never falls back to running the fetch locally.
Before any runner time is spent, the server checks the caller’s compute-unit budget. An exhausted budget ends the stream with a single event whose phase is denied. A successful fetch is then charged against that budget. Budgets are managed through MeteringService (see Operations), and you see them on Settings › Subscription.
The server resolves the connection records the fetch needs and sends them with the request in dispatched_connections. Credentials travel separately: each bundle is sealed to the runner’s ephemeral key for that one dispatch (dispatched_credentials, with dispatch_id). A client can’t set any of these fields, because the server overwrites them on the forward. How the sealing works is covered in Security.

data: Grounding means giving an agent evidence from the tenant’s own corpus, so that it reasons over retrieved records rather than only its prompt. FACE’s grounding layer is ai.Store, and its retrieval is Direct Corpus Interaction (DCI): no embeddings and no vector index. Passages are stored as plain text, and a search reads those passages directly.
data.durability#Durability:
Every passage is written to the blob store before it becomes searchable. With an object store configured, the passages live there. Without one, they go in a local directory with owner-only permissions (directories 0700, files 0600).
At start-up, FACE rebuilds the searchable copy from the blob store. A file that exists only in the local copy is never found. The corpus holds document text, so it is treated as customer data at rest. Security describes how it is sealed at rest.
data.how-a-search-works#How a search works: Retrieval is lexical: a search matches the words of the query against the passages in the tenant’s own indexed corpus, scoped per tenant. Every result cites the passage it came from, with a score that says how much of the query the passage covers, from 0 to 1.
data.per-tenant-scoping#Per-tenant scoping:
Isolation is structural: each tenant has its own directory, and the tenant is fixed by the deployment the request reaches.
The corpus keeps one scope per tenant. IndexDocument writes to the calling tenant’s scope. The tenant comes from the authenticated context, never from document metadata. A tenant key in metadata is dropped, so a document can’t re-scope itself. A search reads only the scopes the caller is entitled to, and each search is confined by a sandbox. A tenant id that can’t be used as a directory name is hashed into its own scope name. It never falls back to another scope.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A grounded answer is not a correct answer. Retrieval supplies context; the model can still misread it. A hit is a word match, not a meaning match. A passage that says the same thing in other words is not found. Ask with the words the documents use. Grounding is only as good as what was indexed. An empty corpus grounds nothing, and that is reported as an absence, not as a finding.
data.retrieval-tiers#Retrieval tiers:
MemoryStore.Ground tries three tiers in order and returns the first that answers:
flowchart TD Q[Grounding requestname + fingerprint] --> M{Exact memo hit?} M -- yes --> R1[Cached response] M -- no --> K[Tenant corpus searchtenant scope] K -- hits --> R2[Top results] K -- no hits --> D{Operator corpusconfigured?} D -- yes --> G[Grep inside theoperator corpus root] D -- no --> N[Empty: nothing cited] Memo cache. An exact (name, fingerprint) hit returns the stored response. No model call is needed. Tenant corpus. The search above runs over what FACE has indexed: ingested documents (a files connection’s Index documents, on Settings › Integrations); memoized answers; fetch samples; hypothesis simulations; retained web research. Operator corpus. inference/dci greps the directory named by FACE_DCI_CORPUS_DIR. FACE reads that directory and never writes to it. If the variable is unset, this tier doesn’t search an empty directory: it doesn’t search at all, and nothing from it is cited as local evidence. Store.GroundEvidence is the direct evidence lookup. The domain graph uses it for relevant documents, and the catalogue item resolver uses it too. It keeps two answers apart:
(nil, nil): the corpus was searched and has nothing to say. ErrRetrievalUnavailable: the corpus could not be searched, because it is not open or the search itself failed. Callers treat those two differently. “Our data says nothing” and “retrieval is down” lead to opposite actions.

data:
On Why you see what your data estate looks like and how ready it is: each business area’s health, the domains and how they relate, and the readiness indicators. PostureService serves those figures and grounds the other agents.
RPC What it does GetHealthScore Serves the latest fetch’s posture snapshot. With no snapshot, it runs the deterministic posture analysis. BuildDomainGraph The fast half of a session fetch. It derives data domains and their relationships deterministically, with no LLM call. AnalyzeEstateCausal A do-calculus intervention over the connected estate (see below). ListIncidents Data-maturity assessments (DataMaturityAssessment). GetContext Semantic context items for an agent type.
data.estate-causal-analysis#Estate causal ana:
AnalyzeEstateCausal runs an intervention over columns of the connected estate. A node is ., carrying the source’s own aggregate over that column.
FACE separates structure from magnitude:
Structure. The estate may propose an edge only from a DECLARED_FOREIGN_KEY, and only where both columns have a measured value. No weaker evidence class proposes anything. Magnitude. The coefficient is always the caller’s (EstateCausalCoefficient), because nothing in a catalogue or a sample measures how much one column moves another. Values that aren’t finite are refused. How to read the response:
Read answered first. With no admitted edge, the RPC refuses and explains why in refusal. It never returns an effect of 0 with an OK status. weakest_basis is the weakest basis among the edges the effect travelled along: OPERATOR_ASSERTED: the caller named both endpoints. DECLARED_KEY_REPURPOSED: the endpoints came from a declared key, which is weaker because a referential constraint is being read as a causal one. basis_statement is written to be shown verbatim beside the number. node_refusals, edge_refusals, nodes_added and columns_refused give the denominators. A graph of four columns out of nine hundred measurable ones is not a causal graph of the estate.
data.health-score-and-grade#Health score and:
Each domain gets a DomainHealth. The structural gauges come from computeStructuralMaturity, which is deterministic Go over a domain’s structure, not a model. Each gauge is on a 0 to 1 scale, and Why displays it as a percentage.
Gauge How it’s computed quality_stability_pct Sampled completeness. A sparse sample stays neutral at 0.75. lineage_pct A base of 0.55, plus 0.35 if a join key is present, capped at 1. freshness_pct A base of 0.6, plus 0.28 if a temporal column is present. risk_pii_pct The share of columns detected as PII, times 2.5, capped at 0.9. policy_pct max(0.4, 0.85 − 0.4 × risk_pii) cost_efficiency_pct A base of 0.7, adjusted by row count. The health value is (quality + lineage + freshness + policy + cost) / 5 − 0.15 × risk_pii, and it maps to a letter grade:
Grade Health A ≥ 0.85 B ≥ 0.72 C ≥ 0.58 D ≥ 0.45 F below 0.45 The base values come from the instance’s risk-scoring configuration. issues lists the structural reasons, for example “no join key detected (lineage risk)”.
A failed scan returns an error, not a grade of F. With no connected data source, the local path answers FailedPrecondition: “connect a data source first”.
The empty_trip category is always empty. Nothing in the platform measures empty-trip or deadhead running, so the server clears it on every response. A client must show it as not measured, never as zero.
Measure wording records where it came from. OptimizationSOP.provenance (MeasureProvenance) is one of:
MEASURED: read from a source. DERIVED: computed in Go from measured data. MODEL_GENERATED: written by the posture agent. Only MODEL_GENERATED may be labelled as AI-generated.
data.lineage#Lineage:
lineage_pct is a schema property, not observed lineage. It reads the same whether a source has been pulled a thousand times or never, because it depends only on whether a join key exists.
Observed lineage is a separate record, written by the backend’s lineage recorder:
Where records come from. Every tabular connector is wrapped by one lineage decorator, so each extraction and each delivery is recorded. Camera ingests are recorded at their own seam. How they’re stored. Records are append-only Avro in the object store, partitioned by UTC day. What they contain. Structure only: column names, counts, durations, a literal-free query shape and a fingerprint, and a closed-set error class. Never result values, driver messages or credentials. A test with sentinel values enforces this. How to read them. LineageService.GetSourceActivity returns per-connection activity over a window: extractions, deliveries and rows. The outcome mix: ok, empty and failed. empty means the source connected and returned nothing, which is neither a failure nor a delivery. error_classes, destinations, and the last_columns names. durable and durable_reason, which say whether the records survive a restart. Without a durable sink, the process keeps only a small in-memory ring. Some reads aren’t in the log. A camera frame ingest is recorded with a row count of zero, because a camera sends frames, not rows. See Vision & CCTV.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A grade reflects structure, not how the data is used. A grade of A means the schema has keys, timestamps and few PII columns. It doesn’t mean the data is correct, current or governed. lineage_pct is not lineage. Use GetSourceActivity for what was actually read and delivered. A declared foreign key is a referential constraint, not a causal claim. An estate causal answer reflects the coefficients you supplied. It rests on those coefficients, over the columns that had measurements.
data.the-domain-graph#The domain graph:
In the FACE app, the estate is mapped by the fetch itself: its business-domains phase derives the domains and their relationships from the connections the fetch reads, and Why shows the result. A newly confirmed connection joins the map at the next fetch. There is no manual control to map it again.
BuildDomainGraph derives domains (structuralCommunities) and structural edges deterministically. It computes no correlations. Measured CORRELATED_WITH edges come from the fetch pipeline’s time-series EDA instead. See Fetch pipeline.
When connected sources are read, each edge’s relation names its evidence class. The classes are a closed set, listed from strongest to weakest:
DECLARED_FOREIGN_KEY: the source’s own constraint. CATALOGUE_CONTAINMENT INFERRED_FROM_DECLARED_KEY INFERRED_SHARED_VOCABULARY INFERRED_FROM_VALUE_OVERLAP GUESSED_COLUMN_OVERLAP: a guess, and named as one. Value sampling is on by default, because sampled values are real evidence about what a table is. metadata_only_connection_ids turns it off per connection. Sampled values reach only counts and shapes in the graph. They never appear in a log line, an error, a lineage record or a model prompt.
FACE still serves include_connected_sources for API clients and for AnalyzeEstateCausal. The FACE app calls GetHealthScore only; BuildDomainGraph, AnalyzeEstateCausal, ListIncidents and GetSourceActivity are API calls.

data:
After a run answers your question on Ask, two pages carry it forward:
Options answers “what could we do, and what is each option worth?”. It leads with the options for the decision behind the run’s checks, scored and sendable for approval. Below them is what FACE tested: the run’s scenarios as a list, with a Graph view, and a New Simulation action. The status counts, what went to the twins and the run step by step sit in the folded How FACE knows this. Actionable Twins holds the decision cards in three lanes (Waiting for you, In flight, Back), with a Map view on the same page that places each card where your own data says it is. This page covers the services behind both, and the claims and reverse-logistics service.
data.claims-and-reverse-logistics-claimsagent:
TriageReturnItem is a fixed rule over the condition grade the caller states:
condition_code Disposition PRISTINE / A RESTOCK DAMAGED / B REFURBISH DEFECTIVE / C RECYCLE EXPIRED / D LANDFILL A missing return_id or condition_code, an unknown grade, or a negative value is refused with InvalidArgument. An unknown grade is never a decision to destroy stock. estimated_recovery_yield_usd, refurbishment_cost_usd and routing_destination aren’t derived, because FACE holds no pricing, cost or facility data for returns. basis_note says so on every response. Reverse-logistics outcomes that rest on records are produced as RETURN_DISPOSITION evidence documents. See Evidence documents.
data.comparing-options#Comparing options: How the options are scored, recommended and sent for approval is covered in Action cards & money. In short: one measure for every option, a range for each, a recommendation only when the best range clears both the next option and the figure as measured, and nothing runs until a named person approves.
data.digital-twins-twinsservice#Digital twins:
RPC What it does Where you see it GetActionQueue / ExecuteAction The action queue and the human decision. See Action cards & money. Actionable Twins lanes, and each card’s place on the Map view GetValueLedger Money identified, approved, filed, recovered and expired for a period, each figure with its basis. Actionable Twins (above the lanes) and Ask’s money line ListDecisionLog The hash-chained decision log. Admins only. Settings › Account, Admin ProposeStandingRule, ApproveStandingRule, RevokeStandingRule, ListStandingRules Turn an approved decision into a decision-authority rule. Proposing needs a writer; approving needs an org admin who is not the proposer. Every step is chained onto the decision log first. A decided card on Actionable Twins ListAssetLocations Where each asset in FACE’s fetched data is: a position only where a source stated one, and every other asset listed with the reason it has none. Map view ListRunRoutes The routes and destinations one run inferred from the rows it read, each proposal with its judging state, and what is missing when no destination has a position. Map view ListLiveTraffic / AnalyseRoutesLive Public transit and road feeds found from the run’s towns and regions, read only while someone watches the map, and each route against the live events near it. Map view ListRunProviders Service providers one run looked for on the public web near the sites in trouble (disposal, alternate warehousing, fleet repair, cold storage), with the queries sent. Map view OptimizeRoute Computes a route through the session’s Google Routes connector and returns distance, duration and polyline. Map view, fleet plan StreamTwins, QuickAsk, UploadAnalyze Interactive twin reasoning over text, audio, frames or a document; retrieval-based Q&A for S&OP and inventory questions; root-cause or savings analysis of an uploaded CSV, Excel or PDF file. The query is screened before it reaches a model. The assistant, opened from its floating button on every page GetSavingsSummary Pipeline savings and approved savings. The FACE app does not display it. API only GenerateRoadmap A phased roadmap (Digitize, Connect, Analyze, Automate) from maturity scores. The FACE app does not call it. API only SubmitFeedback Records feedback on a generated response to the durable record store. From Actionable Twins you also open:
Follow-ups, which run on the cards selected on the list or the map. The Compliance, Finance and Operations remediation views, from the page’s Remediation links. See Compliance, finance, operations. The site plans and the twin entities, as panels over the Map view. Refusals are errors, not empty cards.
OptimizeRoute returns Unavailable when there’s no routing connector or no route, rather than a card with blank measurements. cost_savings is left empty, because the routing provider returns no cost. GenerateRoadmap leaves estimated_investment_usd and expected_roi_percent at zero, which means “not estimated”: the roadmap describes a plan, not a measurement.
data.options#Options and scenarios (\u003ccod: RPC What it does Where you see it CompareOptions Scores the what-if options for one decision on one shared measure over a run’s measured rows, each with a 95% range, and names a recommended one only when it is the clear winner. Reads what the run stored; never re-reads a source. Options, at the top SendToTwins With decision_key, option_key and run_id: compares the options again and queues the named one for approval. Without them: turns a validated scenario into an action card. The card waits on Actionable Twins GetHypothesisVariables Scenario groups inferred from the estate, with each scenario’s simulation_state and the run-level swarm_census. Options InteractiveSimulate / SimulateScenario Runs one scenario through the agentic ReAct loop and returns SimulateScenarioResponse. The app uses InteractiveSimulate. Options ValidateHypothesis Checks a scenario against the recognised rules and data. Options GetTwinsHandoff / SetTwinsHandoffExclusion The scenarios a run’s analysis handed to the twins agent, with each verdict and impact, and whether a person removed one from the next twins analyses. Options, How FACE knows this GetScenarioBuilder, SaveCustomScenario, AddScenarioItem, AddScenarioTerm One run’s scenarios with their business categories, the items each tests and the market terms each watches, plus what your team added. Options, New Simulation AnalyzeTelemetry Agentic analysis of an equipment time series. The FACE app does not call it. API only The scenario list and its Graph view read FetchService.GetScenarioGraph: the run’s scenarios and what each one tested, computed from the run’s stored records only, with no model call. Anything the run did not record is shown as a gap, never as an invented node.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A simulation is a model’s reasoning over grounded context. It isn’t a measured outcome, and its confidence is the model’s own. The swarm results cover only the scenarios that ran. Read the census before treating the results as covering the estate. Passing validation means the rules are consistent. It doesn’t mean the scenario will happen. A compared option is scored over the rows the run read. A recommendation means its range cleared the others on that sample, not that it will work. A triage disposition follows the stated grade, not an inspection. It’s only as good as the grade the caller supplied.
data.scenarios-and-the-swarm#Scenarios and th:
Scenarios are generated from the estate’s domains, synapses and rules. HypothesisScenario.origin records which one proposed each scenario: node, synapse or rule. In a full fetch, Phase 2 runs a bounded-parallel swarm with one agent per scenario. The cap is derived from the time budget rather than chosen:
Inside a fetch, the plan comes from the time left for the phase. Up to three agents run at once. Each agent gets as many reasoning turns as fit, the number of waves is the time left divided by one agent’s turns, and the cap is waves times agents at once. The roster is ranked first, so when not every scenario fits, the ones that run are a measured cross-domain correlation first, then an open rule, then a domain node. Outside a fetch (the swarm a session starts), the limits are fixed: three agents at once, 6 minutes per agent, a 25-minute budget, so at most 12 agents. A scenario the cap left out is marked, not hidden. HypothesisScenarioState takes one of these values:
State Meaning SIMULATED Dispatched, and the agent produced a result. FAILED Dispatched, but the agent produced no result. Causes include a guardrail block, a TOON parse failure, the per-agent ceiling, or the budget running out. CAPPED Inferred, but never dispatched because of the cap. NOT_IN_RUN Newer than the recorded run. UNSPECIFIED No result recorded. This is neither a success nor a failure. HypothesisSwarmCensus records scenarios_inferred, agents_dispatched, agents_succeeded, capped, agent_cap, the source of the roster, and computed_at. Options shows the counts as “N scenarios tested, M succeeded”.
A simulation returns:
Decision scenarios. Impacts (metric, change percentage, risk level and horizon). Evidence traces (source_node → relation → target_node). Forecasts with intervals. Anomalies. The swarm’s aggregate is a union of independent answers, not a consensus: nothing votes, no agent is scored against another, and two agents that disagree are not reconciled.
data.validation#Validation:
ValidateHypothesis is a deterministic check, not a model call:
valid_data is true when a fetch has grounded the instance, meaning a rules or posture snapshot exists. valid_logic also requires that none of the scenario’s rules is in drift, shadow, missing, conflict or violated. Each such rule becomes a risk_flags entry. rationale explains the verdict.

data: All of FACE’s inference, including text reasoning, vision and voice, runs on models served inside the FACE deployment’s own cluster: Runink’s shared machines on Lite, your own cloud or servers on Dedicated and Enterprise. FACE calls no outside AI service on any plan. It also ships no inference binary: it is an HTTP client of the platform’s shared model plane.
data.images-are-typed#Images are typed: A picture travels in ImagePart (raw bytes, a mime_type, and a text_offset into the prompt), never as base64 inside prompt text. The receiver base64-encodes it once, when it builds the data: URL the plane expects. Because an image has its own field, a string in untrusted text can’t be misread as an image. ChatMessage.images carries images per turn in multi-turn conversations.
data.modelservice#ModelService:
ModelService is FACE’s gRPC door to the plane. Every agent, deriver and extractor that needs a model goes through it.
RPC Purpose Generate Text or multimodal generation. Embedding Deprecated. Answers Unimplemented: FACE does not compute embeddings. SynthesizeSpeech Text to WAV audio through the in-cluster text-to-speech service. voice defaults to tara. SpeakFetchSummary The spoken executive summary of the latest fetch, composed deterministically on the server.
data.no-embeddings#No embeddings: FACE does not call an embedding model. Retrieval is Direct Corpus Interaction: passages are stored as plain text and searched by their words. See Grounding. The model plane serves FACE generation, vision and voice only.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A configured URL is not a reachable plane. The startup refusal checks that someone wrote the variable down. It dials nothing. A reachable plane is not a loaded model. The plane can answer on its port while weights are still loading. Being sovereign doesn’t make a model accurate. This page describes where inference runs, not how good its answers are. The structural checks that bound model output are on Structured output and Agents & oversight.
data.task-routing#Task routing:
GenerateRequest.task_type says which kind of model a call needs:
TaskType Model id FACE sends Routed to TASK_TYPE_GENERAL / TASK_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED default The general reasoning tier TASK_TYPE_CODE coder The code tier TASK_TYPE_VISION vision The vision tier The platform’s model router chooses the tier from that id. GenerateRequest.model is deprecated and the server ignores it.
data.the-model-plane-contract#The model plane:
FACE talks to the plane through the OpenAI-compatible HTTP API:
Purpose Endpoint FACE calls Base URL Text and vision generation POST /v1/chat/completions INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL is the only variable FACE reads for the plane. The vision and voice tiers (VISION_REMOTE_URL, VOICE_REMOTE_URL) default to it. INFERENCE_API_KEY is sent as a bearer token when set. FACE never generates a service token. A plane that requires one and a FACE configured without one fails per call with the plane’s own authorisation error. Admission control is available. FACE_ADMIT_MAX bounds concurrent inference calls at the one door every call passes through. It’s off when unset or 0. Deploying and sizing the plane is the platform’s job. See Operations.
data.when-the-plane-is-not-configured#When th:
There is no local fallback tier, so a FACE with no plane has no inference at all. FACE refuses to run in that state, in two places:
At startup. If INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL is unset or blank, the server refuses to start. The error names the variable and explains that FACE has no local model server.
Per call. If a model call still reaches an empty base URL, ModelService returns gRPC FailedPrecondition with a message that names the variable. For example, from Generate:
text generation is unavailable: no inference endpoint configured (INFERENCE_REMOTE_URL is unset or blank). FACE has no local model server; this is a deployment fault in Runink TIDE’s manifests, not a transient error
FailedPrecondition was chosen because retrying can’t fix it. It’s a configuration state, and the FACE app can show the sentence verbatim.

data: FACE’s classical analysis comes from the Runink ml library. It’s pure Go, involves no neural network or external model server, and is standard-library only except for ml/linear and ml/segment. FACE exposes this analysis through AnalysisService, and the fetch pipeline uses the same code internally.
data.analyzecausal#\u003ccode\u003eAnalyzeCau:
A do-calculus intervention over a graph the caller states in full:
nodes maps each node to its observed value. edges (CausalEdge) carry a structural effect_size. An intervention sets intervention_node to intervention_value, and the change propagates along edges by multiplying through each effect size. The response returns effect on target_node and the target’s new_target_value. An edge naming an unknown node, or an edge set with a cycle, is refused with InvalidArgument. The call never runs over a partly built graph. An edge at 0 declares that there is no relationship. A missing edge means the relationship is unknown. To run an intervention over the connected estate instead of a hand-written graph, use PostureService.AnalyzeEstateCausal. See Posture & maturity.
data.analyzedescriptivestats#\u003ccode\u003e: Returns the mean, median, variance, standard deviation, skewness and kurtosis of data, computed by knowledge.DescriptiveStats.
data.analyzefeature#\u003ccode\u003eAnalyzeFe: Tests autocorrelation at lags 1 to 5 of target. Any lag with |ACF| > 0.5 is reported in significant_lags, and a target_lag_k feature is proposed for it. Fewer than 10 points returns Insufficient data, and a constant series returns Constant target.
data.analyzetimeseries#\u003ccode\u003eAnalyz:
Forecasts a series forecast_horizon steps ahead. The default horizon is 3.
Minimum input. Fewer than 5 points returns recommended_model="Insufficient Data (Need > 5 points)" and no forecast. Primary path: prophet.AnalyzeSeries. This is a full series EDA. It runs descriptive statistics, then an ADF stationarity test, then ACF/PACF autocorrelation, then a Prophet decomposition (piecewise-linear trend, Fourier seasonality and changepoints). Finally it fits ARIMA, and a rolling backtest picks between ARIMA and Prophet. The response carries: recommended_model: the chosen model, marked [backtest-selected], for example ARIMA(p,d,q) [backtest-selected]. stationarity_test: the ADF result, with the statistic and the 5% critical value. anomalies: the EDA’s findings, plus any Prophet residual anomalies. Fallback. If the EDA can’t fit a model, an ordinary-least-squares line is extrapolated. The response says Linear Regression (Fallback) and states that the EDA was unavailable.
data.classifyesgrelevance#\u003ccode\u003eCla: Returns relevance_score, a keyword-lexicon score from 0 to 1. Each text is scored by how often terms such as carbon, emission, net-zero and governance appear, weighted per term and capped at 1.0. It’s a relevance heuristic, not a trained classifier. The same texts are also passed to FACE’s digestion pipeline (clustering, EDA, forecast and causal passes). A failure there is logged and doesn’t change the score.
data.clusterrefinement#\u003ccode\u003eCluste:
Clusters items into domains by their feature vectors:
Validate the vectors. The first non-empty vector sets the dimension. Vectors that are missing or have a different dimension are kept in place as noise (-1) rather than dropped, so labels stay aligned with the caller’s items. Cluster with HDBSCAN. knowledge.SelectHDBSCAN runs with a minimum cluster size of 3 and Euclidean distance. It sweeps the minimum cluster size and keeps the candidate with the best silhouette coefficient. Candidates with fewer than two clusters, or with more than half the points in noise, are skipped. Rerank. A heuristic reranker in ml/xgboost applies per-domain feature weights, using BM25 relevance of each item against the request’s metadata as an extra feature. Despite the package name, this step doesn’t use a trained model. The response returns clusters (a label per item), noise (the indices labelled noise) and health_score. The health score is the silhouette, or the reranker’s cluster health when reranking succeeded.
data.inferbayesian#\u003ccode\u003eInferBayes: Posterior inference over a Bayesian network (ml/knowledge). The request carries evidence and a target node, but it has no field for defining variables or conditional probability tables. So on an instance with no defined network, the call answers FailedPrecondition and explains why, instead of returning an empty result with an OK status.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A forecast is a model’s extrapolation of the series you supplied. It knows nothing outside that series. The backtest picks the better of two models on the series’ own history, and that is not a guarantee about the future. A causal effect is the consequence of the graph you stated. The server computes it; it doesn’t discover it. Wrong edges give wrong effects, with no error. Correlation edges are not causal edges. Measured correlations between data domains in a fetch are recorded as CORRELATED_WITH and nothing more. A cluster is a statistical grouping. A high silhouette means the points separate well. It doesn’t mean the domain names attached to them are right. The ESG score counts words. It doesn’t assess performance against any ESG standard.
data.what-ml-provides-underneath#What \u003cc: Package Used by FACE for ml/knowledge HDBSCAN and silhouette selection, k-means, BM25, causal do-calculus, Bayesian networks, descriptive statistics, community detection and domain inference. ml/prophet Prophet decomposition, ARIMA, ADF, ACF/PACF and the unified series EDA. ml/xgboost Two separate things.
