The heuristic cluster reranker above, and a real gradient-boosted tree implementation with probability calibration, which ml/decide uses. ml/decide The pinned tree-model decision engine behind the judging ladder’s fast path. See Agents & oversight. ml/segment Region proposals for vision. It pools a frame into grid features, which are then clustered. It proposes where things are, never what they are. ml/linear Linear regression on a CPU-only backend. FACE wires the library’s audit hook. ml holds no state. Everything is computed and returned, and persistence is the calling app’s concern.

data: Every exchange between a model and the FACE backend is TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation), with one documented exception for vision detection. FACE uses no JSON-schema wrappers and no LLM orchestration framework.
data.from-reply-to-typed-struct#From reply to:
Replies are never unmarshalled straight into generated protobuf messages. The flow has three steps:
Declare an intermediate struct. Each call site defines a Go struct whose fields carry both json and toon tags. For example, the compliance agent parses into ToonComplianceAnalysis, with the fields compliance_status, violations, audit_trail and spoken_response. Parse. ai.NewToonOutputParser[T]() returns a parser, and Parse returns a value of type T, not a pointer. The parser uses the toon-go library. Map by hand. The call site maps the struct field by field onto the protobuf response. The model’s output never becomes a wire message without passing through code that names each field.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A successful parse proves shape, not truth. The repairs above keep formatting from discarding an answer. They say nothing about whether the answer is right. TOON limits what a model can express; it doesn’t constrain what it says. Boundaries on content are set elsewhere: the determination/expression split on Evidence documents, and the guardrails and judging ladder on Agents & oversight.
data.the-one-exception-vision-detection#The o:
One call departs from TOON: cctv.locateInstances, the class-conditioned object detection step of the vision pipeline. It asks the vision model for boxes in the model’s own fine-tuned bbox_2d JSON idiom.
The exception exists because of measurements recorded in the repository, not preference. On a photo of five separable pallet stacks:
The grading question, whether asked in TOON or JSON, with corner or width/height coordinates, returned one box covering 79–96% of the frame. That’s a scene-level classification with a rectangle around it. Two changes together produced per-instance boxes. The first was naming the class, in the singular (“detect each individual pallet stack”, not “every distinct object”). The second was asking in bbox_2d JSON. Class-conditioned TOON got part of the way, then degenerated into repeated rows with pinned coordinates. The scope of the exception is narrow:
It covers one detection primitive. The reply is matched by a regular expression and parsed into FACE’s own structs immediately. Every verdict still travels as TOON. Grading, material, damage grade and severity all come from the TOON grading call. It is off by default (VISION_DETECT_INSTANCES=true enables it) because it roughly doubles vision time per frame. The recorded measurement on a CPU inference tier was about 20 s for grading plus about 50 s for detection. See Vision & CCTV for the full pipeline and coordinate handling.
data.what-the-parser-refuses#What the parser: An empty completion is a failure, not an empty result. If nothing is left after stripping, which includes a reply that was only a reasoning block, the parser returns TOON_PARSE_FAILURE: empty model completion. A model that said nothing is never read as a model that found nothing. An explicitly empty array is a valid answer. rules[0]: or objects[0]{label,material}: means the model found nothing, and that is how a correctly empty frame or rule set is reported. Ambiguous nesting is refused. If sibling branches disagree about depth, the document is rejected rather than having a structure guessed for it. Each call site decides what a parse failure means for its own output. Where a failure would otherwise look like a clean result, it surfaces as an error or a stated absence. The compliance agent, for example, doesn’t report “no violations” when the model gave no usable answer.
data.what-the-parser-tolerates#What the parse: Small models make predictable formatting mistakes. Model output is parsed into typed records, and the parser repairs common formatting slips without changing any data. Anything that does not parse is not shown as a result.
data.why-toon#Why TOON:
TOON is an indentation-based object notation with compact tabular arrays. For record-shaped answers, such as a list of violations, findings or scenarios, the column names are declared once in a header rather than repeated per row. That takes fewer tokens to generate and gives the model less structure to get wrong. It matters on a sovereign, often CPU-bound model plane, where generation time is the dominant cost.
compliance_status: Warning violations[2]{category,severity,description,related_rule_id,remediation}: PII,HIGH,Email column in orders needs masking,R-12,Apply masking policy Retention,MEDIUM,No retention rule on audit table,R-31,Define a retention window spoken_response: Two compliance findings need attention.

data:
FACE models an operation as a twin graph: entities (a site, a dock, a reefer trailer, a sensor) and the relations between them, each fact stamped with where it came from, how it is known and when it was true. The vocabulary is GS1 EPCIS 2.0 + CBV 2.0: every class and relation maps to an EPCIS role, as the tables below show.
The ontology (classes, relations, validators, URI forms) is served by TwinOntologyService (GetTwinOntology, ValidateTwinIdentifier). The graph is Runink’s twin store (append-only, bitemporal) on FACE’s appfs tenant root, served by TwinGraphService (ListTwinEntities, GetTwinEntity, TraverseTwin, UpsertTwinEntity, LinkTwinEntities, ListTwinDevices). In the FACE app, the twin lives on Actionable Twins › Map. The Entities panel over the map is the entity browser (filter by class, search). The map plots located entities as points, and tapping one opens its detail. A device connection’s card on Ask opens the devices that connection reported into the twin.
data.classes#Classes:
Every identifier property is optional. An entity whose GLN or SSCC is not known has none; FACE never pads, derives or guesses one.
Class Key (scheme) EPCIS / CBV role Site GLN (AI 414) bizLocation / readPoint, urn:epc:id:sgln:….0 Facility GLN bizLocation Dock SGLN (GLN + AI 254 extension) readPoint / bizLocation (sub-location) Zone SGLN bizLocation (sub-location) YardSlot SGLN bizLocation (sub-location) Vehicle GIAI (AI 8004) epcList / parentID Trailer GIAI epcList / parentID Container ISO 6346 (BIC) epcList / parentID, urn:epc:id:bic:… LogisticUnit SSCC (AI 00) epcList / parentID Asset GIAI epcList ReturnableAsset GRAI (AI 8003) epcList / parentID (serialised GRAI only) Device GIAI sensorMetadata.deviceID Sensor GIAI sensorReport (type, uom, minValue/maxValue) Shipment GSIN (AI 402) bizTransactionList (desadv, bol) Order none (issuer’s number) bizTransactionList (po) Lot LGTIN (AI 01 + AI 10) quantityList, ilmd (cbvmda:lotNumber, expiry) Quantities carry UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 unit codes, as EPCIS does: CEL (°C), KGM, MTR, MTK, P1 (percent), SEC, DD (degree). The full property list per class, with required/optional and the EPCIS field each maps to, is what GetTwinOntology returns.
data.evidence-and-the-device-registry#Evidenc:
Every fact carries an evidence kind from a closed vocabulary, strongest first: OPERATOR_CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DECLARED, INFERRED, GUESSED. Edits made in the FACE app are OPERATOR_CONFIRMED with source operator:. A session that names no person is refused, and nothing is recorded as anonymous. Writes need the editor or admin role.
ListTwinDevices judges each Device and Sensor against its heartbeat_every_s:
Reporting: it was heard from within that interval. Device fault: it missed its heartbeat, or was never heard from after the first interval. Awaiting first report: it is new and its first heartbeat is not due yet. Not judged: no interval is stated, so its silence cannot be judged. None of these states is shown as “all fine”.
data.example-a-dc-with-a-reefer-at-the-door#E:
The keys below use GS1’s example company prefix 9521141 from the Tag Data Standard. They show the shape, not a real site.
Site "DC Nord" gln = urn:epc:id:sgln:9521141.12345.0 Dock door "7" sgln = urn:epc:id:sgln:9521141.12345.D7 isPartOf → Site YardSlot slot "Y12" sgln = urn:epc:id:sgln:9521141.12345.Y12 isPartOf → Site Trailer plate "AB-123-CD" giai = (absent: not known) locatedIn → YardSlot Y12 trailer_type = reefer assignedTo → Dock 7 Device reefer logger giai = urn:epc:id:giai:9521141.LOG42 assignedTo → Trailer heartbeat_every_s = 300 Sensor return-air probe measurement_type = gs1:Temperature isPartOf → Device uom = CEL, spec_min = 2, spec_max = 8 measures → Trailer LogisticUnit pallet sscc = urn:epc:id:sscc:9521141.1234567890 (carried by) Trailer The trailer’s GIAI is absent because nobody stated one. The graph still knows the trailer, by its plate and by its relations.
data.identifiers#Identifiers:
ValidateTwinIdentifier accepts a plain key, a GS1 element string ((414)…(254)…), an EPC URI or a GS1 Digital Link, checks it (GS1 mod-10 check digits; ISO 6346 mod-11) and returns its other forms. The FACE app’s identifier field calls it on every edit: the server is the only place a check digit is computed, and a server it cannot reach reads not checked, never valid.
The EPC URI needs the GS1 Company Prefix length, which a plain key does not carry. When the caller does not supply it, the EPC URI is reported absent with that reason, and the twin stores the Digital Link instead. It is never formed from an assumed split, because a wrong split is a well-formed URI naming another company’s object.
The validators are tested against the published examples of the GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard 2.1 (§7), for instance urn:epc:id:sscc:9521141.1234567890 ↔ (00)195211412345678900, and against the ISO 6346 code CSQU3054383.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: Operators build the graph, directly or by confirming site-plan elements. An empty twin is shown as empty. A GIAI is checked for form. GIAI has no check digit, so a well-formed GIAI can still be a mistyped one. Supply the GS1 Company Prefix length to form an EPC URI. A plain key does not carry it, and without it the EPC URI is reported absent with that reason.
data.relations#Relations:
Each relation is directed (from rel to), and the ontology lists which class pairs it allows. A write outside that domain/range is refused.
Relation Example EPCIS locatedIn Trailer → YardSlot ObjectEvent, bizLocation; bizStep arriving / receiving / storing, ended by departing isPartOf Dock → Facility, Sensor → Device master data (the SGLN hierarchy; sensorMetadata.deviceID) measures Sensor → Trailer ObjectEvent with sensorElementList; bizStep sensor_reporting carries Vehicle → Trailer → Container AggregationEvent, parentID = carrier; loading / unloading assignedTo Trailer → Dock, Device → Trailer none: a plan, not an observation; maps to bizTransaction or master data fulfils Shipment → Order shared bizTransaction (po + desadv/bol) on the shipping event containedIn LogisticUnit → LogisticUnit, Lot → LogisticUnit AggregationEvent (childEPCs or childQuantityList); packing / unpacking Lots are produced by EPCIS TransformationEvents.
data.site-plans-in-the-twin#Site plans in the:
A factory or warehouse plan (IFC, DXF, PDF or a picture; IFC and DXF are BIM/CAD plan files) is shown on Actionable Twins › Map, in the Site plans panel over the map: the values inferred from the plan, with their twin bindings. The map draws its footprint for physical-storage awareness, and tapping the footprint opens the plan over the map. A plan becomes part of the twin only through an operator. When an editor or admin confirms a zone, a dock or a yard slot, FACE writes it to the twin graph:
a Zone, Dock or YardSlot per confirmed element, named after the element (its door number or slot label for a dock or a slot), with evidence OPERATOR_CONFIRMED, source siteplan:: (the element id carries the IFC GlobalId or the DXF handle) and the person who confirmed it in x_confirmed_by. Its level, outline (x_polygon, in plan units), position, width and area (x_area_m2: the area the file states, else computed from the outline when the plan’s unit is known) are kept as x_ properties; the plan’s Site and Facility, named after the plan and written once. Facility, zones and docks are isPartOf it; a yard slot is part of the Site. Elements read from a file but never confirmed, and everything the vision model proposed, are never written. Identifiers are not derived from a plan: an SGLN appears only when an operator enters it on the twin entity, and a later re-confirm keeps it. Confirming again or editing the element writes a new version of the same entity. Rejecting it, or changing it to a kind with no twin class, writes a tombstone, but only if it was bound before. A kind change between zone, dock and yard slot retires the old entity and writes the new one.
Both sides link to each other. The site plan on the map shows the selected element’s twin entity and opens its detail; the entity’s detail names the plan and element it came from and opens the plan on that element.
The plan’s live overlay places a reading on a zone when its location names the zone, and also when the reading’s sensor is a Device that is locatedIn a zone the plan bound, or a Sensor that isPartOf such a device. The reading says which rule placed it: zone id, zone name, or twin locatedIn (with via for a sensor). A sensor whose twin names two of the plan’s zones is not placed.

data:
FACE grades what a camera sees with the sovereign vision tier: whether a pallet, crate or container door is damaged, how badly, and what it’s made of. The camera surface is SurveillanceService, with two paths that deliberately answer different questions.
RPC Path Model? IngestSurveillanceFeed Graded. A pushed frame, or frames sampled from an RTSP/HTTP feed. Yes: the TOON grading turn, plus optional detection. DetectLiveFrame Live. One validated frame, local detector only. No. It can’t reach the vision model. GetEvidenceFrame Fetches the annotated frame an ingest retained. No. Camera connections are set up on Settings › Integrations, as described in Data sources. A camera connection’s card on Ask opens its live view, with the feed already chosen.
data.aggregating-sightings#Aggregating sighti:
MaterialAnalyticsService.AnalyzeMaterialQuality folds graded ingests into distributions by material, class and damage grade over a time window:
Every count is a count of sightings, meaning one object in one frame in one ingest. It is never a count of things. Ungraded is not pristine. Ungraded sightings are counted separately, and averages are optional and carry their denominators. A comparison needs a baseline window. A delta appears only when a baseline window is supplied. It is never invented. Check whether the corpus was read. corpus_scanned and corpus_durable say whether a corpus was actually read and whether it survives a restart.
data.coordinate-handling-and-its-limits#Coord: Coordinates are normalised. Every box on the wire is 0 to 1 of the frame’s width and height, so a client can draw it at any size. Frames are downscaled first. Before the model sees a frame, its long edge is reduced to VISION_MAX_EDGE (default 448 px). 0 disables downscaling. Detection boxes are scaled per axis. bbox_2d coordinates may be in the model’s native 0 to 1000 space or in pixels. The parser uses the frame’s real pixel size and scales each axis separately, so boxes on non-square frames aren’t skewed. Above 1000 px, pixels and model space can’t be told apart. Once a frame’s long edge reaches 1000 px, a coordinate like 900 could mean either. The parser resolves it correctly only because the default downscale keeps frames well below that. Raising VISION_MAX_EDGE past 1000 brings the ambiguity back, and a test makes that regime visible.
data.notes-that-explain-an-absence#Notes that:
Three response fields explain gaps. An empty object list is also what a correctly empty yard looks like, so these fields are how a reader tells the cases apart.
localisation_note: why findings arrived without boxes. The cause might be that detection is off (the note names the switch), or detection’s own reason if it ran. detection_note: what the local detector did. It is never empty. If no detector is wired into the deployment, the note says so, as a fact about the deployment and never about the camera. evidence_note: why no annotated frame was retained. Retention is off unless an operator sets a window.
data.reading-the-results#Reading the results: A grade and a damage percentage are the vision model’s estimate from downscaled pixels. They aren’t a physical inspection. A box drawn where the coordinates say may not be on the right object. detection_note reports which stage ran, not whether it was correct. A retained evidence frame shows the reviewer what was assessed. It isn’t a forensic artefact.
data.the-graded-path#The graded path: flowchart TD F[Frame or sampled feed frames] --> V[Validate + downscalelong edge ≤ VISION_MAX_EDGE] V --> R[Region proposalsml/segment + HDBSCAN] R --> G[Grading turn — TOONsubject, material, damage grade, %] G --> Q{VISION_DETECT_INSTANCES=trueand a subject found?} Q -- no --> O[Response + localisation_note] Q -- yes --> D[Class-conditioned detectionbbox_2d JSON, one turn per frame] D --> O Frame grading. The vision model is asked, in TOON, for the inspectable subject: the object, its material, a damage_grade (PRISTINE, DAMAGED, DEFECTIVE or DESTROYED) and a model-estimated damage_percentage. A person is not a subject. If the frame holds no inspectable object, subject_object is empty, and every grade field is a no-finding, not a low score. People never appear in objects. Per-object results. objects (DetectedObject) lists every inspectable object with its own box. Labels are checked against a closed class vocabulary, named in class_vocabulary (for example runink.coldchain.v1). label_in_vocabulary is optional: when it’s absent, the classifier wasn’t asked. Class-conditioned detection. This step is off by default. With VISION_DETECT_INSTANCES=true, a second, class-conditioned turn asks the model for one box per instance of the graded class, using the model’s bbox_2d JSON idiom. This is the one sanctioned exception to TOON; see Structured output. The detection turn sweeps up to VISION_SWEEP_FRAMES frames, with one model turn per frame. frames_detected reports how many it looked at. The recorded cost on a CPU inference tier is about 50 s per detection turn, on top of about 20 s for grading. When a local detector has already boxed the graded objects one instance at a time, the sweep is skipped, and detection_note says so.
data.the-live-path#The live path:
DetectLiveFrame runs the injected local detector on one frame and returns. It never makes a model turn or a network hop. DetectLiveFrameResponse has no field for a grade, percentage, material or classification, so there’s nowhere to put a verdict. A test walks the call graph and fails if anything reachable from this RPC can reach the vision model, the catalogue resolver or a headless browser.
detection_latency_micros reports the in-process pipeline time per frame. It isn’t a round-trip time or a frame rate.
A live call is not stored as a result. It writes no evidence frame or sighting.
data.where-each-box-came-from#Where each box:
DetectedObject.box_origin (BoxOrigin) names the stage that produced each box:
BoxOrigin Source VISION_GRADING The grading turn’s own box columns. The weakest source, because grading answers at scene level. VISION_DETECTION The class-conditioned detection turn. REGION_CLUSTERING ml/segment region proposals: geometry only, with no label or grade. LOCAL_DETECTOR A detector running inside the FACE process. A box from a local detector carries detector_label, detector_label_set and an optional detector_confidence. A detector’s class is never written into label, and never mapped onto the cold-chain vocabulary. Material, grade and damage figures come only from the vision model’s grading turn.

data:
FACE is a gRPC API first. The FACE app uses the same public services described here, so any action in the app can also be done by an integration. This section is the reference for that API: how to connect and authenticate, the conventions every service follows, and one page per domain listing each RPC with its messages, fields and errors.
The reference comes from the .proto definitions and the server implementation. Where the two disagree, the page describes what the server does.
data.at-a-glance#At a glance: Protobuf package semantics.v1 API version 1.0.0 (see Versioning) Transports Native gRPC over HTTP/2 with TLS; gRPC-web for browsers Authentication authorization: Bearer metadata on every call except two Services The protos define 41 services with 225 RPCs. These pages document 30 services and 114 RPCs in full. The rest are listed by name in Not yet documented here, and the internal ones in Internal services.
data.authentication#Authentication:
Every RPC requires a session token in the authorization metadata, except these two:
RPC Why it is open semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login It is how a session is obtained. semantics.v1.ActivationService/ValidateLicense It checks a licence before anyone can sign in. Nothing else is exempt, including the landing dashboard. Server reflection is not bearer-token authenticated, but it answers only verified mutual-TLS mesh peers. Any other caller gets UNAUTHENTICATED (server reflection requires a verified mTLS peer). It is not an anonymous surface.
Getting a token. Call IdentityService/Login with one of these methods:
Email and password, followed by a TOTP code if the account has two-factor enabled. An OIDC ID token from the identity provider configured for your deployment. The email in the token must be verified and must be on the deployment’s allowlist. A successful login returns a signed session token that is valid for 12 hours. Send it on every call:
authorization: Bearer Sessions are checked against the server’s session store on every request. A token that was revoked by Logout, or by an admin changing the account, stops working within seconds on every replica.
Machine clients. An org admin can mint a service-account token with GenerateServiceAccountKey. It is valid for 365 days and scoped to the admin’s tenant. Store it as a secret.
Tenant scope. The tenant comes from the verified session, never from a request field. A request field that names a tenant is accepted only when it matches the session’s tenant.
data.basis#Basis: Value Meaning BASIS_UNSPECIFIED Not stated. BASIS_DETERMINISTIC Gates and arithmetic only. No model was consulted. BASIS_MODEL A sovereign model answered the qualitative question.
data.connecting#Connecting:
Connect to your FACE instance through the platform edge, over TLS. The edge address is the host name your instance is published at. This reference uses the placeholder face.example.internal:443. Both transports reach the same services on that address:
Native gRPC (HTTP/2 + TLS). Use this for server-to-server integrations, runners and command-line tools. It is the only transport for client-streaming and bidirectional RPCs. gRPC-web. Use this for browser clients. The FACE app is a gRPC-web client served from the same origin as the API, and it sends the same bearer token as any other client. gRPC-web carries unary and server-streaming RPCs only. The FACE app also sends an x-agent-trace-id metadata header on every call. The value is a random id minted once per app session. ActivityService uses it to scope a subscription to the runs that session started (see Lineage & activity). Other clients may send their own id or omit the header.
Do not build a client on server reflection. It is restricted to platform-internal callers. Build your client from the published .proto files instead (see Getting the protos).
data.domains#Domains: Identity, licences & landingLogin, sessions, TOTP, service-account keys, licence validation, dashboard. Configuration, connections & runnersData-source connections, runners, integrations, runner enrolment. Fetch & tracesRun the fetch pipeline, stream progress, read traces and SOPs. Twins, simulation & claimsDigital twins, action queue, hypotheses, claims triage. Analysis, posture & rulesStatistical analysis, estate posture, rule reconciliation. Compliance, finance & operationsDomain analyses and remediation routing. SQLRead-only SQL against configured engines. Lineage & activityWhat each source delivered; live agent activity. CCTV, surveillance & documentsCamera sources, evidence frames, OCR, material analytics. Calling & supportCall signalling and the support log. Agent orchestratorThe streamed agent loop and its tool gate. Metering & schedulesCompute usage and budgets; briefs (recurring fetch schedules). Crawler, metasearch & CRMSovereign crawl and search, bias rules, HubSpot.
data.getting-the-protos#Getting the protos:
The .proto files are provided with the platform. The module is semantics/v1/*.proto under a buf module root. It imports:
google/protobuf/timestamp.proto (well-known types), and runink/ui/judgement/v1/judgement.proto, the platform’s shared judgement types, which ship with the FACE protos. Generate clients with buf generate or protoc for your language. All messages use proto3.
data.internal-services#Internal services:
semantics.v1.ModelService (Generate, GenerateStream, SynthesizeSpeech, SpeakFetchSummary, and the deprecated Embedding, which answers Unimplemented) is FACE’s internal interface to its own sovereign model plane. It accepts calls only from the FACE process itself (loopback plus a verified mesh mTLS identity) and refuses every other caller with UNAUTHENTICATED, whatever token is presented. It is not part of the integration surface and is not documented here. Model-backed features are reached through the domain services that use them.
The one exception is ModelService/GetModelStatus. The FACE app calls it with an ordinary session to learn whether the inference plane answers. Any role may call it, and it carries no user data.
FetchService/GetDispatchKey is also internal: only a runner serves it, and only to a verified mesh peer.
The same endpoint also serves the platform’s shared components that FACE mounts: estate domains, data sources, billing, profile and member administration. Those services are defined outside the semantics.v1 package and are not covered by this reference.
data.judgement#Judgement:
runink.ui.judgement.v1.Judgement is the platform’s verdict on one claim, usually an action an agent proposed. It appears in fetch results, action cards and the orchestrator stream.
Field Type Description verdict Verdict The verdict. reason_code string Stable reason code, for example evidence-contradicts-the-claim. sentence string The sentence a person can act on. It may be partly model-written: render it as text, never as markup. basis Basis Whether a model was involved. subject string What was judged, as a person reads it: the action or card title. claim string The claim judged about the subject. accepted bool false means the verdict was a dissent and the action was removed from the answer. judged_at google.protobuf.Timestamp When the judgement ran. Unset means not recorded. It never means “now”. ref string Where the action sat in the answer, for example decisions[0]. evidence_items int32 How many evidence items were weighed. 0 with an evidence reason code is a real zero. Otherwise 0 may mean “not reported”. round int32 0 for the first answer. 1 and higher for answers the agent loop revised. verdict_text string The verdict spelled out verbatim. Show it when verdict is VERDICT_UNSPECIFIED.
data.judgementset#JudgementSet:
Every verdict from one run, accepted and rejected, with the server’s counts.
Field Type Description judgements repeated Judgement The verdicts. This may be one page of a longer list. concurs int32 Concurring verdicts. dissents int32 Dissenting verdicts. unable int32 Unable-to-judge verdicts. Use the counts as sent. Do not recompute them from judgements.
data.not-yet-documented-here#Not yet document:
These public RPCs are defined in the protos and served, but this reference does not yet document their messages. Read their request and response messages in the .proto files.
Service RPCs ActivationService ActivateLicense, GenerateLicense AdminService ArchiveRunDerivedMetadata AnalysisService EstimateCausalEffect ConfigService ConfirmConnectionProposal, ConnectSmtpMailbox, DisconnectMailbox, DismissConnectionProposal, GetMailbox, ImportContacts, ListConnectionProposals, ListContactImportSources, PreviewContactImport, SetConnectionActive, SetRunnerActive, StartMailboxConnect DocumentIngestService GetDocumentSource, IngestFromConnection, ListDocumentSources, ReadDocumentTable FetchService ApplyDataListener, ArchiveFetchRuns, GetOperationsBoard, ListDataListeners, QueueDeductionDispute, RestoreFetchRuns, Talk FollowupsService CancelFollowupRun, CompleteFollowupTask, DecideFollowupProposal, DeleteFollowup, DeleteFollowupChatEntry, DryRunFollowup, GetFollowupAddressee, ListFollowupChat, ListFollowupProposals, ListFollowupRuns, ListFollowups, ListFollowupSteps, ListFollowupTasks, ProposeFollowup, RunFollowupNow, SaveFollowup, SetFollowupArmed HypothesisService AddScenarioItem, AddScenarioTerm, CompareOptions, GetScenarioBuilder, GetTwinsHandoff, SaveCustomScenario, SetTwinsHandoffExclusion KnowledgeService DocumentCount, IngestConnection, Search LandingService GetSystemStatus LiveSensorService AcknowledgeFinding, GetIngestHealth, ListFindings, StreamReadings MapFeatureService ListMapLayers, StreamMapFeatures MarketDiligenceService AnalyzeCustomers, AnalyzeFreightMarket, CheckCounterparty, GetMarketDiligencePolicy, ListCounterpartyPublicReviews, QueueRecommendedAction, SetMarketDiligencePolicy MetasearchService GetExternalSearchPolicy, GetScenarioTrends, SetExternalSearchPolicy, SetTrendTopicIncluded OCRService ExportStructured, ExtractStructured, SaveStructuredCorrections PostureService GetDecisionInsight, GetOperationalCoverage SchedulesService DeletePersona, ListPersonas, SavePersona SensorTelemetryService GetReaderStatus, StreamSensorReadings TwinGraphService GetTwinMapOps, GetTwinSiteDetails. Its other seven RPCs, and both TwinOntologyService RPCs, are summarised with their access on Twins, simulation & claims, without their messages. TwinsService AnalyseRoutesLive, ApproveStandingRule, GetValueLedger, ListAssetLocations, ListDecisionLog, ListLiveTraffic, ListRunProviders, ListRunRoutes, ListStandingRules, ProposeStandingRule, RevokeStandingRule
data.roles#Roles:
Each session carries one role:
Role Summary ROLE_ORG_ADMIN Everything, including the admin-only RPCs below. ROLE_WRITER Every RPC except the admin-only ones. ROLE_READER Only the RPCs that change nothing and dial no customer source. A reader cannot run a fetch. ROLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT Machine credential. Allowed what a writer is allowed, except the management surfaces (below). One role table for the whole API. Every semantics.v1 RPC has a least role, checked before the handler runs. An RPC with no entry in that table is refused, so nothing ships ungated. A refusal is PERMISSION_DENIED with this action needs the editor or admin role on this instance or this action needs the admin role on this instance. Every RPC not listed below is open to any signed-in role.
Admin only (ROLE_ORG_ADMIN):
Service RPCs ActivationService ActivateLicense, GenerateLicense AdminService ArchiveRunDerivedMetadata ComplianceService DeleteRemediationRoute, SetRemediationRoute ConfigService ConfirmConnectionProposal, ConnectSmtpMailbox, CreateDatabricksCluster, CreateRunner, DisconnectMailbox, RunDatabricksJob, SetConnectionActive, SetIntegrationConfig, SetRunnerActive, StartMailboxConnect FetchService ArchiveFetchRuns, RestoreFetchRuns HubspotService Connect IdentityService CreateInstance, GenerateServiceAccountKey LiveSensorService GetIngestHealth MarketDiligenceService SetMarketDiligencePolicy MetasearchService EvaluateBias, ListBiasRules, SetExternalSearchPolicy PostureService GetContext, ListIncidents RulesService UpdateRulePolicy SupportService ClearSupportLog TwinsService ApproveStandingRule, GenerateRoadmap, ListDecisionLog, RevokeStandingRule Writer, admin or service account:
Service RPCs CallingService EndCall, Signal ClaimsAgentService TriageReturnItem ComplianceService AssignRemediation, DecideRemediation ConfigService CreateConnection, DeleteConnection, DismissConnectionProposal, ExploreConnection, ImportContacts, ListContactImportSources, PreviewContactImport, SampleConnectionDataset, TestConnection CrawlerService Crawl, Scrape DocumentIngestService IngestFromConnection FetchService QueueDeductionDispute, RunFetch, RunFetchStream, Talk FollowupsService CancelFollowupRun, CompleteFollowupTask, DecideFollowupProposal, DeleteFollowup, DeleteFollowupChatEntry, ProposeFollowup, RunFollowupNow, SaveFollowup, SetFollowupArmed FraudLeakageService ReviewClaimsLeakage, ReviewFraudIndicators HypothesisService AddScenarioItem, AddScenarioTerm, SaveCustomScenario, SendToTwins, SetTwinsHandoffExclusion KnowledgeService IngestConnection LiveSensorService AcknowledgeFinding MarketDiligenceService AnalyzeCustomers, AnalyzeFreightMarket, CheckCounterparty, QueueRecommendedAction MetasearchService SetTrendTopicIncluded MeteringService SetComputeBudget OCRService ExtractCode, ExtractExcelCode, ExtractStructured, ExtractText, SaveStructuredCorrections SchedulesService CreateSchedule, DeletePersona, DeleteSchedule, SavePersona, SetScheduleActive, UpdateSchedule SensorTelemetryService GetReaderStatus, StreamSensorReadings SqlService Execute, ExecuteBatch, ExecuteSelect SurveillanceService IngestSurveillanceFeed, TriggerSensorCueing TwinGraphService LinkTwinEntities, UpsertTwinEntity TwinsService ExecuteAction, ProposeStandingRule, UploadAnalyze Gated by the handler itself: IdentityService/UpdateUser (org admin only), RalphOrchestratorService/ExecuteLoop (each tool the loop calls is gated on its own), RunnerEnrollmentService/Enroll (service accounts only), and FetchService/GetDispatchKey, ApplyDataListener and ListDataListeners (verified mesh peers only).
Further checks apply across the whole API:
Service accounts, on unary calls, are refused on every ConfigService RPC except ListRunners and ListConnections, on all of ActivationService, on every IdentityService RPC, on member and role management, and on messages and calls to people. On streaming calls they are refused on all ConfigService, ActivationService and IdentityService streams and on member and role management. An unrecognised role grants nothing. The session is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED. Subscription tier. On the Lite tier, ConfigService/CreateDatabricksCluster is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED. Licence. When the deployment has a licence configured and it is expired or invalid, every authenticated call fails with PERMISSION_DENIED (license expired or invalid).
data.status-codes#Status codes:
FACE uses standard gRPC status codes. The grpc-message text is written for people, and the FACE app shows it verbatim for refusals. Clients may show it too, but should branch on the code.
Code When FACE returns it UNAUTHENTICATED No authorization metadata, or a token that is malformed, expired, revoked or not issued by this deployment. Sign in again. PERMISSION_DENIED The session is valid but not allowed: wrong role, service-account restriction, subscription tier, another tenant’s resource, or an expired licence. INVALID_ARGUMENT A required field is missing or a value is malformed. FAILED_PRECONDITION The request is well formed but the instance cannot serve it yet. Typical causes: no data source is connected, the sovereign model plane is not configured, or a required integration is not set up. Fix the configuration and retry. NOT_FOUND The named record, trace, connection or schedule does not exist for this tenant. DEADLINE_EXCEEDED A runner accepted dispatched work but did not answer in time. The run may still be in progress on the runner, so this does not mean it failed. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED The caller exceeded the per-user rate limit (on by default; see FACE_RATE_RPS), or a budget or size limit. Back off and retry. UNIMPLEMENTED The RPC is defined in the protos but this server does not serve it. This reference lists the RPCs the server serves. UNAVAILABLE A dependency, such as a runner or the model plane, is temporarily unreachable. Safe to retry with backoff. INTERNAL The server failed. Nothing is claimed to have happened. Many RPCs also report an expected refusal in the response body (success: false plus message) instead of an error. Each RPC’s section says which style it uses.
Unmeasured is not zero. Several responses use explicit presence (proto3 optional) or a stated reason to separate “nothing measured this” from a measured zero, for example confidence fields and usage figures. When a field is absent, report it as not measured. Do not display it as 0.
data.streaming#Streaming: Kind RPCs Transports Server streaming FetchService/RunFetchStream, TwinsService/StreamTwins, TwinsService/UploadAnalyze, HypothesisService/SimulateScenario, SurveillanceService/SubscribeTelemetry, ActivityService/SubscribeAgentActivity, RalphOrchestratorService/ExecuteLoop, LiveSensorService/StreamReadings, SensorTelemetryService/StreamSensorReadings, MapFeatureService/StreamMapFeatures Native gRPC and gRPC-web Bidirectional streaming HypothesisService/InteractiveSimulate, RunnerEnrollmentService/Enroll, FetchService/Talk Native gRPC only Streams are authenticated once, when they open, with the same bearer token and the same rules as unary calls. A long-lived stream therefore keeps running after its token expires. Re-open it with a fresh token when you reconnect. Set a deadline (grpc-timeout) on unary calls and reconnect server streams with backoff.
data.verdict#Verdict: Value Meaning VERDICT_UNSPECIFIED Not judged, or a verdict this enum does not know. Show verdict_text. VERDICT_CONCUR The evidence supports the claim. VERDICT_DISSENT The evidence contradicts the claim. reason_code names what. VERDICT_UNABLE_TO_JUDGE The evidence is absent, unreadable or does not bear on the claim. Never agreement. VERDICT_OUT_OF_SCOPE The platform has no standing over the subject. Counted in no total. FACE does not produce it.
data.versioning#Versioning:
The protos form one module with one version, currently 1.0.0. The build lints the module with buf and runs a breaking-change check against the previous release. A change that breaks the wire format or generated code is rejected unless it is explicitly listed as an exception, with the reason recorded. Additive changes (new fields, RPCs and enum values) arrive without notice. Clients should ignore unknown fields and treat unknown enum values as unspecified.
Where a field has been retired, its number and name are reserved, so they are never reused with another meaning. Deprecated RPCs keep working for at least one release and are marked on their pages.
data.worked-example#Worked example:
This example signs in with grpcurl, then makes an authenticated call. grpcurl reads the protos from disk rather than using reflection. Run it from the directory that holds the proto module root (semantics/) and the shared runink/ import tree.
1. Sign in2. Authenticated call3. Sign out grpcurl \ -import-path . \ -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \ -d '{"method": "AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS", "username": "analyst@example.com", "password": "'"$FACE_PASSWORD"'"}' \ face.example.internal:443 \ semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login A successful response:
{ "status": "STATUS_SUCCESS", "token": "eyJhbGciOi...", "message": "Authentication Successful" } If the account has two-factor enabled, the response is STATUS_MFA_REQUIRED with an mfaSession. Send it back within 5 minutes:
grpcurl -import-path . -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \ -d '{"method": "AUTH_METHOD_MFA_VERIFY", "mfaSession": "'"$MFA_SESSION"'", "mfaCode": "123456"}' \ face.example.internal:443 semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login TOKEN=$(grpcurl -import-path . -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \ -d '{"method": "AUTH_METHOD_CREDENTIALS", "username": "analyst@example.com", "password": "'"$FACE_PASSWORD"'"}' \ face.example.internal:443 semantics.v1.IdentityService/Login | jq -r .token) grpcurl \ -import-path . \ -proto semantics/v1/face.proto \ -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -d '{}' \ face.example.internal:443 \ semantics.v1.LandingService/GetDashboardStats Without the header, the same call fails:
ERROR: Code: Unauthenticated Message: authorization token is not provided grpcurl -import-path . -proto semantics/v1/commons_defs.proto \ -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{}' \ face.example.internal:443 semantics.v1.IdentityService/Logout This ends every session of the account, not only this one.
grpcurl prints and accepts JSON field names in lowerCamelCase (mfaSession), and it also accepts the proto names (mfa_session). Keep passwords and tokens out of your shell history. The example reads them from environment variables.

data:
Statistics, estate posture and business-rule reconciliation.
AnalysisService runs statistical methods on data you send: forecasting, lag features, clustering, causal intervention and descriptive statistics. PostureService serves the data-maturity picture that a fetch produced, maps the connected estate into a domain graph, and runs causal interventions over estate columns. RulesService serves the business rules the reconciliation agent derived and stores the operator’s enforcement policy for each.
data.analysisservice#AnalysisService:
Full name semantics.v1.AnalysisService.
These RPCs compute on the values in the request. They read no data source. Some errors are returned without a specific gRPC code, and clients see UNKNOWN for those.
data.analyzecausal#AnalyzeCausal: rpc AnalyzeCausal(AnalyzeCausalRequest) returns (AnalyzeCausalResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if an edge is refused: an endpoint missing from nodes, or an edge that would create a cycle. An intervention failure is returned without a specific code. Builds the graph exactly as you state it and sets intervention_node to intervention_value (the do-operator). The change propagates along edges by multiplying by each effect_size. With no edges, nothing propagates and the effect is 0. That means “no structure was given”, not “no effect was measured”. For a graph built from the connected estate, use AnalyzeEstateCausal.
data.analyzecode#AnalyzeCode: rpc AnalyzeCode(AnalyzeCodeRequest) returns (AnalyzeCodeResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: FAILED_PRECONDITION when no rules snapshot exists and source_code is empty. Model, template and parse failures are returned without a specific code. If a fetch has written a rules snapshot, returns those rules and ignores the request. Otherwise the reconciliation agent derives rules from source_code.
data.analyzedescriptivestats#AnalyzeDescripti: rpc AnalyzeDescriptiveStats(AnalyzeDescriptiveStatsRequest) returns (AnalyzeDescriptiveStatsResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: None. Empty data returns an empty response, with every field 0.
data.analyzeestatecausal#AnalyzeEstateCausal: rpc AnalyzeEstateCausal(AnalyzeEstateCausalRequest) returns (AnalyzeEstateCausalResponse); Kind: Unary. It builds the estate graph first, so it has the same cost as BuildDomainGraph. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: The same preconditions as BuildDomainGraph. INVALID_ARGUMENT if the coefficients cannot be wired, for example because an effect_size is not finite. Runs a do-intervention over estate causal nodes: columns of connected datasets that came back with a measured value. The structure comes from the coefficients you assert. The estate proposes candidate pairs but never supplies a coefficient. Without at least one admitted edge, the RPC refuses (answered: false) rather than returning an effect of 0. Read answered first, and show basis_statement beside any number.
data.analyzefeature#AnalyzeFeature: rpc AnalyzeFeature(AnalyzeFeatureRequest) returns (AnalyzeFeatureResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: None. Computes the autocorrelation of target at lags 1 to 5 and reports each lag with |ACF| > 0.5 as significant, with a target_lag_ feature for it. Fewer than 10 points returns generated_features: ["Insufficient data"], and a constant series returns ["Constant target"].
data.analyzetimeseries#AnalyzeTimeSeries: rpc AnalyzeTimeSeries(AnalyzeTimeSeriesRequest) returns (AnalyzeTimeSeriesResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: None. Too little data is reported in the response. Runs an exploratory time-series analysis over data. The server chooses a Prophet decomposition or an ARIMA model by backtest, applies an ADF stationarity test (differencing a non-stationary series before modelling), and forecasts forecast_horizon steps. If no model fits, it falls back to linear regression and says so in recommended_model and anomalies. With 5 or fewer points, the response has only recommended_model: "Insufficient Data (Need > 5 points)".
data.builddomaingraph#BuildDomainGraph:
rpc BuildDomainGraph(BuildDomainGraphRequest) returns (GetHealthScoreResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: FAILED_PRECONDITION when include_connected_sources is false (there are no instance data files to map), when no data sources are configured, or when the server has no metadata store. INTERNAL if the configured connections cannot be listed. With include_connected_sources: true, the server asks every configured connection for its catalogue (bounded at 30 seconds per source, concurrently), profiles columns, samples values except where excluded, and groups the discovered datasets into domains. A connection that refused, has no connector, or holds nothing still appears as a source node with its reason.
Sampled values are used only to infer structure. A sampled value never reaches the graph, a log line, an error, a lineage record or a model prompt: the graph carries counts and shapes, never a cell.
data.causaledge#CausalEdge: Field Type Description from string Cause node. to string Effect node. effect_size double Structural coefficient: a unit change in from moves to by this much. An edge at 0 is a declared non-relationship; a missing edge is an unknown one.
data.checkcode#CheckCode: rpc CheckCode(CheckCodeRequest) returns (CheckCodeResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: PERMISSION_DENIED if the snippet trips the rules agent’s guardrail. Asks the model plane to review the snippet. valid reports whether the model answered, not whether the code is valid. Read report.
data.classifyesgrelevance#ClassifyESGRelevanc: rpc ClassifyESGRelevance(ClassifyESGRelevanceRequest) returns (ClassifyESGRelevanceResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: Returned without a specific code if classification fails. Scores the texts together for ESG relevance with a keyword classifier. No model is involved. The texts are also passed to the deployment’s knowledge-ingestion pipeline when one is configured.
data.clusterrefinement#ClusterRefinement: rpc ClusterRefinement(ClusterRefinementRequest) returns (ClusterRefinementResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: Returned without a specific code (clients see UNKNOWN) when vectors is empty, no vector has any dimensions, or clustering fails. Clusters vectors with HDBSCAN (minimum cluster size 3, Euclidean distance), choosing parameters by silhouette. When the deployment has a re-ranking model, the clusters are refined with it, using BM25 scores of items against data_metadata (or telemetry_source) when items lines up with vectors. The dimension is taken from the first non-empty vector. Vectors of any other dimension are labelled noise (-1).
data.datamaturityassessment#DataMaturityAsses: Field Type Description incident string The finding. severity string Severity. impact string Impact. root_cause string Root cause. blast_radius string Blast radius. fix string Suggested fix. domain string The business domain it affects, matched against the fetch’s derived domains.
data.dataqualitypillar#DataQualityPillar: Field Type Description name string Pillar name. status string Pass, Warning or Fail. description string Description.
data.domainhealth#DomainHealth: Field Type Description status string Stable, At Risk or Critical. grade string Letter grade, for example A, B or C. quality_stability_pct double Quality stability percentage. risk_pii_pct double PII risk percentage. lineage_pct double Lineage coverage percentage. freshness_pct double Freshness percentage. policy_pct double Policy coverage percentage. cost_efficiency_pct double Cost efficiency percentage. issues string Issues, as text. uses_and_alignment repeated MaturityIndicator Maturity indicators. data_and_architecture repeated MaturityIndicator Maturity indicators. analysis_and_predictive repeated MaturityIndicator Maturity indicators. tools_and_automation repeated MaturityIndicator Maturity indicators. skills_and_fluency repeated MaturityIndicator Maturity indicators. spatial_logistics repeated MaturityIndicator Maturity indicators. empty_trip repeated MaturityIndicator Always empty, on purpose. Nothing in the platform measures empty-trip running, so the server clears this field on every response. Display it as not measured. shadow_search_ingestion repeated MaturityIndicator Maturity indicators.
data.embedding#Embedding: Field Type Description vector repeated float One embedding vector.
data.enforcementaction#EnforcementAction: Value Meaning ENFORCEMENT_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED Not set. ENFORCEMENT_ACTION_AUDIT_ONLY Observe and record. Nothing is blocked. ENFORCEMENT_ACTION_REVIEW_REQUIRED Flag the breach for a human before the action proceeds. ENFORCEMENT_ACTION_BLOCK Refuse the action outright.
data.estatecausalcoefficient#EstateCausalCoef: Field Type Description from string Estate causal node, ., in the source’s own spelling. It must have a measured value. to string Estate causal node. effect_size double Your assertion of the coefficient. Must be finite.
data.getcontext#GetContext: rpc GetContext(GetContextRequest) returns (GetContextResponse); Kind: Unary. It runs the posture agent. Auth: Bearer session, org admin only. Errors: None. If the posture analysis cannot run, it returns context_json: "{}" and no items.
data.gethealthscore#GetHealthScore: rpc GetHealthScore(GetHealthScoreRequest) returns (GetHealthScoreResponse); Kind: Unary. It can take minutes when no snapshot exists and the posture agent has to run. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: FAILED_PRECONDITION if the instance has no data sources. UNAVAILABLE if the posture analysis cannot run. The server reports these rather than returning a grade it did not compute. Returns the latest fetch’s posture snapshot, or runs the posture agent when there is none. Before it is returned, readiness figures are normalised, edges are cleaned, each assessment is assigned a domain, and each semantic context is grounded in the tenant’s knowledge corpus where one exists. graph_nodes and graph_edges are empty on this RPC.
data.inferbayesian#InferBayesian: rpc InferBayesian(InferBayesianRequest) returns (InferBayesianResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: FAILED_PRECONDITION on every call in the current release. No Bayesian network is defined on the instance, and the request cannot carry one.
data.knowledgegraphedge#KnowledgeGraphEdge: Field Type Description source string Source node id. target string Target node id. relation string The edge’s evidence, as KIND or KIND: detail. DECLARED_FOREIGN_KEY is the source’s own constraint. INFERRED_* kinds are FACE’s measurements. GUESSED_* kinds are guesses and say so. Display the three differently.
data.knowledgegraphnode#KnowledgeGraphNode: Field Type Description id string Node id. label string Display label. properties map Node properties. domain string Business domain. access_level string Access level. telemetry_source string Telemetry source. data_metadata string Metadata. business_unit string Business unit.
data.listincidents#ListIncidents: rpc ListIncidents(ListIncidentsRequest) returns (ListIncidentsResponse); Kind: Unary. It runs the posture agent. Auth: Bearer session, org admin only. Errors: None. If the posture analysis cannot run, the list is empty. An empty list therefore does not mean “no incidents”. Returns the posture agent’s data-maturity assessments. Entries that repeat the agent template’s example are dropped. domain is not set on this RPC.
data.listrules#ListRules: rpc ListRules(ListRulesRequest) returns (ListRulesResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: Returned without a specific code if the rules agent cannot run (for example, no model plane). Derives rules from the latest fetch session’s analysis, using a cached result when one exists, then merges in each rule’s stored policy. With no fetch session yet, it returns an empty list.
data.maturityindicator#MaturityIndicator: Field Type Description indicator_name string Indicator name. rating int32 1 to 5. metric string The metric. description string Description.
data.measureprovenance#MeasureProvenance: Value Meaning MEASURE_PROVENANCE_UNSPECIFIED Written before this field existed. Says nothing. MEASURE_PROVENANCE_MEASURED Read verbatim from a source the fetch pulled. MEASURE_PROVENANCE_DERIVED Computed deterministically from measured data. MEASURE_PROVENANCE_MODEL_GENERATED Written by a model.
data.optimizationsop#OptimizationSOP: Field Type Description type string Measure type. title string Title. action string The action. reason_impact string Why, and the expected impact. button_label string Suggested action label. provenance MeasureProvenance Where the wording came from. Only MEASURE_PROVENANCE_MODEL_GENERATED may be labelled AI-generated.
data.postureservice#PostureService:
Full name semantics.v1.PostureService.
Posture comes from a fetch. After a fetch, GetHealthScore serves that run’s snapshot. Without a snapshot, the posture agent runs on the model plane. For how a fetch is started, see Fetch & traces. Long posture runs are visible live through ActivityService.
data.request-analyzecausalrequest#Request: An: Field Type Description nodes map Node name to observed value. intervention_node string The node to set. intervention_value double The value to set it to. target_node string The node whose change to report. edges repeated CausalEdge The graph’s edges. Both endpoints must be in nodes, and the graph must stay acyclic.
data.request-analyzecoderequest#Request: Anal: Field Type Description source_path string Not used by the server. source_code string Code to derive rules from, used only when no snapshot exists.
data.request-analyzedescriptivestatsrequest#R: Field Type Description data repeated double The values.

An excluded connection contributes no causal node. intervention_node string Estate causal node to set: .. intervention_value double Value to set it to. target_node string Estate causal node whose change to report. coefficients repeated EstateCausalCoefficient Your structural coefficients. At least one must be admitted.

More than 5 points are needed. forecast_horizon int32 Steps to forecast. 0 or negative means 3. frequency string Series frequency label. Not used by the server. domain string Domain label. This field is still served, and without it the RPC refuses. metadata_only_connection_ids repeated string Connections to read as catalogue only, with no rows sampled. Sampling is on by default for every other connection.
data.request-checkcoderequest#Request: CheckC: Field Type Description source_code string The code. language string Its language.
data.request-classifyesgrelevancerequest#Requ: Field Type Description texts repeated string The texts to score, as one group.
data.request-clusterrefinementrequest#Request: Field Type Description items repeated string Text items, one per vector. Used for BM25 scoring when the counts match. granularity string PARAGRAPH or COLUMN. Not used by the server. vectors repeated Embedding Required. The vectors to cluster. domain string Context for re-ranking. access_level string Context for re-ranking. telemetry_source string Context for re-ranking, and the BM25 query when data_metadata is empty. data_metadata string Context for re-ranking, and the BM25 query. business_unit string Not used by the server.
data.request-getcontextrequest#Request: GetCo: Field Type Description agent_type string Not used by the server.
data.request-inferbayesianrequest#Request: In: Field Type Description evidence map Variable to observed state. target_node string The variable whose posterior to return.
data.request-listrulesrequest#Request: ListRu: Field Type Description domain_filter string Keep only rules whose category equals this, case-insensitively. Empty returns all.
data.request-updaterulepolicyrequest#Request:: Field Type Description rule_id string Required. An existing rule’s id. policy RulePolicy Required. Author fields are ignored.
data.response#Response: GetHealthScoreResponse with graph_nodes and graph_edges set.
data.response-analyzecausalresponse#Response:: Field Type Description effect double Predicted change in target_node. 0 when the target is not reached or not named. new_target_value double The target’s value after the intervention.
data.response-analyzecoderesponse#Response: A: Field Type Description found_rules repeated Rule The rules.
data.response-analyzedescriptivestatsresponse: Field Type Description mean double Mean. median double Median. variance double Variance. std_dev double Standard deviation. skewness double Skewness. kurtosis double Kurtosis.

Read this first. refusal string Why it declined, in full. effect and new_target_value are 0 and meaningless then. effect double Predicted change in the target. new_target_value double Target value after the intervention. weakest_basis string The weakest basis among the edges used: OPERATOR_ASSERTED or DECLARED_KEY_REPURPOSED. basis_statement string What that basis means. Show it verbatim beside the number. edges repeated string Every edge that entered the graph, basis first. candidate_pairs repeated string Every pair the estate proposed, priced or not. node_refusals repeated string Columns that were not made nodes, with reasons. Read nodes_added against it.
data.response-analyzefeatureresponse#Response: Field Type Description significant_lags repeated string For example Lag-2 (ACF: 0.63). generated_features repeated string Feature names such as target_lag_2, or a sentence when there are none.

data.response-gethealthscoreresponse#Response:
Also returned by BuildDomainGraph.
Field Type Description domains map
data.response-inferbayesianresponse#Response:: Field Type Description probabilities map State to posterior probability. Not returned in the current release.
data.response-listincidentsresponse#Response:: Field Type Description assessments repeated DataMaturityAssessment The assessments.
data.response-listrulesresponse#Response: Lis: Field Type Description rules repeated Rule The rules.
data.response-updaterulepolicyresponse#Respon: Field Type Description policy RulePolicy The stored policy, with the server-set author and time.
data.riskcompliancecheck#RiskComplianceCheck: Field Type Description check_name string Check name. status string Pass, Warning or Fail. details string Details.
data.rule#Rule: Field Type Description id string Rule id. name string Rule name. logic_plain_english string The rule in plain English. source_document string Document the rule was found in. category string For example Logistics or Finance. severity string Critical, High, Medium or Low. maturity string High, Medium or Low. inferred_objective string The rule’s inferred objective. related_documents repeated string Related documents. proposed_code string Proposed implementation. rule_type string Rule type. reconciliation_status string Code-versus-policy verdict: Aligned, Drift, Shadow or Missing.
