For LOCAL, only the base name is used. credentials string Write-only. For SFTP, JSON with user or username, password and host_key; a host key is required when the server has no known-hosts file. For GCP_BUCKET and GDRIVE, service-account JSON. format string PDF, DOCX, PPTX or AUTO. host string Host for NETWORK and SFTP, or bucket for GCP_BUCKET. port int32 Port for NETWORK and SFTP.

data.response-ingestsurveillancefeedresponse#: Field Type Description threat_detected bool Whether the grading found a threat. classification string For example NO_THREAT, INFRASTRUCTURE_DAMAGE or UNAUTHORIZED_DRONE. Empty when not assessed. threat_severity string SEVERE, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW. Empty when not assessed. suggested_remediation_action string Suggested action. Empty when not assessed. damage_grade string Worst object’s grade: PRISTINE, DAMAGED, DEFECTIVE or DESTROYED. Empty when not assessed. Empty is not PRISTINE. ocr_text string Readable text from the frames and the edge OCR payload. Never image data. frames_processed int32 Frames that reached the grading turn, which sees them together as one scene. damage_percentage int32 The vision model’s estimate for the worst object, 0 to 100. 0 when not assessed. subject_object string The inspectable object assessed, such as a pallet or container door. Empty means none: every grade field is then a no-finding. subject_material string What the subject is made of. damage_box_x float Worst object’s box, as a 0 to 1 fraction of frame width. All four box fields zero means no localisable region. damage_box_y float Box top, as a fraction of frame height. damage_box_w float Box width fraction. damage_box_h float Box height fraction. objects repeated DetectedObject Every inspectable object, each with its own box. People are never listed. localisation_note string Why there are no per-object boxes, when there are none. Empty when boxes are present or localisation did not apply. class_vocabulary string The closed class set that label_in_vocabulary was graded against, for example runink.coldchain.v1. Empty only when there are no objects. frames_detected int32 Frames that each got their own detection turn. DetectedObject.frame_index indexes these. It can differ from frames_processed. evidence_frame EvidenceFrameRef The retained annotated frame. Absent is the normal case, because retention is off unless the operator configures it. evidence_note string Why no frame was retained, when none was. detection_note string What the local detector did. Never empty. If no detector is set up in this deployment, the note says so; that is not a statement that the camera saw nothing.

Absent when the denominator is 0. damaged_share optional double Share of graded sightings that are not PRISTINE. Absent when none were graded. first_seen google.protobuf.Timestamp First sighting. last_seen google.protobuf.Timestamp Last sighting.
data.sightingtotals#SightingTotals: Field Type Description sighting_count int32 Sightings in the window. ingest_count int32 Distinct ingests. sensor_count int32 Distinct sensors. ingests_with_no_sightings int32 Ingests that were read and held no inspectable object. grades GradeCounts Grade distribution. vocabulary VocabularyCounts Vocabulary tally. damage_percent_stated_sightings int32 Denominator of mean_damage_percent. mean_damage_percent optional double Mean over stated sightings. Absent when none stated one. damaged_share optional double Share of graded sightings that are not PRISTINE, 0 to 1. Absent when none were graded. multi_frame_sweep_sightings int32 Sightings from multi-frame sweeps, where one object may be counted once per frame.
data.subscribetelemetry#SubscribeTelemetry: rpc SubscribeTelemetry(SubscribeTelemetryRequest) returns (stream SubscribeTelemetryResponse); Kind: Server streaming. Available over native gRPC and gRPC-web. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: None of its own. The stream stays open until the client cancels. Streams events as IngestSurveillanceFeed and TriggerSensorCueing produce them. There is no replay, so only events after subscribing arrive. A second subscription with the same subscriber_id replaces the first. Use a unique id per client session.
data.summary#Summary: Service RPC Kind Purpose SurveillanceService IngestSurveillanceFeed Unary Grade a frame or feed with the vision model SurveillanceService DetectLiveFrame Unary Local object detection on one frame, no model SurveillanceService GetEvidenceFrame Unary Fetch a retained annotated frame SurveillanceService TriggerSensorCueing Unary Broadcast a cross-sensor cue event SurveillanceService SubscribeTelemetry Server streaming Stream surveillance events MaterialAnalyticsService AnalyzeMaterialQuality Unary Aggregate sightings by material, class and sensor OCRService ExtractText Unary OCR text from documents and images OCRService ExtractExcelCode Unary Formulas, macros and VBA from a workbook OCRService ExtractCode Unary Structure of a source-code file Camera credentials sent to these RPCs (access_key_id, secret_access_key) are used for the call only. The password is never echoed in a response.
data.surveillanceservice#SurveillanceService:
Full name semantics.v1.SurveillanceService.
Two paths answer different questions at very different costs:
IngestSurveillanceFeed asks the sovereign vision model what is in the frame, what it is made of and how damaged it is. It can take minutes on CPU inference. It writes a lineage record and a sighting, may retain an evidence frame, and emits a telemetry event. DetectLiveFrame runs a local detector in the serving process and returns boxes in milliseconds. It grades nothing and writes nothing.
data.telemetryevent#TelemetryEvent: Field Type Description event_id string Event id. timestamp google.protobuf.Timestamp When it happened. event_type string DAMAGE_ASSESSMENT, DAMAGE_ASSESSMENT_NOT_PERFORMED or SENSOR_CUE. severity string SEVERE, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW. Empty for a frame that was not assessed. domain string LAND, AIR, MARITIME or CYBER, from the ingest. description string Human-readable summary. sensor_id string Originating sensor. damage_grade string Grade, when applicable. gps_coordinates string Location. metadata map For assessments: frames_processed, confidence_score, analysis_source. For cues: target_sensor_type, target_status, alert_payload. damage_percentage int32 Estimated damage, 0 to 100.
data.triggersensorcueing#TriggerSensorCueing: rpc TriggerSensorCueing(TriggerSensorCueingRequest) returns (TriggerSensorCueingResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session, writer, admin or service account. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if source_sensor_id or target_sensor_type is empty, or the target type is not one of INFRARED_CAMERA, YARD_CCTV or PLC_CRANE_LOCK. Broadcasts a SENSOR_CUE telemetry event with severity HIGH. No actuator is contacted: this service has no PTZ camera or PLC client. The status says a cue was requested.
data.vbamodule#VBAModule: Field Type Description name string Module name. code string Module code.
data.vocabularycounts#VocabularyCounts:
The three counts add up to the set’s sighting_count.
Field Type Description in_vocabulary_sightings int32 Label in the class vocabulary. out_of_vocabulary_sightings int32 Label graded and not in the vocabulary. not_asked_sightings int32 The classifier was not asked. Neither in nor out.
data.windowcomparison#WindowComparison: Field Type Description baseline_since google.protobuf.Timestamp Baseline window actually used. baseline_until google.protobuf.Timestamp Baseline window end. current_since google.protobuf.Timestamp Current window start. current_until google.protobuf.Timestamp Current window end. baseline_sighting_count int32 Sightings in the baseline. current_sighting_count int32 Sightings in the current window. material_deltas repeated GroupDelta One row per material present in either window. object_class_deltas repeated GroupDelta One row per class present in either window.

data: Web collection and CRM access. CrawlerService scrapes and crawls public web pages. MetasearchService runs the sovereign metasearch engine and carries the RPCs used to administer the prompt guardrail’s rules. HubspotService reads deals and contacts from HubSpot. All three run inside the FACE deployment: no third-party search or AI API is involved.
data.biasrule#BiasRule:
A guardrail rule, as used in rule administration.
Field Type Description rule_id string Rule id. description string The rule’s description. severity string The rule’s severity. category string The rule’s family. compliance repeated string Compliance standards the rule is cited under. is_domain_scope bool Rule administration field.
data.connect#Connect: rpc Connect(HubspotServiceConnectRequest) returns (HubspotServiceConnectResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session, org admin only. Errors: INTERNAL if the verification request cannot be built. Every other outcome is reported in success and message. Verifies api_key by making one read-only request to HubSpot. The key is not stored. For GetDeals and GetContacts to work, the operator must configure a HubSpot key on the deployment.
data.crawl#Crawl:
rpc Crawl(CrawlRequest) returns (CrawlResponse); Kind: Unary. The call returns when the crawl has finished. Auth: Bearer session, writer, admin or service account. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if url is empty or not an absolute http(s) URL with a host, or if depth or limit is negative. If the call’s deadline passes or the call is cancelled mid-crawl, the matching status is returned (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED or CANCELLED). Crawls breadth-first from the seed. Only http and https links are followed. The crawl stops when limit pages have been attempted. The result is kept under the returned crawl_id in the serving process’s memory, for GetCrawlStatus.
depth counts link hops from the seed: the seed is at depth 0, and links are followed from any page whose depth is below depth. For example, depth: 1 fetches the seed and the pages it links to.
data.crawledpage#CrawledPage: Field Type Description url string Page URL. title string Page title. Empty on error. content_snippet string The first 500 bytes of extracted content, followed by ... when truncated. status string Success or Error.
data.evaluatebias#EvaluateBias: rpc EvaluateBias(EvaluateBiasRequest) returns (EvaluateBiasResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session, org admin only. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if agent_name is not a known rule set (the message lists the known names), or if text is empty or only whitespace. An administrative RPC used when maintaining an agent’s guardrail rules.
data.getcontacts#GetContacts: rpc GetContacts(GetContactsRequest) returns (GetContactsResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: Same as GetDeals. Returns one page of contacts from HubSpot’s default page size.
data.getcrawlstatus#GetCrawlStatus: rpc GetCrawlStatus(GetCrawlStatusRequest) returns (GetCrawlStatusResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: None beyond authentication. An unknown crawl_id returns status: "Unknown" and no pages. Returns the pages recorded for a crawl. Crawl results are held in memory by the process that ran the crawl. They do not survive a restart and are not shared between replicas.
data.getdeals#GetDeals: rpc GetDeals(GetDealsRequest) returns (GetDealsResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: FAILED_PRECONDITION if no HubSpot key is configured on the deployment. A HubSpot transport, HTTP or decoding failure is returned without a specific status code (clients see UNKNOWN). Returns one page of deals from HubSpot’s default page size, with the properties below.
data.hubspotcontact#HubspotContact: Field Type Description id string HubSpot contact id. firstname string First name. lastname string Last name. email string Email address.
data.hubspotdeal#HubspotDeal: Field Type Description id string HubSpot deal id. dealname string Deal name. amount string Amount, as HubSpot returns it. pipeline string Pipeline id. dealstage string Deal stage id. closedate string Close date, as HubSpot returns it.
data.hubspotservice#HubspotService:
Full name semantics.v1.HubspotService.
HubSpot access uses a key that the operator configures on the deployment. A key sent to Connect is only verified: it is never stored or used for later calls.
data.listbiasrules#ListBiasRules: rpc ListBiasRules(ListBiasRulesRequest) returns (ListBiasRulesResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session, org admin only. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if agent_name is not a known rule set. An administrative RPC used when maintaining an agent’s guardrail rules.
data.metasearchservice#MetasearchService:
Full name semantics.v1.MetasearchService.
This service returns only numbers that the search engine or the guardrail computed. It reports no invented score, ratio or percentage.
data.request-crawlrequest#Request: CrawlReque: Field Type Description url string Required. Seed URL. It must be an absolute http(s) URL with a host. depth int32 Maximum link hops from the seed. 0 means the default, 2. Capped at 5. limit int32 Maximum pages to attempt. 0 means the default, 10. Capped at 500. allow_external bool Follow links to other hosts. When false (the default), the crawl stays on the seed’s host or its subdomains, on the same port. This is a host rule, not a registrable-domain rule: with seed www.example.com, a link to example.com counts as external.
data.request-evaluatebiasrequest#Request: Eva: Field Type Description text string Required. The text to evaluate. agent_name string The rule set to use. See Rule sets. An unknown name is refused.
data.request-getcontactsrequest#Request: GetC: Field Type Description limit int32 Not applied by the server.
data.request-getcrawlstatusrequest#Request: G: Field Type Description crawl_id string The id returned by Crawl.
data.request-getdealsrequest#Request: GetDeal: Field Type Description pipeline_id string Not applied by the server. Deals from all pipelines are returned. limit int32 Not applied by the server.
data.request-hubspotserviceconnectrequest#Req: Field Type Description api_key string HubSpot API key or private-app access token. Write-only: never returned, logged or stored.
data.request-listbiasrulesrequest#Request: Li: Field Type Description agent_name string Same names and refusal as EvaluateBiasRequest.agent_name.
data.request-scraperequest#Request: ScrapeReq: Field Type Description url string Required. The page to fetch. render_js bool Render the page in a headless browser before extracting. The server implements it.
data.request-searchtermsrequest#Request: Sear: Field Type Description query string Required. The search query. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed. max_results int32 Ranked results to return. 0 or negative means 5. Capped at 20.
data.response-crawlresponse#Response: CrawlRe: Field Type Description crawl_id string Id for GetCrawlStatus. status string Completed, or Failed when at least one page was attempted and none was fetched. The call is synchronous, so the server never returns Started. pages_visited int32 Pages fetched successfully.
data.response-evaluatebiasresponse#Response:: Field Type Description agent_name string The rule set used. rules_evaluated int32 Rule administration field. hits repeated BiasRule Rule administration field. blocked bool Rule administration field.
data.response-getcontactsresponse#Response: G: Field Type Description contacts repeated HubspotContact The contacts.
data.response-getcrawlstatusresponse#Response: Field Type Description status string Completed, Failed or Unknown. pages repeated CrawledPage Every page attempted, in visit order.
data.response-getdealsresponse#Response: GetD: Field Type Description deals repeated HubspotDeal The deals.
data.response-hubspotserviceconnectresponse#R: Field Type Description success bool true if HubSpot accepted the key. message string Outcome, including HubSpot’s HTTP status on rejection.
data.response-listbiasrulesresponse#Response:: Field Type Description agent_name string The rule set returned. rules repeated BiasRule The rule set.
data.response-scraperesponse#Response: Scrape: Field Type Description success bool Whether the page was fetched and extracted. url string The URL that was fetched. title string Page title. content string Main detected content, as Markdown or plain text. metadata map Not populated by the server. error_message string Why the scrape failed, when success is false.
data.response-searchtermsresponse#Response: S: Field Type Description query string The query as searched, echoed so responses can be matched to requests. results repeated SearchTermResult Ranked hits. There may be fewer than requested. requested_results int32 How many results the engine was asked for, after the default and cap were applied.
data.rule-sets#Rule sets:
agent_name accepts exactly these values. They name agents’ rule sets, not gRPC services, so most of them are not services in this reference. An empty agent_name means HypothesisService.
AnalysisService, ClaimsLeakageService, ClaimsService, ComplianceService, CopService, CounterpartyCheckService, CustomerAnalysisService, DocumentationService, FetchService, FinanceService, FraudDetectionService, FreightMarketService, FulfilmentService, HypothesisService, PostureService, PredictiveMaintenanceService, ReverseLogisticsService, RulesService, SelfHealingService, SurveillanceService, TelemetryService, TwinsService, UnderwritingService, VisionService, VoiceService.
data.scrape#Scrape: rpc Scrape(ScrapeRequest) returns (ScrapeResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session, writer, admin or service account. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if url is empty. A page that cannot be fetched, or no free browser slot for render_js, returns success: false with error_message instead of an error. Fetches one page and extracts its title and main content. With render_js: true, the page is rendered in the server’s headless browser first, which waits for a browser slot. Otherwise it is fetched as plain HTML.
data.searchtermresult#SearchTermResult: Field Type Description title string Page title. url string Page URL. content string Clean readable text extracted from the page, truncated by the engine. Not a summary: no model has processed it. score double The engine’s relevance score for this hit. Comparable within one response only. Do not display it as a confidence or a percentage. image_url string A representative image for the page, when the engine found one.
data.searchterms#SearchTerms: rpc SearchTerms(SearchTermsRequest) returns (SearchTermsResponse); Kind: Unary. Auth: Bearer session. Errors: INVALID_ARGUMENT if query is empty or only whitespace. UNAVAILABLE if the search fails. Runs a live search through the sovereign metasearch engine. The engine drives a headless browser, fetches and extracts candidate pages, then ranks them. This is an expensive call, not a typeahead: bind it to an explicit user action.
data.summary#Summary: Service RPC Kind Purpose CrawlerService Scrape Unary Fetch and extract one page CrawlerService Crawl Unary Crawl from a seed URL and record the pages CrawlerService GetCrawlStatus Unary Read a finished crawl’s pages MetasearchService SearchTerms Unary Ranked, content-extracted web search MetasearchService EvaluateBias Unary Guardrail rule administration MetasearchService ListBiasRules Unary Guardrail rule administration HubspotService Connect Unary Verify a HubSpot key HubspotService GetDeals Unary Read deals from HubSpot HubspotService GetContacts Unary Read contacts from HubSpot

data:
You ask FACE a question about your operation. It answers first, shows the options it tested and why it believes them, and drafts the decisions for a person to approve. Nothing goes to a third party until a person approves it.
This section has one page for each page in the app’s rail, in rail order. Text in bold is the exact wording on screen in the English interface.
data.start-here#Start here: Sign in and choose an instance NavigationThe rail, the run on every page, the activity card and the assistant
data.the-journey#The journey:
The rail follows the journey from a question to an approved decision:
Ask a question and get the answer, with the money it puts at stake. Briefs ask your questions for you, on a schedule, for each persona. Options shows what FACE tested for the run and which option wins, if one does. Why shows the checks, rules and counterparties behind the answer. Actionable Twins holds the drafted decisions: you approve, reject and follow them up, as a list or on the map. AskThe question, the answer, the money line and how FACE knows it BriefsWeekly briefs per persona, and your own scheduled questions OptionsWhat could we do: the options FACE compared and the scenarios it tested WhyWhat FACE checked, the rules, and the counterparties Actionable TwinsLanes, the Map view, site plans, entities and Follow-ups SettingsAccount, Personas, Integrations and Subscription

data: FACE works with a keyboard and a screen reader, never relies on colour alone, comes in light and dark themes, and speaks English, French, Spanish and Portuguese.
data.languages#Languages:
FACE is available in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. Under Settings › Account:
Interface language sets the language of the app’s screens. The interface switches at once. Agent language sets the language the agent listens and reads its answers aloud in, and the language FACE writes its answers in. Some text is not translated: technical identifiers, and text that comes word for word from a server or a source system. FACE marks where a server’s own reply is shown.
data.light-and-dark-themes#Light and dark the: FACE has separate light and dark themes, each designed for contrast in its own right. Choose under Settings › Account, next to Theme: Light, Dark or System, which follows your device. This device remembers your choice.
data.screen-readers-and-the-keyboard#Screen r: Navigation. Each rail entry is a real button. It takes keyboard focus, shows a visible focus ring, and responds to Enter and Space. Screen readers announce its label and whether it is the page you are on. Icon-only buttons. A button without a text label carries a tooltip and a spoken label. For example, the assistant button is announced as Open FACE AI assistant. Status changes. Errors and changing states are announced as they happen, such as the filter notice on Actionable Twins, a list that failed to load, the reject dialog’s character counter, the answer on Ask, and the hand-off to the twins on Options. The map. On the Map view, On the map lists every placed thing, so a keyboard can open the same card a tap does. Reduced motion. When your system asks for reduced motion, FACE stops decorative animation, such as the rotation of partner messages on the activity card.
data.severity-is-never-colour-alone#Severity:
Neighbouring severity colours are too close to tell apart by colour alone, so every severity mark also has its own shape, and usually its word:
Severity Glyph Critical filled circle with an exclamation mark High warning triangle Medium square Low dash OK check mark Other states work the same way:
Rule verdicts on Why pair a glyph with the words Aligned, Drift, Shadow, Missing and Unrated. How a scenario ended on Options is an icon and a word. Remediation banners and audit rows print their status word beside the glyph.

data:
Actionable Twins is where you decide. It lists every decision the twins drafted for the selected run, in three lanes: what waits for you, what is on its way, and what came back. You approve or reject each one, follow it up, and see the same decisions where they sit on the map. Open it with Actionable Twins, under Twins in the rail (/today_command).
FACE never acts alone. A decision stays waiting until a named person approves or rejects it, and FACE recommends an option only when it is a clear winner (see Options).
data.decision-artifacts#Decision artifacts: A decision artifact is the full record of one decision, with the drafts it would produce. Open the evidence on a card opens it, marked PENDING before approval. The page shows DECISION ARTIFACT #{id}, the title, the decision trail and the GENERATED DRAFTS. A link that carries no decision shows No decision artifact.
data.entities#Twin entities:
Twin entities is a side panel over the map (/twins/map?panel=entities): every entity FACE discovered from your sources (sites, docks, assets, devices), each with where it came from. Open it from Layers.
All classes filters by class, Search id or values searches, Load more reads the next page and New entity adds one by hand. Select an entity to open its page. An empty twin says so; Could not read the twin means the request failed.
data.filter-the-decisions#Filter the decision:
The play chips filter by play, in this order: Claims recovery, Disruptions, Routes, Fulfilment, then Cold chain, Maintenance, Inventory and Fleet. Once the twins have finished, each chip shows its count, for example {play} · {count}. Deadlines in the next 30 days keeps only decisions due in that window. All bands, Medium and up and High only filter fraud and leakage indicators by likelihood. While a filter is on, a notice titled Filtered to {filter} says so. Show all clears every filter.
The toolbar above the chips holds:
Scenarios for this run, which opens Options; Analyze document, which sends a csv, txt, tsv or json file of up to 3 MB to the twins and reads the list again when it is done; Draft next steps automatically, with Recovery leakage or Fraud indicators: an agent drafts steps for a person to approve (Drafted for a person to approve. Nothing has been filed, sent, paid or held.); Refresh. While a run is still working, Updating with the latest results… shows, and the list reads itself again until the run ends.
data.follow-ups#Follow-ups: A follow-up is a flow that chases the items on FACE’s boards (work orders, claims, deductions) by calling or messaging the people responsible, on rules you approve.
data.list-or-map#List or Map: The toggle at the top switches between List (/today_command) and Map (/twins/map), the same decisions on the map. On the list, Collapse all draws every card as one row and Expand all opens them all. Open card and Minimize card change one card.
data.map-view#Map view:
The Map view (/twins/map) draws the selected run’s sites, vehicles and routes where your data places them, with their decisions on them. FACE geocodes nothing: a thing is placed only where its source states a position.
The banner says what is on the map from your data: On the map from your data: {sites} places, {vehicles} vehicles, {routes} routes. It also says which run the map shows, and when vehicle positions come from earlier runs or are live positions rather than this run’s.
data.open-the-card-and-read-what-approving-do: WHAT APPROVING DOES says what this approval will and will not do. Read the drafts: the email, the calendar invite, the ERP change.
data.read-a-decision#Read a decision:
A card’s row shows its title and the money it states, for example {amount} at risk, {amount} revenue at risk or {amount} drafted order, or not measured: {reason}. Open the card to read:
the twin’s reason, its priority and the run that produced it; its items, as on an order: route stops, missing documents, recommended vendors. An amount is printed only when the card states one; Next:, the stage it waits on, for example Next: Approval — waiting for your decision; its pipeline, one step per stage, each done, now, stopped, not yet or not recorded; Open the evidence, which opens the decision artifact; Show on the map, on a decision about a vehicle, a route or an asset; Why, the figures behind it: what the twin stated, the cited records and the measured figures, or No measured figures were recorded for this action.
data.read-the-outcome#Read the outcome:
A decision that needs two approvers shows 1 of 2 approvals recorded after the first. When the server records an approval but part of it could not run, Recorded, but not executed lists each part with its reason.
When the claims play is selected and more than one claim is ready, Approve all {count} ready claims · {amount} asks first, then approves each claim one after another, through the same approval as a single one, under your name.
FACE has no way to edit a draft before it goes out. To change one, reject it with your reason.
data.record-what-happened-next#Record what ha: On a claim you approved, Record what happened next records its outcome: Filed, Awaiting reply, Recovered, Partially recovered or Denied. A recovery asks for Amount recovered (USD), recorded as you entered it. Nothing is billed on it. A denial asks why. The claim then moves to Back.
data.reject-a-decision#Reject a decision: Every rejection needs a reason: it is the only record of why.
data.remediation#Remediation:
Remediation: Compliance, Finance and Operations, above the lanes, open the remediation screen for that twin. Each shows the verdict, the server’s statement of which data it rests on, VIOLATIONS ({count}) or FINDINGS ({count}) with each item’s remediation and rule, and the AUDIT TRAIL. Unable to Assess is not a verdict: nothing could be assessed, and the summary says why.
Findings can become work orders. Remediation orders lists them; FACE sends no order anywhere: approving records a decision, and a person sends the order and marks it sent.
On the compliance screen, Routing table holds your own map from finding category to department. FACE holds no org chart and proposes no route. Enter a DEPARTMENT, a CONTACT or both, then Save rule. A rule applies to future orders only.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: TwinsService.GetActionQueue, ExecuteAction, ListDecisionLog, UploadAnalyze (server stream). MapFeatureService.ListMapLayers, StreamMapFeatures (server stream). TwinGraphService.GetTwinSiteDetails, for a site’s card. ComplianceService.AnalyzeCompliance, AssignRemediation, DecideRemediation. runink.ui.siteplan.v1.SitePlanService, for the site plans. See the API reference.
data.run-a-follow-up-on-selected-cards#Run a: Select cards on the list, or on the map (Select its card for follow-ups). The selection bar shows {count} selected, with Follow-up and Clear. Follow-up opens a sheet: Pick a follow-up. FACE first tries it on each item and sends nothing; you then choose to run it. After the dry run, Run on {count} items runs it.
data.select-a-place#Select a place:
Tap a site, a vehicle or a route, and its card opens beside it. With a keyboard, open On the map and choose an entry. Esc, the close button or a tap on the map closes the card. Show on the map on a list card opens the map on that card.
A site card tells its story first, for example how its demand moved in this run, then Outbound demand, Inventory safety nets, Cold chain, Policies, Verified shippers and Suppliers, each with its Basis. No model proposes a supplier or shipper here. Open the entity page opens the site’s own page. A vehicle card shows Predictive maintenance and Cold chain for this run, then its pending decisions with Approve and Reject. A route card shows its mode, its temperature band, the Re-plan (kilometres in the current order against the proposed order) and what triggered it. A figure the run does not contain says not measured, and why.
data.select-approve#Select Approve: Your decision is sent at once (Sending your decision…) and the card moves to In flight. If the server cannot be reached, Decision not delivered yet: {reason} · retrying shows, and the app keeps trying. Nothing is recorded until the server confirms.
data.select-reject#Select Reject: The dialog Why are you rejecting this? opens, naming the decision (Rejecting: {title}).
data.select-reject-with-this-reason#Select Re:
The decision’s later stages are marked stopped, and the rejection is kept in its decision record. Cancel leaves it where it was.
A fraud or leakage indicator is dismissed the same way: Why are you dismissing this indicator?, then Dismiss with this reason.
data.site-plans#Site plans:
Site plans opens a side panel over the map with the plans FACE inferred from your BIM/CAD files: each plan’s levels, its elements (zones, docks, yard slots) and the twin entity each element is bound to. Open it from a place’s card, from a plan’s footprint on the map, or from Layers.
Plans come from IFC or DXF files. DWG is a proprietary format and is not read: export DXF or IFC from your CAD tool. PDFs and pictures are read by the vision model, and what it finds is labelled proposed by the model until you confirm it. Select an element to see its twin (This element is the twin {entityClass} {id}.), or This element is not in the twin. Only a confirmed zone, dock or yard slot is written. Open in the twin opens the entity.
data.the-follow-ups-page#The Follow-ups page:
Follow-ups (/twins/followups) opens from the sheet. It is not a rail entry: it lights Actionable Twins. Calls and messages that chase your work orders, claims and deductions, on rules you approve.
With no follow-up yet, Start with a ready-made follow-up offers starters, for example When a claim’s window closes in 3 days, message the carrier. Use this opens one as a draft. Nothing runs until you arm it. Each follow-up is built from steps: When (what starts it), Reach people (a voice call, WhatsApp or SMS, or telling the addressee), Work orders (mark an order Draft or Sent; approving or rejecting stays a person’s decision) and Timing and checks (wait, or check before going on). A follow-up is Not armed until you arm it, and runs only as a dry run until then (Runs only as a dry run until you arm it.). Once Armed, it Runs by itself when its trigger fires. The assistant on the page drafts changes as pending steps; a person approves them. Tasks lists the open follow-up tasks with their due time. While no carrier is connected, the page says Calls and messages can’t go out until your carrier is connected., with Connect a carrier, and steps that need one show Needs a carrier.
data.the-lanes#The lanes:
Lane Holds Waiting for you Decisions that still need a person. In flight Decisions approved, with no final outcome recorded yet. Back Decisions with an outcome recorded: recovered, partly recovered or denied. Each lane heading shows how many items it holds and the money their cards state. Cards that state no amount are counted apart ({count} state no amount), never added as zero. An empty lane says why, for example Nothing waits for your decision on this run.
Inside a lane, decisions are grouped by category, with a count such as {count} actions · {waiting} waiting for you. Decisions whose documents state a deadline come first, soonest first. Decisions already decided are marked DECIDED.
data.the-pipeline-stages#The pipeline stages:
Every stage is drawn from what FACE records. A stage FACE keeps no record of says not recorded.
Decision Stages Claim or dispute Detected → Evidence gathered → Dispute drafted → Approval → Sent → Response → Resolved Sourcing or fulfilment Shortfall found → Order drafted → Approval → Placed → Confirmed Any other decision Approval, then what the approval carried out What FACE does not record today:
Placed and Confirmed: FACE places no ERP order. An approval records not placed: {reason}. A route approval records the new order. Nothing is sent to a vehicle or a TMS. Sent is done only when the decision log records that the message went out, and stopped with not sent: {reason} when it did not.
data.what-the-map-draws#What the map draws:
Placed assets: sites and vehicles at their stated position. Vehicles come from a connection tagged telemetry, equipment or shipments; the banner names them, or says No connection is tagged telemetry, equipment or shipments yet. Route proposals: The line joins this card’s stated positions in the proposed order. It is not a road. A route waiting for the route judge’s verdict cannot be approved yet. Reefers: minutes out of band: cold-chain pins, with value at risk only when the card states it. Money at stake, Cold-chain excursions and Detention & dwell: money layers, each with its total and what it could not place. Fleet plan (live): planned stops from the vehicles’ current GPS positions and pending shipments, not from the selected run. Live layers from each active connection that reports positions, and the providers FACE found near sites in trouble (Providers found), each with what the option costs against doing nothing. Layers lists every layer with a switch, how many features it has on the map ({count} on the map), the attribution its source requires, and how old its data is (Old data · newest {time}). Fit to sites frames every site, route and provider.
Not on the map lists what your data names but the map cannot place, each with its reason: No location in the data, or Address only — waiting for the FACE geocoder.
The basemap is FACE’s own, served by your FACE instance. No third-party map, tile or geocoding service is called.
data.when-the-list-is-empty#When the list is: You see Meaning The twins are working… The run is still working. The twins finished and proposed nothing The run’s data led to no decision that needs a person. Digital twin reasoning… The decisions are loading. Failed to fetch action queue: {error} The decisions could not be read. This is not an empty run.
data.write-your-reason#Write your reason: Type it in Your reason. An empty reason is refused, and so is one too long to keep word for word (Room for about {count} more characters.).

data:
Admin (/admin) manages who can use an instance and with which role, and the settings that govern FACE itself on that instance: its guard rules, whether anything may leave the instance, and the decision log.
Open Settings at the foot of the rail. The Account tab has an Admin card with the Admin entry, shown only when the server reports that you are an admin of the selected instance. The server checks your role again on every call, so the page cannot be used by someone without it.
Roles are Admin, Editor and Viewer.
data.decision-log#Decision log: Decision log lists every approval, rejection, refusal and outcome, hash-chained and written before anything runs. Each record names the card, who decided, the inputs it cited and the model and prompt template involved. Chain verified ✓ ({count} records) confirms the chain is intact; Chain broken at record {seq} names where it is not. No decisions recorded yet. means the log is empty; a failed read says the log is unknown, not empty.
data.enter-the-address#Enter the address: Under Invite someone, type the person’s Email address.
data.external-web-search#External web search: External web search is always on. Only a query a person types, or one of the confirmed public names an admin lists here (carriers, ports, competitors), is sent to public search engines; a query built from your data is made only from those names, and only when the text mentions them. Schema, table, column and row content never is. Each result says whether an external source was consulted, and which.
data.grounding-gate#Grounding gate:
GROUNDING GATE holds FACE’s own guard rules: the rules every agent call runs through, such as the OWASP and OpenBias rule sets. They govern the application, not your business, so they live here and not on Why. Your business rules are on Why.
Show the {count} rules lists the rule inventory with each rule’s CATEGORY, RULE and SEVERITY. Hide rules folds it away. Type a term or hypothesis and select Check this text. It is checked against the same rules that guard the agent call. Nothing is sent and nothing is logged. The result reads No rule fired or Would be refused, with how many rules were evaluated. Not checked yet means nothing was checked; The check couldn’t run means it failed. There is no “percent grounded”: a rule fires or it does not. Only an admin of the instance sees the gate, and every use is audited.
data.members-and-roles#Members and roles:
The list shows every person who holds a grant on the instance. You marks your own row. You cannot change your own access. A row marked Pending has been filed and applies when the platform reconciles.
Change role lets you pick a new role, then Save. Remove asks Remove {email} from this instance? They lose access on their next request. Confirm with Remove access. No person holds a grant on this instance means the list was read and is empty. Service accounts are counted but not listed.
data.pick-the-role#Pick the role: Choose Admin, Editor or Viewer under Role. The default is Viewer.
data.public-registries-and-market-data#Public:
Public registries & market data are always on. The market and due-diligence agents contact public registries and statistics with the identifiers a person types, and nothing from your records; each result names every source, its publisher, licence and retrieval time. An operator can turn live public data off for a whole deployment, for example an air-gapped one; each source then says it was not checked, and why. Thresholds for this organisation sets the limits those agents apply.
Every change to the public names or the thresholds is audited with its author.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: runink.ui.access.v1.AccessService: ListMembers, InviteMember, SetMemberRole, RemoveMember. MetasearchService.EvaluateBias, ListBiasRules, for the grounding gate. See the API reference.
data.select-invite#Select Invite:
Invited {email} as {role}. confirms the invitation. The person can then sign in and choose this instance.
If you have not chosen an instance yet, the page shows the instance picker first. Only an admin of this instance can manage its members. means your role on the selected instance is not Admin.

data:
Ask is where you put a question to your own data and get the answer first: what the run found, how many decisions wait for you and what they add up to. Open it with Ask, the first entry under Fetch in the rail (/fetch). The app opens here after you choose an instance.
From top to bottom, the page holds:
The question box (Ask a question or use voice command…) and who the run is for. Start here, until your first run has finished. The money line: what is owed, at risk and waiting, for the selected run. The plays and FETCH STARTERS: prepared questions, filtered by play. The answer for the selected run. How FACE knows this, folded: the sources, connections, coverage, runners and run history behind the answer.
data.choose-how-to-be-told#Choose how to be t: Call Me When Finished and WhatsApp Me tell you when the run ends: once every phase has ended, not when the answer comes back. The message says whether the run finished, partly finished, was interrupted by a server restart, or failed.
data.connections#Connections:
Under ACTIVE CONNECTIONS, each connection has a card with its name and type, what the server holds for it (such as whether its credential is stored), and a caption: Included in fetch or Not included for an active connection, Switched off: not read by Fetch for one that is switched off. The caption describes your selection. It does not say whether the source is reachable.
Tap an active card to include it in, or leave it out of, your next run. New connection opens the connection wizard on Settings › Integrations › Systems. Connections a run proposed are listed with Confirm and Dismiss.
data.execution-history#Execution history:
What the run also found lists, for the selected run, the actions the judge removed from the answer (each marked with its verdict) and the forecasts, with ANOMALY where one was detected.
Runs recorded on the server lists every run the server recorded for you, newest first: when it started, how long it took, the runner, and how it ended. An org admin sees every run in the organization. The run cards above it are kept on this device.
Outcome Means Successful It answered, and every phase finished. Partial It answered, and at least one phase did not finish. The run names each one and why. Running It has not answered yet, or a phase after the answer is still running. Answered It answered, and the server has no record of its phases. It is never counted as successful. Failed It did not answer. Refused It was refused before it ran. Interrupted The server stopped before it answered. Run it again. The answer comes back before the run is done: the analysis (the checks, the rules and the scenario verdicts) and the twins’ decisions run after it, in the background.
Archive run history, for org admins, takes every run so far off every page (Ask, Briefs, Why, Options, Actionable Twins) for everyone on the instance. Nothing is deleted: the runs are kept for audit, and an admin can bring them back from Show archived with Restore or Restore all.
data.how-face-knows-this#How FACE knows this:
How FACE knows this (Sources, coverage, runners and run history) is folded under the answer. Open it to see:
how many of its sources the selected run read, naming the ones it could not read and why; how the run sampled each table and what the sample shows of each column, when the run recorded a sample; ACTIVE CONNECTIONS, then Operational coverage, then COMPUTE RUNNERS; EXECUTION HISTORY, with What the run also found and Runs recorded on the server.
data.live-views#Live views:
Cameras, sensors, field readers and devices are connection types. Their card opens a live view, already narrowed to that connection (Connection {id} only; Show all widens it):
Connection type Button What it shows Video Stream (cameras) Surveillance The Surveillance Dashboard: Feed Ingestion grades a feed (Threat Detected — {classification} or No Threat Detected), Sensor Cueing cues one sensor from another, and COP Telemetry Feed streams events. Photos taken with Camera Input are listed under Captured media. MQTT Bus, Sensor Gateway, GPS Telematics, RFID Reader Live sensors What the always-on connections hear, the candidate findings, and for admins the health of the ingest path. Runink Edge (a handheld field reader) Field reader That reader’s sightings as they arrive. When the stream stops, the last frame stays with its age. Any source that reports devices Devices The devices the connection reported, with when each was last seen. A reading with no stated value is never drawn as a number, and silence nobody can judge is shown as unjudged, never as fine.
data.open-a-past-run#Open a past run:
Tap a run under Runs recorded on the server to see its question and how it ended; Show this run’s results makes it the selected run.
Tap a run card kept on this device to open Fetch details (/fetch/run/): how it ended, Query, Runner, Connections, Started, Duration, Error when there was one, Result, What happened to the sources, Automated analysis and Generated SQL. Reuse request asks the same question again.
The page also shows What this fetch was given: each file or capture attached to the run and how it ended (read, read, nothing on it, skipped: {reason} or could not be read: {reason}). Show what was read opens the reading: the structured reading of a photo, Tables in the document, Text read (cut after 64 KiB, and it says so) and Left out. You can correct a value read from a document; the correction is recorded with your name and the value it replaced.
data.operational-coverage#Operational coverag: Operational coverage shows what FACE can see of your operations in the sources it has read (fleet, yard, warehouse and racks, cold chain, shipments, orders, maintenance, drones and automation, IoT sensors and tags), and which decisions that supports. Each decision is Ready, Blocked or Couldn’t check.
data.pick-who-the-run-is-for#Pick who the run: Beside the question box, Who this run is for shows Generalist view until you pick a persona, then For: {name}. The run is written for that persona: the money line and the plays lead with what the persona reads first. The persona changes what the answer leads with, never what FACE reads. Personas are set up under Settings › Personas.
data.plays-and-fetch-starters#Plays and fetch:
The plays are what FACE recovers or protects money on: All plays, Claims recovery, Disruptions, Routes, Fulfilment, Cold chain, Maintenance, Inventory and Fleet. Pick a chip to see only that play’s questions under FETCH STARTERS. The persona the run is for puts its plays first.
The starters come from your connections and your runs. While FACE samples your sources the row says Sampling your sources…, then Suggestions from a quick sample of your sources · {time}, how many sources answered, and Refresh. A source the sample could not read is named with a short reason; Show details shows the source’s own error.
If a play has no question yet, the row says so and offers Connect a source.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: FetchService.RunFetchStream (server stream), ListFetchStarters, ListFetchRuns, GetFetchAttachments. ConfigService.ListConnections, ListRunners, SetConnectionActive, SetRunnerActive (admin only). TwinsService.GetActionQueue, for the waiting decisions. See the API reference.
data.run-it#Run it:
Press Enter or select the send button (Run Fetch). The activity card narrates the run, phase by phase, over whatever page you open next.
If the app cannot reach the server, the run is queued on your device and sent when the connection returns.
data.runners#Runners: Under COMPUTE RUNNERS, each runner has a card with its own Active switch. Tap an active runner to run your next question on it. The card marked Active is the runner the next run will use; other active runners show Standby, and a switched-off one shows Switched off. With no pick, the run goes to the managed runner if it is active, otherwise to the first active runner. New runner opens Settings › Integrations › Runners.
data.start-here#Start here: Until a run has finished, a Start here panel sits above the money line: From no source to your first fetch. Each step is read from the platform, never ticked by hand. Its steps are Connect a data source, Have a runner ready and Run your first fetch. Each says whether it is done, or Could not check this step. The panel goes away once every step is done.
data.the-active-switch#The Active switch:
The Active switch on a connection or runner turns it on or off for every run on the instance: yours, other people’s and scheduled ones. The server enforces it and refuses a run that names a switched-off connection or runner.
Only an admin of the instance can flip the switch. Everyone else sees Active or Inactive. If a switch cannot be saved, {name} was not switched: {error} gives the reason. A switched-off connection also leaves the Map view’s live layers.
data.the-answer#The answer:
The answer card shows the selected run:
its question, or when it ran, as the card’s title; who it was for: Generalist view or For: {name}; what it said. The spoken answer stays on the device that asked, so a run asked elsewhere reads The spoken answer stays on the device that asked. What the run left for you is below.; how many decisions wait and what they add up to (No decision waiting when none does); three ways on: Decide in Actionable Twins, See why and See the options. With no run selected, the card is not shown: the question box and the plays are the page.
data.the-money-line#The money line:
The money line opens the page on money, for the selected run. Each tile opens the page that holds its figure.
Tile What it counts Opens At risk Shipments past their promise, or with a temperature excursion no claim names Why Owed to you Overbilling and duplicate invoices, plus every open claim at its claimed amount Why Claim windows closing in 14 days Of that, what is claimed on open claims whose window closes within 14 days Why Waiting for your approval The run’s decisions not yet decided, and the money they state Actionable Twins Recovered this quarter What your team recorded as recovered Actionable Twins Shipments at risk The value of the shipments at risk, with their count Why A tile shows the change since the last successful run, for example ▲ {amount} since the last run, or Same as the last run. A figure that was not read or not stated says Not measured with its reason. It is never shown as zero. Decisions that state no amount are counted apart ({count} state no amount).
The persona the run is for decides the order: one that reads what is owed first leads with Owed to you and Recovered this quarter; one that reads what is at risk first leads with At risk and Claim windows closing in 14 days. Only the order changes, never a figure.
data.the-selected-run#The selected run:
Ask, Options, Why and Actionable Twins each show one run: the selected run. The page’s title line names it, with Change run and Clear under Run actions.
A run you start selects itself when it answers. Otherwise the newest Successful run on the server is selected. A partial run is never selected for you, but you can open one. Open an earlier run lists every run the server recorded. Only a run with a transaction id can be opened. Clear selects no run. The choice is kept on this device. When the selected run is not the newest one, a notice says so, for example This page shows the fetch of {date}; a newer fetch finished on {newer}., with Show the fetch of {date}.
With no run selected, Options, Why and Actionable Twins show only Your operation’s story starts with a fetch, with Run a fetch and Open an earlier run ({count}). A page shows what the selected run recorded and nothing else: no figures borrowed from other runs. If the run recorded nothing for a page, the page says so.
data.type-say-or-attach-your-question#Type, s:
Type in Ask a question or use voice command…, or pick a question under FETCH STARTERS. Beside the box:
the microphone dictates your question; Camera Input takes a photo; Attach File attaches one or more files. Attachments appear as chips you can remove. FACE reads each file by its content, whatever its name says:
photos: their text, and for JPEG and PNG a structured reading of the document (type, fields, tables, checkboxes); PDF: the text of each page, and a scanned page as a photo; DOCX and PPTX: their text and tables; XLSX: its tables; plain text and HTML: the text; video clips: sampled frames, read the way a camera feed is. A file FACE has no reader for is skipped, and the run says why. A run with only an attachment and no connection still answers, from what it read.

data:
Briefs asks your questions for you, on a schedule, and tells the right people what needs a decision. Each persona gets a weekly brief with one tap, and you can schedule any question of your own. Open it with Briefs, under Fetch in the rail (/active_schedules). The page is titled Weekly briefs.
A brief is an ordinary run of FACE, asked at a set time or when your data changes. Its answer, options and decisions land on Ask, Options, Why and Actionable Twins like any other run.
data.create-or-edit-a-brief#Create or edit a: The editor is titled New brief or Edit brief: A question FACE asks on its own, for one person, and who hears the answer.
data.data-listeners#Data listeners: When any connection’s listener is on, DATA LISTENERS lists it: LISTENING, STARTING, DEGRADED, NOT LISTENING with the reason, or OFF; the events and bytes it read; and the account its usage is metered to. Not reported by the runner yet means the runner has said nothing yet; the page does not guess a state. The page reads the listeners again every 15 seconds while it is open.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: SchedulesService.ListSchedules, CreateSchedule, UpdateSchedule, SetScheduleActive, DeleteSchedule. SchedulesService.ListPersonas, SavePersona, DeletePersona, for the personas. See the API reference.
data.save-brief#Save brief: Next run shows when it will run first. Cost reads Not estimated: FACE does not forecast what a brief that has never run will use. Select Save brief. Brief saved. confirms it; Could not save the brief. Nothing was changed. means nothing was stored.
data.time-or-event#At a set time, or when dat:
A brief set to When data changes runs when a connection’s data listener sees the changes you ask for. The run is the same full run as a timed one.
Listen to: a PostgreSQL connection with the change-event ledger installed, or a Kafka connection. No other source type has a data listener. Run after this many events: how many matching events start a run. Wait for more events (seconds): after the first matching event, wait this long so a burst of changes becomes one run. At most one run every (minutes): the cooldown between runs. Only tables or topics starting with and Only this change narrow what counts. Saving turns the connection’s listener on, on the managed runner. Its events and listening time are metered to your account. NEXT RUN reads On the next matching event. A brief never runs while its previous run is still going, and events that arrive while it is paused are not counted. Pausing or deleting the last active event brief on a connection turns its listener off.
On an event brief’s card, LAST TRIGGER says when it last fired, how many events fired it, the first of them, how many of their rows were read back, and the run’s outcome. When the run’s analysis finishes, RULE RESULTS FROM THESE CHANGES lists each rule the changed rows bear on, with its verdict. Not fired yet — waiting for events means no run has started.
data.weekly-briefs#Weekly briefs:
The top of the page lists one row per persona of this instance: the product’s five (Field operations manager, CFO, CRO, CMO and CEO) and any your instance added. Each row shows the question its brief asks and the persona’s plays. Your own persona, set under Settings › Account, is listed first and marked Yours.
Add brief schedules that persona’s brief. It runs every Monday at 07:00 on this device’s clock, and is sent on WhatsApp to the numbers in Settings › Integrations › Channels. Once added, the row reads Added · next run {next}, or PAUSED. Edit opens the persona editor, the same one as Settings › Personas. Add persona adds a new one. What you save is shared with everyone on the instance. Ask FACE as {name} opens the assistant for that persona, with its question first. Deadline watch is not a persona. It asks every day at 07:00 which claim windows close in the next 3 days, and what evidence each still needs.
If the instance’s personas cannot be read, the page says so and lists the product’s five in the product’s own words.
data.what-to-ask#What to ask: Type the question in plain words, or pick one under Start from a common question. The question is also the brief’s name.
data.when#When: At a set time runs Every day, Every week or Every month, at the time of day you save it. When data changes runs on events (see below). Times are on this device’s clock.
data.where-to-look#Where to look: Tick the connections each run reads. With all ticked, it reads every connection, including ones added later. A brief that reads nothing cannot be saved.
data.who-hears-about-it#Who hears about it:
Pick WhatsApp, Phone call or Email, and when to Tell them: After every run, When it drafts a Twins decision, When a decision needs approval, or When $ at stake reaches a threshold with a Minimum $ at stake. Only decisions that state a dollar figure count toward the threshold.
When a run finishes, FACE tells the numbers in Settings › Integrations › Channels what needs a decision: the new decisions, the top ones with the money at stake and the deadline when stated, and a link to Actionable Twins. Email goes out from the mailbox connected under Settings › Integrations › Channels, to that same address. With no mailbox connected, the editor says email is off.
data.who-its-for#Who it\u0026rsquo;s for: Pick the persona, or Generalist view. Their question fills in below.
data.your-briefs#Your briefs:
Below the weekly briefs, each brief has a card:
ACTIVE or PAUSED, and EVENT for a brief that runs when data changes; who it is for (For: {name}), and what it reads, for example Reads: all connections; FREQUENCY, NEXT RUN and LAST RUN. A brief that has not run yet says Never run, not a success or a failure; how it notifies (Notify: {channels} · {condition}, or Notify: off), and under LAST NOTICE what its last notice did: Sent, Not needed, Not sent (with the reason), Partly sent or Waiting for the run to finish. The switch (Toggle schedule status) pauses or resumes a brief. Edit Schedule opens it in the editor. Delete Schedule asks Delete schedule? first. Filter Tasks shows All, Active only or Paused only. CREATE NEW SCHEDULE opens a blank editor.
With no brief at all, the page says No schedules yet and offers Create schedule. A list that could not be read shows the error, not an empty page.

data: Every page after sign-in shares one frame: the rail on the left, one title line across the top, and the assistant at the bottom right. The rail is the only menu.
data.the-activity-card#The activity card:
While a run or another long operation works, a card narrates it over whatever page is open. Long operations include testing a connection, indexing documents and reading a document source.
The headline says what is running, for example Running your fetch…, then how it ended. The steps are the phases as the server reports them, each running, done, failed, out of time, skipped or partial. Show reasoning opens the run’s full reasoning, with every step. While a run works, the card may show messages from Runink’s partners, each under the partner’s name (From {name}).
data.the-automated-analysis-notice#The automa:
If automated analysis is not ready, a strip under the title line says so:
Automated analysis is starting up… while it loads; Automated analysis is not ready — features that need it are unavailable. when it cannot answer. The strip adds Everything else works now. and offers Check again. It goes away once automated analysis is ready.
data.the-face-ai-assistant#The FACE AI assist:
The round button at the bottom right of every page opens the assistant. Its tooltip is FACE AI, and screen readers announce Open FACE AI assistant. It floats over the page.
The assistant knows which page you are on. It suggests the question of the selected run, your persona’s question, then two prompts for the page: on Ask and Integrations, Create new connection and Find extra docs; on Options, Trigger Shadow Simulation and Optimize sliders; on Why, Check Rules and Find logic gaps; elsewhere, Help me with this screen and What can I do here?.
Control Label Text box Ask FACE… Send Send message Microphone Speak your question. It is sent when you stop. Camera Take a photo Attachment Attach a file The answer lists every step FACE ran as done, failed or blocked, with the reason. How this was worked out shows the reasoning. FACE AI could not answer means the request failed, and the reason follows. No answer came back means the assistant finished but returned nothing.
Behind the frame: FetchService.RunFetchStream, ListFetchRuns and ModelService.GetModelStatus. See the API reference.
data.the-rail#The rail:
The rail has three labelled sections, and Settings at its foot:
Section Pages Fetch Ask · Briefs Simulate Options · Why Twins Actionable Twins (foot) Settings Below Settings are the signed-in account, with Log out, and the instance FACE is acting for. Select it to choose another instance.
Pages that are not in the rail light the entry they belong to:
You are on Lit entry A past run (/fetch/run/), or a live view opened from a connection’s card (Surveillance, Live sensors, Field reader, Devices) Ask A brief’s editor Briefs A scenario’s details page Options The Map view, site plans, twin entities or one entity’s page, Follow-ups, a decision artifact, a remediation screen Actionable Twins Admin, and the connection wizard Settings An address the app does not know lights Ask.
Each rail entry is a button with a visible focus ring. Screen readers announce its label and whether it is the page you are on.
data.the-storyboard#After the answer:
The answer coming back does not finish a run. The analysis and the twins’ decisions run after it. From the answer on, the card tells the run’s story:
The headline follows how the run ends: Fetch answered — still analysing while a phase runs; Fetch finished when every phase finished; Fetch partly finished, or Fetch partly finished — interrupted by a server restart; Fetch failed; or Fetch answered — its phases were not recorded. A partly finished run says Did not finish: and names each phase. The steps are four items, one per page: Ask (what was read), Why (what it means), Options (what could happen) and Actionable Twins (what we do). Each shows its state and one line from the run’s own record. While a phase works it says so, for example Judging the scenarios…, or Waiting to start. Nothing recorded appears only for a phase that ended and left nothing. Select an item to open its page for this run. A finished card closes itself after a short while, but not while the pointer is over it or focus is inside it. A running card never closes on its own. If several operations run at once, the card shows the most recent.
data.the-title-line#The title line:
The title line reads FACE and the page’s name. On Ask, Options, Why and Actionable Twins it also names the selected run, with Run actions (Change run, Clear). On every other page it carries the audit: how the last run ended, as Passing, Needs attention, Failing, Running or Not run yet, with the reason and Open audit. When runs have proposed connections, the audit counts them.
Not run yet appears only when the server has recorded no run at all.

data:
Options answers “what could we do, and what is each option worth?” for the selected run. It compares the options for each decision the run’s checks stand behind, recommends one only when it is a clear winner, and lists the scenarios FACE tested. Open it with Options, under Simulate in the rail (/simulate?tab=swarm).
FACE never acts alone. An option you send goes to a named person for approval on Actionable Twins, and nothing changes until they approve it.
data.a-clear-winner-or-none#A clear winner, o:
FACE recommends one option only when its range clears both the next option’s range and the figure as measured. The card is then marked Recommended, and the header says Recommended: {option} with the reason.
Otherwise the header says No clear winner on this data, with why:
The best option’s range overlaps the next one’s. The best option’s range overlaps the figure as measured, so it is not clearly better than leaving things as they are. Fewer than two options could be measured. A sample that did not read every row says so: A bounded sample: some tables hold more rows than were read.
data.found-outside-your-data#Found outside yo: When the run searched the web, what it found is shown here, and only here, under SHADOW CRAWLER TELEMETRY: each finding with its source, Relevance: {relevance} and the query that found it (Query: {query}).
data.how-face-knows-this#How FACE knows this:
How FACE knows this (How each scenario ended, what went to the twins, and the run step by step) is folded at the foot of the page. It holds:
how many scenarios ended each way; the hand-off to the twins: Sent to the twins: {sent} · removed from twins analyses: {removed}, or why it is not known; the run’s story: what the analysis proposed and simulated, which verdicts went to the twins, and what the twins do next; the agents re-running on their own after a rule was validated or a scenario changed (Running on their own after a rule or scenario change: {agents}).
data.new-simulation#New Simulation: New Simulation builds and runs a scenario of your own. Back to the options returns you to the page.
data.pick-a-business-area-and-a-scenario#Pick: Under Scenario categories, pick a business area and one of its scenarios, or New scenario: name it, pick its business area, then what it tests.
data.pick-what-to-test-and-the-news-to-watch#: Under What to test, pick one or more items (New item adds a business measure, such as spoiled pallets per week). Under Market news to watch, pick the terms a coming run searches on the web (New term adds your own). Each run searches only a limited number of terms, and the ones your team added go first.
data.read-the-options#Read the options:
Every option is scored on one measure, stated at the top. For example: Every option is scored on one measure: the share of the temperature readings read that sit past a limit their own row states. Each option card shows:
the option, as a lever and a change (for example a temperature excursion moved by −1 °C), or by name (Air expedite, Internal transfer, Do nothing); its rank (#{rank}) and its figure with a 95% range; the evidence it leans on: the effect estimated from the run’s rows with its 95% interval, The baseline: the other options’ effects are measured against it., or Effect not estimated: {reason}; who must approve it: One named person must approve it. or Two different named people must approve it. An option marked Advice only: approving it records the decision and runs nothing. changes nothing when approved. An option whose baseline is missing reads Not measured: needs {needs} and is never ranked. Not measured is never drawn as zero.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: HypothesisService.CompareOptions, SendToTwins. HypothesisService.InteractiveSimulate, FetchService.GetScenarioGraph. See the API reference.
data.save-or-run#Save or run:
Save Scenario saves it without simulating. Run Full Simulation simulates it.
The result shows how confident the simulation is, the effects it reasoned from (Why: what this draft reasoned from), any anomalies it detected and its forecast. A forecast needs at least two points; one point is not drawn as a trend.
Send to Actionable Twins hands the result to the approval queue:
You see Meaning Queued for Twins A card was queued. VIEW IN TWINS opens it. No actions were produced by this run The server accepted the scenario and named no card, so there is nothing to approve. The handoff to Twins did not complete Nothing was queued. The reason is shown.
data.send-an-option-for-approval#Send an opti: Select Send for approval on an option. FACE compares the options again on the server and puts its own figures on the decision, then queues it for a named approver on Actionable Twins. Not sent: {error} means nothing was queued.
data.set-the-levers#Set the levers: Under Scenario levers, set the levers for what you picked. Until you pick, each lever keeps its usual value.
data.what-could-we-do#What could we do:
The page opens on What could we do, under For: {alert} when the run raised an alert on Why. Each decision the run’s checks stand behind is a chip; the one behind Why’s alert comes first. See options on Why opens this page on that decision. Pick a chip to read its options.
If no check on the run stands behind a decision, the page says No check on this run stands behind a decision yet, so there is nothing to compare.
data.what-face-tested#What FACE tested:
Under the options, one line counts the scenarios the run tested and how many succeeded, with See them.
The scenarios are a List by default: how each ended, as an icon and a word, its title, its business area and what it found. Graph shows the same scenarios as a flow from what was tested to how it ended. Select a scenario to open its details page (/lab/scenario/).
If the run recorded no scenario, the page says This run recorded no scenario.

data: Settings is where you set up who you are, who your briefs are for, what FACE connects to, and your plan. Open it with Settings at the foot of the rail (/settings). It has four tabs: Account, Personas, Integrations and Subscription. The address names the tab (/settings?tab=account, personas, integrations or subscription), so a link or a bookmark opens the right one.
data.account#Account: Account (/settings?tab=account) is about you: who is signed in, your preferences, your sessions and your data.
data.add-a-connection#Add a connection:
New connection opens the wizard: Pick a source, fill in its details, choose a runner, then test and save. Its steps are Source, Details, Credentials, Runner and Review.
Source. Pick a source card from the catalog, or search by product or by system. Details. Name the connection and fill in its settings. For a database, choose the encryption in transit; the strictest option is Encrypt, verify the chain and the hostname. Credentials. A credential field is write-only: once saved it is never shown again. Runner. Choose where the source is read from. Runink managed runs inside the server. Every test and read of the connection runs on the runner you pick, or is refused. Review. Check every value, then select Test & save. A passing test means the source answered; it does not mean data has been read. A connection proposed by a run opens the same wizard from Confirm, on the proposal’s source card with its name filled in. You still enter every address and credential.
For each connector’s settings, see Data sources.
data.admin#Admin: If you are an admin of the selected instance, an Admin card comes first. It opens Admin. Nobody else sees it.
data.channels#Channels:
Channels holds how FACE reaches people: each channel’s status (voice, SMS and WhatsApp), the sender numbers, the carrier’s write-only secrets and the delivery trail. Everyone with a role on the instance can read it; only an admin can change it.
KEYS & NUMBERS holds the WhatsApp Phone Number, Phone Number, SMS Phone Number, Stripe API Key, Google Credentials (Gmail, Drive) and Google Analytics ID. A secret shows only Configured (hidden) or Not Set. To change it, enter a new value: Enter a new value to replace it. The stored value is never shown.
EMAIL FOR BRIEFS is the mailbox your briefs are emailed from. Briefs by email leave from your own mailbox and go to its own address; FACE has no shared sender. Connect it with Connect Gmail or Connect Microsoft 365 when your instance has those sign-ins set up, or as an SMTP mailbox with Test and connect: FACE logs in to test it and keeps it only if that works. The card shows the address, the provider and whether it can send now.
data.compute-units#Compute units:
Compute units shows how many CUs are left out of the dedicated CUs you set (CUs left out of {dedicated} dedicated). This is a ceiling you set yourself, not your plan’s allowance. When none are left, FACE refuses new runs until you raise it. Change it under Adjust dedicated CUs. Card payment says whether a Stripe key is set.
The readout tells three cases apart:
You see Meaning Measuring… The budget has not answered yet. Unavailable The budget did not load, so nothing is a measurement. Not measured No budget has been read for this instance yet.
data.contacts#Contacts:
Contacts lists who the agent may message or call, one row per contact and channel, with whether that channel can reach them. A banner names each channel contacts may use but nobody set up, with a button to set it up.
Import from a system (Import contacts) reads contacts from your connected systems (CRM, ERP, TMS and others). Imported contacts are read-only here: change them at the source and import again, and they are updated, not duplicated.
data.integrations#Integrations: Integrations (/settings?tab=integrations) has four sections: Channels, Systems, Contacts and Runners. The address names the section with §ion= (channels, data-sources, contacts or runners).
data.personas#Personas:
Personas (/settings?tab=personas) holds who a brief is for: Who a brief is for: a name, the question its brief asks, and the money figure it reads first. What you save here is shared with everyone on the instance.
Every persona of the instance is a profile: the product’s five, in your instance’s words if someone reworded one, then the ones your instance added. Each shows:
what it Reads first: Owed, At risk or the money line’s own order (Line order); Responsible for, Asks (the question its brief asks) and Plays (None picked: this persona answers for every play.); Briefs: how many it has and the next run, or No brief yet; Next step: Add a brief for {name} or See the briefs for {name}. Edit and Add persona open the persona editor, the same one as on Briefs. Save with Save for everyone. An added persona can be deleted (Delete for everyone), and a reworded product persona can be reset (Put back the product’s words).
data.preferences#Preferences: Theme: Light, Dark or System. This device remembers your choice. Interface language: the language of the app’s screens. Agent language: The agent listens to voice commands and reads its answers aloud in the agent language. It is also the language FACE writes its answers in. Your role: the persona you are. Your brief is listed first on Briefs, and Ask’s money line leads with the figures your role reads first. Not set changes nothing. Offline answers says whether this device can answer offline, and why not.
data.rpcs-behind-this-page#RPCs behind this p: runink.ui.profile.v1.ProfileService: GetProfile, EndAllSessions. ConfigService.GetIntegrationConfig, SetIntegrationConfig. runink.ui.datasources.v1.ConnectionsService and RunnersService. MeteringService.GetComputeBudget, SetComputeBudget. runink.ui.billing.v1.BillingService: GetOverview, ListPlans, QuotePlan. See the API reference.
data.runners#Runners: Runners lists where reads of your data sources run: the managed runner (Runink managed, part of the server, the default for every connection) and runners on your own network that the server connects to. Add runner registers a self-hosted runner and gives its one-time setup ticket. Each runner shows its state (active, pending or revoked), its health and how many reads it has in flight.
data.security#Security: Sign out ends this session. Sign out everywhere ends every session of yours on every device, this one included. Confirm with Yes, sign out everywhere.
data.subscription#Subscription:
Subscription (/settings?tab=subscription) shows your plan, your compute units and what FACE returned. See Plans and billing for the prices.
What FACE returned: what was recovered this quarter, against the success fees billed. The plan card: the plan, its status, the seats and the instance FACE is acting for. Compare plans opens the plan list, the measured usage and the estimate. Compute units and Adjust dedicated CUs (see below). FACE takes no payment itself. The plan list says so: Billing is not configured on this deployment. Plans and prices are shown for reference; no payment can be taken here. Readers and service accounts can’t start a checkout or open the billing portal.
No subscription is on record for this account. means the record was read and is empty. The subscription record could not be read. This does not mean there is no subscription. means the request failed.
data.systems#Systems:
Systems is the list of your data sources. Each row shows the connection’s name, type and id, where it runs (Runink managed or runs on {runner}), its credential chip (for example credential stored) and its last test. A stored credential is never shown; the chip says only that one is held.
The row buttons are Edit, Rotate credentials, Test, Listener and Delete. Test opens the source with its stored credential on the connection’s runner, read-only and time-limited, and reads nothing from it. Delete asks first, because it also deletes the credential bundle. A files connection also offers Index documents.
data.who-you-are#Who you are: The identity card lists your Email, Name, Signed in with, Role, Platform admin, Tenant and Account ID. A value the server did not provide reads Not provided. Signed in with is Google account, Password or an API key.
data.your-data#Your data: It stays on your instance. No exit fees, no lock-in. Close account & take my data explains what closing an account involves; closing is not automated, and nothing here schedules a deletion. Open-source licences lists the licences of the software the app includes.

data:
