Streams link to their replay recordings, never to a file bundle.
data.what-these-quickstarts-are-not#What thes: Not product data. Nothing in the downloads is read by the FACE backend at runtime, and the product image carries none of it. Not a deployment. The test estate is made of throwaway test services whose credentials are published. Keep it on a scratch machine. Not a measurement of every connector. A test compares FACE’s discovery with the expected model for PostgreSQL and MySQL. For every other type, the expected model is the shape the source holds, and each page says what FACE reads for that type.
data.where-a-quickstart-connection-goes-in-fa: Add it in Settings › Integrations › Systems: select New connection, pick the source, fill in the settings and credentials, choose the runner, then Test & save. Use it on Ask. Every connection shows as a card among Ask’s sources, marked Included in fetch or Not included. An admin can switch a connection Active or Inactive; an inactive one is not read. Use it in a brief. In the brief’s editor on Briefs, tick the connections it reads. With all ticked, it reads every connection, including ones added later. A brief that reads nothing cannot be saved. Watch a live source. A camera opens Surveillance; an MQTT, IoT, sensor-gateway, GPS or RFID connection opens Live sensors and Devices; a field reader opens Field reader and Devices. Each opens from that connection’s card on Ask, already narrowed to it.

data: The test-estate safety rule: stand the test estate up only beside a test instance, never a production deployment. Its systems are throwaway test services with published credentials: change-me is every test credential. They are still encrypted and still ask for a login, because FACE refuses a connection that is not (see Connector security). Use a scratch machine or a scratch cluster. This is the end-to-end walkthrough: one company in every connector, and FACE making sense of all of them together. Every source below is a view of the same company, Quillmere Freight Lines (quillmere.invalid). A shipment in PostgreSQL is the same shipment in the Kafka events, the GPS track, the SAP delivery, the Salesforce case, the claim PDF, the dock-camera frame and the RFID read. Six anomalies are planted across the sources, and each one can only be seen by reading more than one of them.

data.add-the-business-apps-and-the-systems-of: Add salesforce, sap, guidewire, servicenow, hubspot, d365, sharepoint and github, then the logistics systems: oms, tms, whs, yms, ims, inventory and logisticsapi. Each page says what FACE reads for that type. Where FACE reads no catalogue, open the payload next to its expected model: the shared keys are the same strings.
data.add-the-cloud-warehouses#Add the cloud w: snowflake, databricks, redshift and bigquery need a cloud account. Load their SQL into an account you own. Against a real account, FACE reads the Snowflake and Databricks catalogues; for Redshift and BigQuery, show the dataset next to its expected model.
data.add-the-event-bus-and-the-telemetry#Add: Stand up kafka, or the live Kafka estate for a stream that does not end, and use the recordings for mqtt, iot, gps, rfid, sensorgateway and cctv. Kafka shows its topic list and value schemas. Its Schema Registry and ksqlDB add which business domain each topic’s schema belongs to, which topic a query computes from which, and which topics carry no traffic. The telemetry sources have no catalogue: FACE collects for a window and infers each feed’s shape, and the reader location, the GPS asset_ids and the gateway channels settings tie readings to docks and trailers.
data.add-the-files#Add the files: The files dataset lays the estate’s files out by the store each would live in: claim and invoice PDFs on S3, dock photos on GCS, dock video on Azure, the carrier rate sheet over SFTP, the scorecard on SharePoint, and an orders export on the runner’s disk. The PDFs are real PDF text, the images decode and the clips are MJPEG. Its page names the connection type that reads each store. excel, document and objectstore hold three more small datasets.
data.connect-the-two-databases-face-reads-end: Load postgres and mysql into scratch engines and add both connections. Explore returns their tables, columns, types, primary keys and declared foreign keys: the operational system (customers, orders, shipments) and freight billing (carriers, rate contracts, invoices). These two are the ones a test checks against the expected model, so start here.
data.the-six-planted-anomalies#The six plante: Each anomaly is the only one of its kind in the universe, and a test re-measures each one from the data. Files inside a zip are named by their path in that zip.

data.stand-up-the-test-system#Stand up the te:
The safety rule at the top of this page comes first: a scratch machine or a scratch cluster, never a production or platform one.
Download postgres.zip and unzip it. It holds postgres/01_schema.sql, the rows in postgres/02_data_01.sql to postgres/02_data_16.sql (load them in name order), and postgres/expected.json.
Start a scratch PostgreSQL 13 or later with TLS on, because ssl_mode require needs it. The official image ships a self-signed certificate you can use for a test:
docker run --rm -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me -p 5432:5432 postgres:16 \ -c ssl=on \ -c ssl_cert_file=/etc/ssl/certs/ssl-cert-snakeoil.pem \ -c ssl_key_file=/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key Create the database and the reader role, then load the schema and the rows, in that order:
psql -h localhost -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE quillmere_ops" psql -h localhost -U postgres -c "CREATE ROLE face_reader LOGIN PASSWORD 'change-me'" psql -h localhost -U postgres -d quillmere_ops -f postgres/01_schema.sql $(for f in postgres/02_data_*.sql; do printf -- '-f %s ' "$f"; done) psql -h localhost -U postgres -d quillmere_ops -c "GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA ops TO face_reader; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA ops TO face_reader" Add the connection with the settings above, as Create it in the Console shows. Replace pg.quillmere.invalid with the address of your scratch engine: a .invalid name never resolves.

data.what-face-finds#What FACE finds:
FACE reads the catalogue: information_schema, with the declared primary and foreign keys, every COMMENT ON table, view and column as the dataset’s and field’s description, and each view’s definition (pg_get_viewdef). Partitions and relations an extension owns (such as pg_stat_statements’ views) are not listed as datasets; the discovery says how many were left out. A test loads this dataset into an empty engine, runs FACE’s discovery, and compares the result with the expected model (TestSynthUniverseDiscoveryMatchesExpected).

data.what-it-is#What it is: A PostgreSQL database. In the test estate it is Quillmere’s operational system, schema ops: customers and their delivery sites, warehouses, yards and docks; 150 days of orders and the shipments that served them, leg by leg; the fleet, the site and yard equipment with their readings against stated limits, and the maintenance work orders; inventory, reorder policies and replenishment orders; route plans, their stops and their revisions; freight invoices, claims, their evidence and correspondence. The connector reference is SQL warehouses and databases.
data.what-the-rows-let-face-show#What the row: Scenario Tables What FACE does with them Routes shipments (origin_warehouse_id, dest_site_id, status, transport_mode, temp_min_c/temp_max_c), customer_sites (lat/lon) the run’s routes phase draws every pending shipment from its warehouse to its customer site, with the tightest temperature band the routed shipments state Reactive fulfilment inventory_positions (on_hand, available, lead_time_days), orders + order_lines the site page computes safety stock and a reorder point per item from the lead time and the daily demand, and shows the items under it after the last demand spike Fleet planning route_stops (a dispatch feed’s columns: vehicle_id, stop_sequence, latitude/longitude, demand_kg, vehicle_capacity_kg, planning_speed_kmh, window_start/window_end, temperature_min_c/max_c), vehicles (status, capacity, reefer capability), vehicle_shifts the fleet planner’s stops, beside the GPS fixes of the live fleet topic Recursive re-plans route_plan_revisions (trigger_kind, triggered_by_revision_id, legs_before/legs_after) the history of re-plans, an excursion’s re-plan triggering a delay re-plan, a reassignment and the receiving plan’s re-plan Predictive maintenance site_assets, asset_channels (each limit and its source), asset_readings, maintenance_work_orders 30 days of readings to check a projection against what happened; the live readings are on the Kafka equipment topic Cold chain shipment_legs (band per leg), reefer_readings, temperature_excursions time out of band per leg Claims claims, claim_evidence, claim_messages (sent, replied, resolved, closed), remediation_orders follow a claim from filing to close Late deliveries, invoices over the contracted rate and claims filed past the carrier’s window occur at about 15%, 12% and 15%. About one asset in twelve has a service overdue.
data.where-the-sites-are#Where the sites are:
ops.warehouses and ops.yards give every warehouse and yard a postal address and coordinates, so a fetch of this source puts them on the twins Map: FACE writes a Site entity for each row, placed by the coordinates the row states (lat/lon on warehouses, latitude/longitude on yards), with the address and the docks of ops.docks on its page. FACE never geocodes an address: a site with only an address is listed, not placed.
The customer delivery sites (ops.customer_sites), the suppliers and the carriers’ depots stand at real city centroids: the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2024 Gazetteer internal point of an Illinois or Indiana city, with no street address. FACE places a destination at the coordinates the row states.
The distribution centres are authored for this quickstart, not measured. The cities, postal codes and coordinates are real places, a point in an industrial district of each city, so the Map puts each site somewhere true. No street address is a real business’s.

data.what-face-finds#What FACE finds:
Against a real account, FACE reads INFORMATION_SCHEMA. There is no local engine, so the expected model is what that read returns for this dataset.
FACE also reads object tags and masking and row access policies from SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.TAG_REFERENCES and POLICY_REFERENCES. It runs two bounded queries per discovery. To allow them, grant the connection’s role IMPORTED PRIVILEGES on the SNOWFLAKE database, or the SNOWFLAKE.OBJECT_VIEWER and SNOWFLAKE.GOVERNANCE_VIEWER database roles. Without that grant, discovery still works and reports tags and policies as not readable. These views lag by up to two hours. The quickstart dataset declares no tags or policies.

data.stand-up-the-test-system#Stand up the te:
The safety rule at the top of this page comes first: a scratch machine or a scratch cluster, never a production or platform one.
Download files.zip and unzip it. Each store has its own folder under files/: s3/, gcs/, azure/, sftp/, sharepoint/ and host/.
Put each folder where its store expects it: upload files/s3/quillmere-claims/ to a bucket named quillmere-claims in an S3-compatible store you own, served over https:// (MinIO is one open-source option), files/gcs/ to a GCS bucket, and so on.
Connect each store, in Settings › Integrations › Systems, with the connection type that reads it:
many documents under one bucket and prefix, on an S3-compatible store, GCS or a SharePoint library: a files connection, with provider naming the store; delimited files, JSON and Parquet in a bucket, one object as a table: objectstore; a workbook read from a path: excel; a SharePoint list: sharepoint. A files connection does not read the azure/, sftp/ or host/ folders: providers azure, sftp and host are refused when the connection is tested, before anything is dialled. Those folders are here as the shape of the estate’s files.
data.the-expected-model#The expected model:
The expected model is what each file yields when it is read by its format: PDF text, an image, video frames, a sheet, or delimited text. A file is read by what it is.

data.stand-up-the-test-system#Stand up the te:
The safety rule at the top of this page comes first: a scratch machine or a scratch cluster, never a production or platform one.
Run an MQTT 3.1.1 broker you control, with a TLS listener (port 8883) and password logins, and a face-reader user. Eclipse Mosquitto is one open-source option: give its listener a certfile, keyfile and cafile, and a password_file.
Download messages.jsonl from the recording below and publish it. Each line is one message, in time order: its topic, qos, retain flag and JSON payload. With Mosquitto’s client and jq, over the same TLS listener (ca.crt is the CA that signed the broker’s certificate, and is the name on it):
jq -r '"\(.topic)\t\(.qos)\t\(.retain)\t\(.payload | tojson)"' messages.jsonl | while IFS=$'\t' read -r topic qos retain payload; do if [ "$retain" = true ]; then r=-r; else r=; fi mosquitto_pub -h -p 8883 --cafile ca.crt -u -P change-me \ -t "$topic" -q "$qos" $r -m "$payload" done Add the connection in Settings › Integrations › Systems, with endpoint set to mqtts://:8883 and the settings above. FACE subscribes to quillmere/tags/+/event for the collection window.
To watch the events arrive, open Live sensors or Devices from the connection’s card on Ask.

data: The test-estate safety rule: stand the test estate up only beside a test instance, never a production deployment. The broker below is encrypted and every client logs in, but its certificate authority, keys and passwords are generated on your machine for this test only. Use a scratch machine. Streaming · type kafka · a broker on your machine, fed without end
data.1-generate-the-keys-and-passwords#1. Gen:
In an empty directory, save this as setup.sh and run it once (sh setup.sh). It writes the passwords to .env, which Compose reads, and the certificate authority, the broker’s and the registry’s certificates and the client files to secrets/. The authority’s private key is deleted as soon as it has signed, so nothing else can be signed with it.
#!/bin/sh # The name FACE uses to reach this machine. Keep localhost when FACE runs here. KAFKA_HOST=${KAFKA_HOST:-localhost} set -eu umask 077 mkdir -p secrets pw() { openssl rand -hex 20; } cat > .env <
data.2-start-the-broker-the-registry-and-the-:
Save this as compose.yaml in the same directory:
x-kafka-image: &kafka-image apache/kafka:4.2.2 x-karapace-image: &karapace-image ghcr.io/aiven-open/karapace:6.2.4 services: # Formats the broker's storage WITH its SCRAM users, once, before it starts. format: image: *kafka-image user: "1000:1000" volumes: [kafka-data:/var/lib/kafka/data] entrypoint: ["bash", "-c"] command: - | cat > /tmp/format.properties <
data.3-list-the-topics-and-read-a-few-records:
Log in as face-reader, the user FACE will use:
docker exec broker /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server broker:29092 \ --command-config /etc/kafka/tls/face-reader.properties --list . ./.env curl -s --cacert secrets/ca.crt -u "face-reader:$REGISTRY_FACE_READER" https://localhost:8081/subjects You see the twelve topics below and one -value subject for each.
docker exec broker /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-console-consumer.sh \ --bootstrap-server broker:29092 \ --consumer.config /etc/kafka/tls/face-reader.properties \ --topic quillmere.fleet.telematics.v1 \ --from-beginning --max-messages 5 \ --property print.key=true --property print.timestamp=true The key is the trailer ID. The value is Avro in the Confluent wire format: a zero byte, the 4-byte schema ID, then the Avro body. The console consumer prints it as raw bytes. To read values as text, run the producer without --registry: it then writes JSON values and registers no schemas.
data.4-add-the-connection-in-face#4. Add the:
In Settings › Integrations › Systems, add a Kafka connection:
Setting Value bootstrap_servers localhost:9092 topics quillmere. client_id face-quickstart security_protocol sasl_ssl sasl_mechanism scram-sha-512 username face-reader ssl_ca_pem the contents of secrets/ca.crt schema_registry_url https://localhost:8081 schema_registry_username face-reader Credential Value password SCRAM_FACE_READER from .env schema_registry_password REGISTRY_FACE_READER from .env ssl_ca_pem is a certificate, not a secret: it is what lets FACE check the broker’s and the registry’s certificates against the authority you generated, instead of trusting anything. localhost works when FACE runs on the same machine as the broker. If FACE runs elsewhere, use the KAFKA_HOST you gave setup.sh in both addresses, for example kafka-host.example.invalid:9092 and https://kafka-host.example.invalid:8081.
topics is a prefix filter: quillmere. matches all twelve topics.
FACE lands a fetch of one Kafka connection as one table, every topic it reads side by side. So that the readings are read as readings, give the two sensor-reading topics their own connections, each with the property runink.domain:
Connection topics Property runink.domain What FACE reads from it Fleet sensor readings quillmere.fleet.sensor-readings. telemetry vehicle positions on the map, and cold-chain time out of band Equipment readings quillmere.assets.equipment-readings. equipment trends towards each channel’s stated limit, with the projected crossing and narrow the first connection’s topics to the other ten (quillmere.fleet.telematics., quillmere.site., quillmere.drone., quillmere.yard., quillmere.mainframe.). All three use the same security settings and credentials.
data.reproducing-a-run#Reproducing a run:
The stream is deterministic. The same --seed and --start give the same records, byte for byte:
docker run --rm face-stream-producer:1.4.0 produce kafka --dry-run --ticks 60 --start 2026-10-11T12:00:00Z --dry-run prints a minute of records as JSON lines and opens no connection. Other flags:
Flag Default --bootstrap none The broker, host:port --security-protocol plaintext sasl_ssl for this broker; FACE itself connects only with sasl_ssl --sasl-mechanism SCRAM-SHA-512 SCRAM-SHA-512 or SCRAM-SHA-256 --sasl-username, --sasl-password-file none The broker login; the password is read from the file --tls-ca-file none The certificate authority the broker’s and the registry’s certificates must chain to --registry none The Schema Registry URL, https:// with a secured broker. Without it, values are JSON. --registry-username, --registry-password-file none The registry login; the password is read from the file --rate about 7 Events per second across all topics. A higher rate runs the estate faster. --seed 20261005 The quickstart universe’s seed --start now Event time of the first record --retention, --retention-bytes 24h, 64 MiB Topic retention, set when the producer creates a topic
data.step-by-step-in-the-console#Step by step:
Open Settings › Integrations › Systems and select New connection.
Source: under Sensors & telemetry, select Apache Kafka, then Next.
Details: enter a Connection name (the Id follows it) and the Environment. Under Settings, fill in Bootstrap servers (comma-separated), Topics (a prefix) and User (face-reader).
Set Security protocol to sasl_ssl. It is the only value FACE saves: plaintext and SASL_PLAINTEXT send everything unencrypted, and ssl carries no login.
Under Credentials, enter Password and Schema Registry password from .env.
Open Advanced and set SASL mechanism to scram-sha-512, Client ID, Schema Registry URL (https://…), Schema Registry user (face-reader) and CA certificate (the contents of secrets/ca.crt). The form has no switch to skip certificate checks, and FACE refuses a connection with insecure_skip_verify on.
Runner: keep Runink managed, or pick a registered runner that can reach the broker, then Next.
Review: check the values, keep Test after saving ticked and select Test & save. If a security setting is missing, the Console says which and does not save.
The test routes to the runner and asks the broker to answer. Tested: the source answered means the broker is reachable and accepted the login; it does not mean records have been read. Select Done.
The connection joins the list and appears among the sources on Ask, and in every brief’s source list.
data.stop-and-clean-up#Stop and clean up: docker compose down -v rm -rf secrets .env -v removes the broker’s volume with every topic and record, and the registry’s login file. Removing secrets/ and .env deletes the keys and passwords.
data.the-mainframe-records#The mainframe reco:
The two mainframe topics are change data, as a capture agent delivers it from an IMS database updated by CICS transactions. Each record carries the fixed-width record, already converted from EBCDIC, and the same fields decoded. op is REFRESH for the initial full read, then INSERT or UPDATE.
The order header record, copybook QORDHDR, 88 bytes:
05 OH-ORDER-ID PIC X(10). 05 OH-CUST-ID PIC X(10). 05 OH-CUST-PO PIC X(16). 05 OH-WHSE-ID PIC X(10). 05 OH-STATUS PIC X(2). OP, AL, PK or SH 05 OH-LINE-COUNT PIC 9(3). 05 OH-TOTAL-CENTS PIC 9(11). 05 OH-CHANGED-TS PIC X(26). YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.NNNNNN The inventory balance record, copybook QINVBAL, 88 bytes:
05 IB-SKU-ID PIC X(10). 05 IB-LOC-ID PIC X(10). 05 IB-DESC PIC X(24). 05 IB-UOM PIC X(2). 05 IB-ON-HAND PIC S9(7) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE. 05 IB-ALLOCATED PIC S9(7) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE. 05 IB-CHANGED-TS PIC X(26). The mainframe is a source in its own right: it opens with a balance for every quickstart item at every warehouse, then changes them. New orders continue the order numbers after the quickstart’s 24 orders and use its customers and items.
data.the-planted-anomalies#The planted anomal:
Six anomalies recur every hour, so FACE has something to find whenever you connect. The minute is counted from when the producer started.
ID Minute Where What ANOM-L1 10 to 30 fleet.telematics, trailer TRL-102 A reefer temperature excursion. The door opens, then the return air climbs through 9.2, 10.8 and 11.4 °C and stays above the 8 °C limit for about 12 minutes. It is the same profile as the cold-chain scenario of shipment SHP-50004. ANOM-L2 25 to 45 site.dock-doors, DOCK-EAST-02 A stuck sensor. It keeps sending heartbeats, but the door state, cycle count and last-change time do not move for 20 minutes. Every other door changes at least every 10 minutes. ANOM-L3 32 to 40 drone.survey at WH-SOUTH A drone count that disagrees with the mainframe. For one item, the drone counts 48 cases (one pallet) fewer than the mainframe’s on-hand balance at that moment. Every other item agrees. ANOM-L4 from 30 yard.gate-events A duplicate gate read. The first gate event after the half hour is delivered twice, with the same event_id. ANOM-L5 35 fleet.telematics, trailer TRL-105 A GPS jump. One frame puts the trailer about 380 km north of its lane, 5 seconds after and before frames on the lane, at an ordinary speed. ANOM-L6 40 to 48 drone.survey at YARD-SOUTH A perimeter finding: three frames report a gap in the north fence. The producer prints this list, with the item for ANOM-L3, when it starts.
data.the-topics#The topics:
Every topic has 3 partitions. The key is a business ID, as plain text, so a consumer can join on it without the registry. The value schema is registered under the topic name (-value). Positions are WGS84 degrees, in latitude and longitude. Times are UTC, and each record’s Kafka timestamp is the time of the event.
Topic Key What it carries How often quillmere.fleet.telematics.v1 trailer_id Position along the lane between sites, speed, heading, odometer, fuel, engine fault, reefer setpoint and return-air temperature, rear door every 5 s per trailer, 10 trailers quillmere.site.dock-doors.v1 dock_id Dock door open or closed, dock occupied, door cycle count, last change every 10 s per dock, 9 docks quillmere.site.environment.v1 sensor_id Temperature and humidity per zone: ambient, cold room, freezer, dock apron, the port’s reefer rack every 15 s per sensor, 14 sensors quillmere.site.equipment.v1 equipment_id Forklifts, AGVs and straddle carriers: position, state, battery, speed, load every 5 s per machine, 11 machines quillmere.site.energy.v1 meter_id Demand and energy per circuit: refrigeration, lighting, dock doors, chargers, reefer rack, gate every 60 s per meter, 16 meters quillmere.drone.survey.v1 flight_id Survey frames with position and altitude: case counts by rack location in the DCs, trailer counts in the yards and the port, perimeter checks every 4 s while flying; one 8-minute flight per site each hour quillmere.yard.gate-events.v1 trailer_id Trailers in and out of the yard and port gates, read by RFID or plate on each arrival and departure quillmere.yard.trailer-positions.v1 trailer_id Parked trailer’s yard slot, load state, gate-in time and dwell every 30 s per parked trailer quillmere.mainframe.orders.cdc.v1 order_id Order header changes from the order-entry mainframe every 10 s quillmere.mainframe.inventory.cdc.v1 @ On-hand and allocated cases per item and warehouse every 5 s, after a full refresh at start quillmere.fleet.sensor-readings.v1 asset_id Sensor readings: a GPS fix (metric gps_fix, latitude/longitude with geo_stated, speed, odometer) for every tractor, van and trailer; every reefer’s return air (metric temperature) with its load’s stated band (threshold_min/threshold_max) and the load spec’s allowance out of band (max_excursion_minutes), and, on a reefer trailer carrying a shipment, the load’s value (load_value, load_value_currency) every 30 s per vehicle (28), every 60 s per reefer (7) quillmere.assets.equipment-readings.v1 asset_id Sensor readings for every equipment channel of the fleet, the yards and the warehouses: tractor coolant, oil pressure, battery, brake pads, tyres; reefer return air and compressor duty; yard tractor hydraulics, gate barrier motors, reefer plug-ins; forklift batteries and motors, dock levelers, refrigeration compressors, cold and freezer rooms. Each states its limit in attributes (alarm_c, trip_c or replace_below_pct, with limit_source) every 120 s per channel (183) The two sensor-reading topics use the field names a telemetry source lands as (asset_id, observed_at, metric, value, value_stated, unit, the threshold pair with its *_stated flags, attributes). The tractors and vans run loops from their distribution centre through three customer delivery sites and back, on straight lines between the points, not on roads. A dozen channels drift towards their limit on a three-hour ramp and reset, time compressed so that minutes of the stream show the slope: coolant creeping up, brake pads wearing, a reefer’s return air leaving its 2-8 °C band, a cold room drifting off its setpoint, a refrigeration compressor running hotter.
The sites are the quickstart’s three distribution centres and their yards, at their authored addresses (Elk Grove Village IL, Plainfield IN and Edwardsville IL), and one port terminal: Quillmere Calumet Terminal, a point in the Lake Calumet port district in Chicago. The trucks run four lanes along the interstate corridors between them. The lanes are polylines through the cities on those corridors, not a road network.
data.what-it-is#What it is:
A Kafka broker on your own machine that never stops receiving events, so you can watch FACE take in a stream rather than a recording. A producer generates the quickstart estate’s operations: trucks moving between the sites, dock doors, cold rooms, forklifts, meters, drone surveys, yard gates, and the mainframe’s order and inventory changes.
The events are about the same Quillmere estate as every other quickstart: the same warehouses, yards, docks, trailers, carriers, customers and items, with the same IDs. The values are authored for the quickstart, not measured. Every record says so in its provenance field: authored quickstart estate.
The broker setup follows Confluent’s Kafka on Docker tutorial: one Apache Kafka node in KRaft mode, no ZooKeeper. A Schema Registry is added, because the values are Avro. For the recorded topics and the ksqlDB catalogue, see Apache Kafka. The connector reference is Streaming: Kafka.
FACE connects to Kafka only over SASL_SSL. The broker below speaks TLS with a certificate from a certificate authority you generate, and every client logs in with SCRAM-SHA-512. The Schema Registry answers HTTPS only, from the same authority, and every call logs in with its own user and password. FACE refuses a Kafka connection without encryption or without a login, and a registry over plain http:// or without its login.
data.what-you-need#What you need: Docker with Compose, and openssl. The producer image, face-stream-producer:1.4.0. The producer image is not on a public registry yet. Without it, steps 1 to 3 still give you a running broker and Schema Registry, but no events.

data.how-the-registries-reduce-noise-in-domai:
The inference block of expected.json states what FACE’s estate map infers from this connection twice: from the topic names and columns alone, and with the registry read added.
Names and columns alone With the Schema Registry and ksqlDB orders order.created, order.po-duplicates order.created, order.po-duplicates shipments shipment.status, shipment.latest, shipment.export.v0 shipment.status, shipment.latest cold_chain not placed reefer.alerts, coldchain.excursions freight_audit freight.invoice.posted, freight.rate-variance freight.invoice.posted, freight.rate-variance Withheld none shipment.export.v0: ksqlDB states it carries no traffic The legacy export uses the same words as the live shipment feed, so names alone place a dead topic in the shipments domain. With the registry read, ksqlDB states that the export carries no traffic, and no recorded flow ties it to a live topic, so it is withheld. The excursion table’s columns (breach_count, peak_celsius, limit_celsius) share no vocabulary with the reefer alerts they are computed from, so names alone place neither topic. Their shared Avro namespace, and field docs that name the reefer alerts, put both topics in cold_chain.

data.stand-up-the-test-system#Stand up the te:
The safety rule at the top of this page comes first: a scratch machine or a scratch cluster, never a production or platform one.
Stand up a broker with a SASL_SSL listener (SCRAM logins) and a Confluent-compatible Schema Registry that answers HTTPS only, with its own logins. FACE connects to nothing less. The live estate page stands up exactly that with Docker Compose, and writes the CA certificate (secrets/ca.crt) that the client configs below point at. Use a login that may create topics and produce.
Download the recording files listed under Download below. Create the nine topics, with 3 partitions each. client.properties is a Kafka client config for that listener (security.protocol=SASL_SSL, sasl.mechanism=SCRAM-SHA-512, the login and the CA):
for f in schemas/*-value.avsc; do kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --command-config client.properties --create --if-not-exists --topic "$(basename "$f" -value.avsc)" --partitions 3 --replication-factor 1 done Register the subjects as the registry recording has them: every version in order, then each subject’s own compatibility level. Most value schemas use TopicNameStrategy (-value). The freight invoice topic uses TopicRecordNameStrategy, and two topics also have a key subject. Set SR to your Schema Registry’s https:// URL, and SR_AUTH to a registry login as user:password:
cd schema-registry for d in subjects/*/; do s="$(basename "$d")" for v in $(jq -r '.[]' "$d/versions.json"); do jq '{schema, schemaType} | with_entries(select(.value != null))' "$d/versions/$v.json" \ | curl -fsS -u "$SR_AUTH" -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.schemaregistry.v1+json' --data @- "$SR/subjects/$s/versions" done done for f in config/*.json; do jq '{compatibility: .compatibilityLevel}' "$f" \ | curl -fsS -u "$SR_AUTH" -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.schemaregistry.v1+json' --data @- "$SR/config/$(basename "$f" .json)" done Put the records on the bus. Each line of records.jsonl is one record: its topic, key and JSON value. Write one kcat file per topic, one keyvalue line per record, then produce them. kcat.conf holds the same listener settings in librdkafka form (security.protocol=SASL_SSL, sasl.mechanisms=SCRAM-SHA-512, sasl.username, sasl.password, ssl.ca.location):
mkdir -p kcat for t in $(jq -r .topic records.jsonl | sort -u); do jq -r --arg t "$t" 'select(.topic == $t) | "\(.key | if type == "string" then . else tojson end)\t\(.value | tojson)"' records.jsonl > "kcat/$t.kcat" done for f in kcat/*.kcat; do kcat -F kcat.conf -P -b localhost:9092 -t "$(basename "$f" .kcat)" -K $'\t' -l "$f" done Add the connection in Settings › Integrations › Systems. FACE saves only a secured Kafka connection: security_protocol sasl_ssl, sasl_mechanism scram-sha-512 or scram-sha-256, a username and its password, and, when a Schema Registry is named, an https:// URL with schema_registry_username and its schema_registry_password. A broker or registry without encryption and a login is refused. The live estate page stands up a broker and registry that way and lists every setting.
Where the deployment runs ksqlDB, set the ksqldb_url extra setting. The recording’s ksqldb/ folder holds the test ksqlDB’s answers to LIST STREAMS EXTENDED;, LIST TABLES EXTENDED; and LIST QUERIES;, which are what FACE reads from it.

data.what-it-is#What it is:
An Apache Kafka cluster, with a Confluent-compatible Schema Registry and ksqlDB. In the test estate it is the event bus: order, shipment, reefer-alert and freight-invoice events, and the topics ksqlDB computes from them. The connector reference is Streaming: Kafka.
This page is the recording: a bounded set of records you load once. For a broker on your machine that keeps receiving the estate’s sensor, drone, yard and mainframe events without end, see Apache Kafka, live estate.
data.what-the-schema-registry-and-ksqldb-add#:
The registry read adds metadata, not data. It sends no Fetch and no ksqlDB SELECT or PRINT. It keeps no query text and samples no value.
Schema Registry: 11 subjects. There are nine value subjects and two key subjects. Some subjects have more than one version: the shipment status and reefer alert schemas each dropped a field in version 2, and the freight invoice schema added an optional one. Every subject’s compatibility level is stated. Most use the global BACKWARD, the freight invoice subject uses FULL_TRANSITIVE, and the legacy export uses NONE. Each value schema’s Avro namespace names its business domain: invalid.quillmere.orders, .shipments, .coldchain or .freight. ksqlDB: 9 sources and 4 persistent queries. ORDER_PO_DUPLICATES counts order-created events per customer PO and holds only the duplicate PO. SHIPMENT_LATEST keeps each shipment’s latest status. REEFER_EXCURSIONS aggregates the reefer alerts per shipment and holds only SHP-50004. INVOICE_RATE_VARIANCE flags invoices billed more than 5% over contract and holds only INV-90003. Each query records which topic flows into which. Traffic. ksqlDB states each source’s message figures. For the legacy export, LEGACY_SHIPMENT_EXPORT, it states zero messages, and no query reads or writes it.

data.stand-up-the-test-system#Stand up the te:
The safety rule at the top of this page comes first: a scratch machine or a scratch cluster, never a production or platform one.
Run an MQTT 3.1.1 broker you control, with a TLS listener (port 8883) and password logins, and a face-reader user. Eclipse Mosquitto is one open-source option: give its listener a certfile, keyfile and cafile, and a password_file. FACE refuses a broker without TLS or without a login.
Download messages.jsonl from the recording below and publish it. Each line is one message, in time order: its topic, qos, retain flag and JSON payload. With Mosquitto’s client and jq, over the same TLS listener (ca.crt is the CA that signed the broker’s certificate, and is the name on it):
jq -r '"\(.topic)\t\(.qos)\t\(.retain)\t\(.payload | tojson)"' messages.jsonl | while IFS=$'\t' read -r topic qos retain payload; do if [ "$retain" = true ]; then r=-r; else r=; fi mosquitto_pub -h -p 8883 --cafile ca.crt -u -P change-me \ -t "$topic" -q "$qos" $r -m "$payload" done Add the connection in Settings › Integrations › Systems, with broker_url set to mqtts://:8883, use_tls on and the password credential. Leave insecure_skip_verify off: FACE refuses a connection with it on. FACE subscribes to quillmere/reefer/+/temperature for the collection window.
To watch the readings arrive, open Live sensors or Devices from the connection’s card on Ask.

data: A runner is the process that executes a fetch. It dials your sources, runs the queries and reads the telemetry. The FACE control plane orchestrates, stores connections and serves the FACE app, but it does not run fetches itself. You add, edit and remove runners in Settings › Integrations › Runners. Each fetch names a runner (runner_id), and a fetch with no runner is refused with no runner is selected.
data.credentials-on-a-runner#Credentials on a:
For the managed runner, the control plane reads a connection’s credential bundle once for each dispatch (an audited read). It then seals the bundle to the runner’s in-memory key under that dispatch’s context. The runner:
opens the bundle only for a verified mesh peer uses it for that fetch never writes it to disk or logs it A restarted runner has a new key, so earlier sealed blobs cannot be opened. See /docs/security/.
data.enrolling-a-self-hosted-runner#Enrolling:
Enrolment uses RunnerEnrollmentService.Enroll, one bidirectional stream:
Get a credential. An organisation admin mints a service-account key for their own tenant (IdentityService.GenerateServiceAccountKey). Only a service-account credential can enrol a runner. A person’s session, even an admin’s, is refused with runner enrolment requires a service-account credential; a user session token cannot enrol a runner.
Configure the runner. It needs these environment variables:
Variable Meaning RUNNER_ENROLL_ADDR The FACE gRPC address as the runner can reach it. Setting it turns enrolment on. RUNNER_ENROLL_TOKEN The service-account token. It is required whenever the address is set, and the runner refuses to start without it. RUNNER_ID A stable id kept across restarts, so a reconnect reuses the same slot. Up to 64 characters from A–Z a–z 0–9 - _ .. It is generated when empty. RUNNER_NAME, RUNNER_VERSION Display only RUNNER_ENROLL_TLS TLS with system roots is on by default. false turns it off. Say hello. The first message must be RunnerHello with runner_id, name, version, capabilities (for example fetch) and load_score. Any other first message is refused.
Get accepted. FACE answers with EnrollmentAccepted:
runner_id: the tenant-namespaced id. tenant_id: taken from the verified token, never from the hello, so a runner cannot enrol into a tenant it holds no credential for. heartbeat_interval_seconds (15). Do the work. FACE pushes RunnerWorkAssignment messages, each with a dispatch_id and a RunFetchRequest. The runner answers with a RunnerWorkResult carrying the same dispatch_id and either a RunFetchResponse or an error. A result for an unknown dispatch is dropped.
Heartbeat. RunnerHeartbeat messages update load_score.
Disconnect. Closing the stream de-registers the runner. A runner that re-enrols with the same id replaces its previous stream. If the stream ends, the runner reconnects after 5 seconds.
A fetch for a tenant that has an enrolled runner is dispatched down that runner’s stream. The control plane waits up to 10 minutes for the result. If none arrives, it reports runner "…" accepted the work and has not answered within 10m0s — the run may still be in progress there. It does not retry the work on control-plane compute.
Enrolled runners are listed only to their own tenant. A runner’s name, version and capabilities are its own statements, and FACE does not verify them.
data.health#Health: List. ListRunners always lists the managed runner. Its state is RUNNING only when a live heartbeat is in the replicated registry. Otherwise it is UNKNOWN, with a description that says liveness was not observed. compute_units is 0 when capacity is not measured. Process health. GetRunnerHealth reports the answering process’s CPU, memory and goroutine count. Any metric it does not measure is named in unmeasured instead of being reported as zero.
data.keeping-fetches-off-the-control-plane#Ke: Set REQUIRE_RUNNER_ISOLATION=true to make a SQL fetch fail rather than fall back to the control plane when the runner cannot be reached. The failure reads …: runner isolation enforced but runner unreachable — refusing control-plane execution for …. The refusal appears on the fetch response as a notice as well as an error.
data.kinds-of-runner#Kinds of runner: Kind Where it runs How the control plane reaches it Managed runner (“Runink Managed Runner”) A dedicated FACE process (SERVICE_ROLE=runner) on separate compute next to the control plane The control plane dials it over mutually authenticated TLS with the platform’s rotating mesh identity. There is no plaintext fallback. Registered runner Any runner you add with an endpoint in Settings › Integrations › Runners The control plane dials that endpoint. https:// endpoints use public TLS on port 443. All others use the mesh identity. Self-hosted (enrolled) runner Your machine, inside your network, behind NAT if needed The runner dials out to FACE and holds one long-lived stream. Nothing dials in to it. On the managed path, several runners can register themselves with the platform’s replicated registry by heartbeat. A tenant’s fetches stick to one live runner so its cache stays warm, and a newly added runner starts receiving work with no configuration change.
data.warehouse-runner-settings#Warehouse runn:
Snowflake and Databricks connections can carry runner-deploy settings, such as a compute pool, image, network rule, cluster policy, node type or artifact checksum (see SQL warehouses). FACE stores and format-checks them when the connection is saved:
A value that looks like a credential is refused. runner_artifact must not contain a .. segment. runner_artifact and runner_artifact_sha256 must be given together. An organisation admin can deploy, redeploy and decommission runners from Settings › Integrations › Runners (see Runner deployment). Snowflake and Databricks targets are offered only when FACE’s runner channel is configured, because those runners connect out to FACE. Without it, the tab lists them as unavailable and says why.
data.why-data-can-stay-in-your-network#Why da: A self-hosted runner runs the whole fetch pipeline in-process on your machine. It dials your warehouses, APIs, readers and cameras from inside your network, and only the fetch result travels back over its outbound stream. Your sources never need an inbound firewall rule, a public address, or reachability from the FACE platform. Because the runner makes the connection, the two ends do not need to share an address family either.

data: FACE reads Snowflake, Databricks SQL, PostgreSQL and MySQL through their standard drivers.
data.common-behaviour#Common behaviour: Queries are read-only. Every statement must start with SELECT, WITH, SHOW, DESCRIBE, DESC or EXPLAIN. A statement that contains restricted keywords is refused. Unclosed comments and string literals are refused. Parameters are bound. Values in params are passed to the driver as bound parameters, never interpolated into the SQL. A positional parameter list may accompany only a single statement. Multi-statement batches report partial failure. If some statements in a batch are refused by the engine, the read still returns the rows from the others. The message states how many statements failed. It lists up to 8 reasons, and the count is never truncated. Credentials come from the credential bundle, never from the record. See Connections and credentials. Test dials the source. For every engine on this page, Test opens a connection and runs the driver’s Ping. A success means the endpoint answered and the credential was accepted. It does not mean the role can read any particular table. How queries arrive. In a fetch, Snowflake and Databricks run FACE’s built-in fetch template for that engine. PostgreSQL and MySQL read the business tables they expose (a sweep of their tables). Both run on the selected runner. Outside a fetch, SqlService.Execute and ExecuteSelect accept an explicit sql and params against a stored connection_id (see /docs/api/). A failure is reported as a failure. When an engine cannot be reached, the fetch reports Execution Failed for : …, with personal data masked. No other data is substituted.
data.database-tls-ssl_mode#Database TLS (\u00:
PostgreSQL reads the typed ssl_mode field. MySQL reads the ssl_mode property. Every PostgreSQL and MySQL connection must state it, and must have a username and a password credential. See Security requirements.
Value Behaviour (empty) Refused. The setting must be stated, so that it can be audited. require Encrypt without verifying the server certificate verify-ca, verify-full Encrypt and verify disable, prefer, allow Refused. These modes send data without TLS, or can fall back to it silently.
data.databricks#Databricks: Type spellings databricks Config message DatabricksConnectionConfig Settings host (the workspace host, required; https:// is assumed, and http:// is refused), http_path (required: the /sql/1.0/warehouses/… path of one SQL warehouse or cluster) Scope properties catalog (or databricks_catalog, unity_catalog), schema (or databricks_schema) Credentials personal_access_token (or token) Connection string connection_string, parsed at save time Transport Port 443, through FACE’s hardened transport. The address policy applies, and internal addresses are refused unless opted in. Test A live dial (driver ping) Explore system.information_schema columns joined to tables (metastore-wide, or one catalog when catalog is set). Declared units and PII classes come from column tags. Complete vocabularies come from CHECK (col IN (…)) constraints. Sample Default 25 rows, at most 1000 (a larger value is refused). Cells are capped at 4096 bytes. Method: FIRST_ROWS. Optional runner-deploy settings (none of them is a credential) are cluster_policy_id, node_type_id, spark_version, runner_artifact, runner_artifact_sha256, runner_scope (the name of a secret scope), service_principal (an application id, not its secret).
data.mysql#MySQL: Type spellings mysql Config message MySqlConnectionConfig Settings host, port (default 3306), database, username; ssl_mode as a property Credentials password Test A live dial (driver ping) Explore information_schema tables and columns, and declared keys from TABLE_CONSTRAINTS joined to KEY_COLUMN_USAGE Multi-statement mode is off at the driver.
data.postgresql#PostgreSQL: Type spellings postgres, postgresql Config message PostgresConnectionConfig Settings host, port (default 5432), database, username, ssl_mode Credentials password; username may also come from the bundle Test A live dial (driver ping) Explore information_schema tables and columns (up to 500 tables) and declared keys from pg_catalog.pg_constraint
data.snowflake#Snowflake: Type spellings snowflake Config message SnowflakeConnectionConfig Settings account (required), warehouse, database, schema, role, user Credentials password (or pat / token for a programmatic access token). user or username may also come from the bundle. Connection string connection_string in the form user[:password]@account/database[/schema][?param=value…], parsed at save time Transport HTTPS through FACE’s hardened transport. The address policy applies, and internal addresses are refused unless allow_internal_network=true is set. Test A live dial (driver ping) Explore INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES and .COLUMNS, scoped to database and to schema when set. Includes the table kind, column order, the account’s own type spelling, declared nullability, and ROW_COUNT (left unstated for views). Sample SAMPLE (n ROWS). Default 10 rows, at most 100, cells capped at 512 bytes. Optional runner-deploy settings (none of them is a credential) are compute_pool, image_repository, runner_image (pinned by digest, …@sha256:), network_rule, external_access_integration. See Runners.

data:
FACE connects to Kafka (and to Redpanda, which speaks the same protocol) to enumerate its topic catalogue and read declared structure from a Confluent-compatible Schema Registry. FACE implements the handshake, ApiVersions, Metadata and the SASL exchange natively. No Kafka client library is used.
Kafka connections serve the topic catalogue and Schema Registry structure through Explore.
data.explore#Explore:
Explore reads the topic catalogue (up to 5,000 topics) and, where a registry is configured, each topic’s value subject (-value). No record body is read.
Topic Columns With a registered value schema The schema’s fields, with the Avro type verbatim, nullability from the union, enum symbols as allowed values, and each doc as a description. This is declared structure. Without one None. FACE never infers fields from sampled messages. Registry not asked, or unreadable None. The schemas aspect shows asked=false or readable=false, so you can tell this case apart from “no schema”. Topic names ending in .by-.v (for example acme.orders.events.by-order_id.v1) yield a partition key, marked with a name-match basis. It is never reported as declared. Key subjects and offsets are not requested, and the aspects say so.
For Kafka, use Explore. Sample and Profile apply to the SQL warehouses.
data.settings-kafkaconnectionconfig#Settings:
Setting Meaning bootstrap_servers One or more host:port values (default port 9092). Required, and there is no default broker. List several: Test succeeds as soon as any one of them answers. topics Optional prefix filters over the catalogue. An empty list is normal and enumerates every topic the principal may see. Reading the catalogue moves no data. client_id Sent in every request header. The default is runink-face-. security_protocol sasl_ssl. Required. Unset (which means plaintext), plaintext, sasl_plaintext and ssl are refused: ssl encrypts but carries no login. sasl_mechanism scram-sha-512 or scram-sha-256. Required. SCRAM verifies the broker’s server signature and refuses the connection if it does not match. Any other mechanism is refused. username The SASL username (a setting). Required. schema_registry_url An https:// base URL. Optional: without it, topics are listed with no columns. The URL must not contain credentials. http:// is refused. schema_registry_username The registry’s HTTP-basic user. Required when a registry URL is set. ssl_ca_pem The PEM CA certificate the broker’s TLS certificate must chain to, for a broker with a private CA. Empty means the public roots. Only these roots are trusted for the broker, its host name is still checked, and a value holding a private key is refused. It is a public certificate, not a credential. The Schema Registry keeps the system roots. Credentials: password for SASL (required), and schema_registry_password for the registry (a separate credential, because the registry authenticates separately; required when a registry URL is set).
insecure_skip_verify is refused: the broker’s and the registry’s certificates are always checked. A connection that does not meet these rules cannot be saved, and a stored one is refused on every read until it is upgraded. See Security requirements.
Set allow_internal_network to control whether the connection may reach internal addresses.
data.test#Test:
Test performs a real handshake against the bootstrap servers in order: dial, TLS, ApiVersions, and the SASL exchange. It returns success on the first broker that completes it. If none does, it returns no bootstrap server answered: … with each broker’s error.
A successful Test does not establish:
that the principal may list topics, because topic authorisation is checked per topic that the Schema Registry exists or answers, because Test does not contact it that any topic holds a record
data.type-spellings#Type spellings:
kafka, redpanda, apachekafka (the “Apache Kafka” card).
Azure Event Hubs and Amazon MSK are not aliased, because they require SASL mechanisms this connector does not speak.

data:
Four connectors read physical telemetry: a sensor bus, a tag reader, a fleet tracker and a fixed probe gateway. Every protocol is implemented natively against its wire format. MQTT 3.1.1 packets, LLRP inventory rounds and Modbus-TCP register reads are written in FACE, with no third-party protocol library. All four emit one row type, SensorReading.
You add these in Settings › Integrations › Systems. Once added, each one’s card on Ask opens its live view: Live sensors and Devices for MQTT, sensor gateways, GPS and RFID. Every link must be encrypted: see each section below, and Security requirements.
Plant equipment normally lives on private networks. Set allow_internal_network on a connection to control whether it may reach internal addresses. The cloud instance-metadata service is always refused. See Networking.
data.common-rules#Common rules: An empty batch is not a success. A connector that connected and received nothing returns Success=false with connector reached and received no readings. A silent reader is reported as silent, never as “no excursions”. Zero means “use the default” for every window and cap below. It never means “collect nothing”. Values above a maximum are reduced to the maximum. Readings are sorted by observed time, then asset, then metric. What Test does not establish. A successful probe does not establish that a sensor is publishing, that an antenna is attached or aimed, that a probe is calibrated, or that any readings exist.
data.gps-and-telematics#GPS and telematics:
Type spellings gps, telematics, eld, tracker Config message GPSConnectionConfig Setting Meaning provider samsara, geotab or generic_rest (also generic, rest, http, https). If it is empty and the endpoint is https://, generic_rest is used. The nmea provider (and the nmea type) is refused: it is a raw TCP stream with no encryption. Use the tracker’s https API instead. endpoint A REST base URL, https://. Required. asset_ids Restrict to these vehicles or assets. A query may narrow further, but only within this set. lookback_minutes Default 60, maximum 7 days include_sensors Also request reefer and cargo sensor channels where the provider has them property carrier / fleet Carried onto readings Credentials by provider:
Provider Credentials Samsara api_key, token or bearer_token Geotab database, username, password (or session_id) Generic REST bearer_token / token, or api_key, or username + password Test: Samsara: one GET /fleet/vehicles/stats?types=gps&limit=1 Geotab: a Get of one Device Generic REST: one request Execute returns position fixes as readings (latitude, longitude, geo_stated), with speed and heading in attributes. It also returns sensor channels where requested. At most 5,000 readings and 20 pages. Truncation is stated in the message. REST bodies are capped at 8 MiB. Units are taken from the provider (for example Geotab’s unit-of-measure ids) and never assumed. Explore returns supported=false.
data.mqtt-sensor-bus#MQTT (sensor bus):
Type spellings mqtt, mqtts, iot, iothub, sensorbus, messagebus, iottelemetry (iot_telemetry) Config message MQTTConnectionConfig, or legacy IoTConnectionConfig with endpoint plus a comma-separated topics property Protocol MQTT 3.1.1 (protocol level 4): CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH/PUBACK, PING, DISCONNECT Setting Meaning broker_url tls://host:8883 (also ssl://, mqtts:// or wss://). Required to carry a TLS scheme. tcp://, mqtt://, ws:// and a bare host:port are refused. topics Topic filters. Required: an empty list is an error, and FACE never subscribes to # by default. A query can override the list with comma-separated filters. qos 0 or 1 (FACE subscribes at QoS 1). 2 is refused. client_id The default is a stable id derived from the connection id username A setting. Required. The password is a credential. collect_seconds The listening window: default 15 s, maximum 5 min max_messages Default 500, maximum 20,000 protocol_version 4 or 0. 5 and 3 are refused with an explanation. use_tls Required on. The broker’s certificate is always checked: insecure_skip_verify is refused. property asset_topic_segment The topic segment index that holds the asset id Credentials: password (required); username may also come from the bundle.
Test dials the broker and completes CONNECT/CONNACK within 10 s, then disconnects. It does not subscribe. Execute subscribes, listens for the window, and decodes each message: JSON objects, arrays, numbers, booleans and numeric strings become readings. When a JSON value names no metric, the metric comes from the topic’s last segment. Non-JSON payloads are kept as rows with payload_kind and a short sample. Topic, QoS and retained flags go into attributes. The connector speaks MQTT 3.1.1 over TLS, at QoS 0 or 1, with a clean session on every connect. A legacy iot connection that declares a non-MQTT protocol (such as AMQP) is refused by name. Explore returns supported=false. MQTT has no catalogue call.
data.rfid-llrp-and-vendor-rest#RFID (LLRP and:
Type spellings rfid, epc, llrp, tagreader Config message RFIDConnectionConfig Setting Meaning protocol llrp (default, also llrps) or http (also https, rest) endpoint LLRP: host or host:5084. HTTP: the reader’s event API base URL. reader_id Carried onto every reading. It defaults to the endpoint. location Where the reader physically is. It is carried onto every reading. antenna_ports Antennas to enable (1–65535). Empty means all. collect_seconds The inventory round: default 10 s, maximum 2 min max_reads Default 1,000, maximum 50,000 report_duplicates Report every sighting instead of first/last seen per EPC use_tls TLS. It is also implied by https:// or llrps://. Required for LLRP: an LLRP link without TLS is refused. LLRP has no login of its own, so TLS is all the protocol offers. property api_key_header The header for an API key (default X-API-Key) An HTTP reader’s endpoint must be https://.
Credentials for HTTP readers, tried in order:
token → Authorization: Bearer api_key → the API-key header password with the username property → HTTP Basic Test for LLRP connects and waits for the reader’s connection-attempt event. For HTTP, it makes one GET to the event API within 8 s. Execute runs an inventory round and returns one reading per tag sighting. EPC, antenna, RSSI and read count go into attributes when the reader states them. HTTP event bodies are capped at 16 MiB, and an over-cap stream is refused rather than reported as a short round. Explore returns supported=false.
data.sensor-gateway-modbus-tcp-and-http#Senso:
Type spellings sensorgateway (sensor_gateway), sensor, modbus, temperature, infrared, thermal, probe Config message SensorGatewayConnectionConfig with one or more SensorChannel Setting Meaning transport modbus_tcp (default) or http. mqtt is refused here: use an MQTT connection, which emits the same rows. endpoint Modbus: host:802, with use_tls on. HTTP: an https:// base URL. unit_id The Modbus unit (slave) id channels Required. There is no safe default register. collect_seconds The sampling pass: default 15 s, maximum 5 min poll_interval_seconds The interval between polls: default 5 s. It is carried as sampling_interval_seconds. use_tls Modbus/TCP Security. Required for Modbus: Modbus has no login of its own, so a gateway without TLS is refused. Each SensorChannel states its own mapping:
Field Meaning asset_id, device_id What is measured, and by which device metric temperature, infrared, humidity, shock, door or battery. It is written verbatim to the reading. address Modbus: the starting register. HTTP: the JSON path of the value. register_type holding (default), input, coil or discrete data_type int16 (default), uint16, int32, uint32 or float32. Word-swapped variants are accepted. scale, offset value = raw * scale + offset. A scale of 0 means 1. unit Written to the reading’s unit, for example C, F, %RH or g threshold_min / _stated, threshold_max / _stated, threshold_source The band the product spec states, and where it is stated. Leave these unset when nobody stated one. HTTP credentials: token, api_key, or username + password.
Test connects and reads the first channel. For HTTP, it fetches the document and resolves the first channel’s path. A failure names the channel, register and unit. A Modbus exception response is reported as the device’s own refusal. Execute polls every channel at the interval for the whole pass. The raw register and count go into attributes. Explore returns supported=false. Modbus has no register map, so the channel list you configure is the schema.
data.the-sensorreading-row#The SensorReading:
Every telemetry connector, and the Flipper edge reader, returns rows with these columns, in this order:
Column Meaning asset_id The thing measured, for example REEFER-12 device_id The thing measuring reading_id, window_id The reading id, and the monitoring run it belongs to reference, carrier Shipment or monitoring reference and carrier, only when the source states them observed_at RFC 3339, UTC observed_at_source Whose clock: device, gateway, or received (receipt time, used when the wire carries no timestamp) metric, value, value_stated, unit The measurement. value_stated=false marks a row with no numeric payload (a heartbeat, a door event, a tag sighting). Such rows are kept, because a gap in a feed is evidence too. threshold_min, threshold_min_stated, threshold_max, threshold_max_stated, threshold_source The band the source stated, and where sampling_interval_seconds The configured cadence. 0 means the source did not say. max_excursion_minutes, max_excursion_minutes_stated The excursion allowance stated by the spec load_reference, load_value, load_value_stated, load_value_currency The load on the asset, where named. load_value is money only with an ISO 4217 load_value_currency stated by the source; a load’s weight (load_weight, payload_weight, net_weight, a numeric load) never fills it and is kept in attributes as load_weight / load_weight_field / load_weight_unit location, latitude, longitude, geo_stated Where the reading was taken source, transport The connection type and the protocol actually spoken quality The source’s own quality flag. FACE never computes it. attributes Everything else the protocol knew, such as EPC and antenna, speed and heading, register and raw count, or topic
data.the-stated-fields#The \u003ccode\u003e*S:
In the protocol format FACE uses, “the probe read 0 °C” and “the row has no reading” look the same, and in a cold chain they are opposite facts. So every connector sets a *_stated flag from whether the source carried the field, never from whether the value is non-zero:
A threshold is never assumed. FACE does not assume 2–8 °C because an asset is called REEFER. A band that no one stated stays unstated, and analysis reports that the threshold was not stated. A unit that is absent stays absent. FACE never assumes Celsius. A position without geo_stated is not a position. Consumers must read a value only when its *_stated flag is true. See /docs/analysis/ for how these rows feed temperature-excursion and claims evidence.

data:
FACE reads the web in two ways:
a web connection reads one configured page as rows of text the crawler service scrapes a page, or runs a bounded crawl from a seed URL
data.crawler-service#Crawler service:
CrawlerService exposes:
RPC Behaviour Scrape Reads one url and returns its title, main content and metadata. render_js is reserved. Crawl Starts from url and visits linked pages, returning a crawl_id, a status and pages_visited. GetCrawlStatus Returns the pages of a crawl: url, title, content_snippet and status for each. Crawl bounds:
url must be an absolute http(s) URL with a host. depth: 0 means the default of 2. The maximum is 5, and a negative value is refused. limit (pages): 0 means the default of 10. The maximum is 500, and a negative value is refused. allow_external: false by default. The crawl then stays on the seed’s host and its subdomains, on the same port. Only http(s) links are followed.
data.web-connection#Web connection: Type spellings webtelemetry (web_telemetry), webpage (the “Webpage” card), web, url, website Settings (properties) url (also endpoint, target_url, page_url, website, host) Schemes https only. http:// is refused, and a bare address is read as https. Internal addresses Refused unless allow_internal_network=true is set on the connection. Set it to read an intranet page. Execute fetches exactly one page and follows no links: 30-second timeout, body capped at 8 MiB. At most 5 redirects, on the same host only. Only text and HTML are accepted. A document or image is refused, with a pointer to the file path. FACE extracts the readable text and splits it into chunks of up to 2,048 characters, with at most 400 chunks. Rows have the columns url, final_url, fetched_at, http_status, content_type, title, chunk_index, chunk_count, chunk_chars, content, truncated, source and transport. truncated is true when the body or the chunk count hit its cap. Test fetches the page, reading at most 64 KiB, within 15 s, and applies the same address and redirect rules. Explore returns supported=false. The connector reads one page by design. The request’s User-Agent is Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; RuninkFACE/1.0) unless the operator sets SCRAPER_USER_AGENT.

data:
A model card describes one of FACE’s agents in plain language: what it is for, what it reads, what it hands a person, who has to approve it, which model it runs on, and where it stops. There is one card for each kind of work you meet in FACE. What an agent finds shows on Ask, its options on Options, and what it drafts for approval on Actionable Twins. Several cards cover more than one agent, because those agents do one job together.
These cards are written for buyers, evaluators and operators. The mechanics behind them are on the Analysis & evidence pages, which these cards link to rather than repeat.
data.facts-shared-by-every-card#Facts shared:
Models. FACE sends each model call to one of three tiers on the deployment’s model plane, chosen by the kind of task (see Sovereign models):
General reasoning: most agents. Code: rule checks written as code. Vision: documents and images; it starts on demand. Each tier serves the deployment’s own models.
Not everything is a model. Many of the figures on these cards are fixed arithmetic over cited records: evidence documents, the dock triage of returns, forecasts, the approval policy. A model may phrase a result only after it has been determined. See Evidence documents.
Where inference runs. Every agent calls the model plane of its own FACE deployment: Runink’s shared machines on the Lite plan, the customer’s own cloud or servers on Dedicated and Enterprise. FACE calls no outside AI service on any plan. Records an agent reads are passed to the model as fenced, untrusted data, never as instructions (see AI safety). The connections you configure still reach their own systems, and an approved action, such as an email sent through a connected account, goes where that action says.
Guardrails. Each agent’s requests are checked against its OpenBias guardrail rules before a prompt reaches the model, and each proposed action passes the judging ladder. Both are described in Agents & oversight and AI safety, including the scope of each.
data.how-to-read-a-card#How to read a card:
Every card has the same sections:
What it does: one sentence, then the jobs it handles. What it reads: the records, documents and systems it takes in. What it produces: what you get back, and in what form. Human oversight: what a person approves, and what the agent can never do by itself. Model: the base model it runs on. Where it runs and data handling: where inference happens. Guardrails: the policies it follows, in plain words. How to read its results: what a result shows, what stays with a person, and when it declines or says data is missing. To see what each agent produces on real data, load the quickstart estate and ask about it on Ask.
data.one-rule-for-every-card#One rule for eve: FACE drafts. A person decides. Every claim, short-pay, filing, order, quarantine, remediation and repair that an agent proposes is a recommendation for a named approver. Nothing is sent, filed, paid or settled until someone with the authority approves it, and the server records who did. The one exception is FACE’s own operational self-healing: restarting, isolating, rolling back or scaling FACE itself runs automatically from a fixed list, and an operator can switch it off. The approval tiers and the hash-chained decision log are described in Auditability & lineage and Agents & oversight.
data.the-cards#The cards: Card What it helps with Base model Claims & recovery Shortage, OS&D and SLA claims, filing windows and the letter for approval. General Freight invoice audit Carrier invoices against the rate confirmation, SLA credits and spend. General Customs & trade documents Customs holds, document cross-checks and draft trade documents. General Compliance review Policy against practice, framework checks, personal data and remediation. General, plus code for code checks Insurance claim files Assembling the cargo claim file for an adjuster. General (documents use no model) Cold chain & telemetry Temperature excursions, sensor faults, site thresholds and custody. General Maintenance Equipment trending towards a limit its feed states. General Stock & demand Reorder decisions, forecasts and purchase orders for approval. General (forecasts use no model) Returns Return windows, quantities and disposition by your policy. General (dock triage uses no model) Yard & transport Yard capacity, border dwell, demurrage, custody and route ranking. General Options & approvals The options for a decision, scored, and the approval tier for each action. General (option scoring and approval policy use no model) Field readings (edge) Writing up a handheld reader’s site walk. General Data posture Grouping your tables into domains and grading their readiness. General Voice dispatch Short spoken answers for drivers, with the call logged. General, plus the voice tier Documents & plans (vision) Camera frames, photographed forms and floor-plan images. Vision model, starts on demand Self-healing FACE’s own health: restart, isolate, roll back or scale, automatically. General Claims leakage Recoverable losses, credits and short-pays that never became a claim, handed to claims recovery. General Fraud indicators Patterns worth a reviewer’s look, with evidence and a likelihood band; never an accusation. General Freight market analyst Each lane against its own history and public fuel prices; re-bid and consolidation candidates. General Counterparty background check Public registry and sanctions findings on a carrier, shipper or broker, for review. Businesses only. General Customer analysis Cost to serve, service performance, claims, payment behaviour and concentration per business account. General

data: Agent: the claims leakage agent (claims_leakage in ExecuteLoop), with the CLAIMS_LEAKAGE evidence document and the ReviewClaimsLeakage call.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Never invents a figure. A missing amount is shown as not stated, never as zero. Refuses to inflate a recoverable amount or move a delivery date or deadline. Refuses to file, serve or deduct without the approver. Refuses to waive recovery against a favoured or related party. Each drafted step is checked by these rules as output, before it reaches you.
data.how-to-read-its-results#How to read its: It works from your records. A credit or payment that is not in a connected ledger cannot be seen, so “not received” is only reported when the ledger is connected. A concealed-damage window is calendared only when your terms state one. Identified money is not recovered money. Only what a counterparty pays back or credits is recovered.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: A claims handler or accounts-payable manager approves every recovery on the card it points to. Approval seals the evidence document; rejection needs a reason. The agent never files or serves a claim, sends a notice, takes a short-pay or deduction, or pays anything. A computed deadline is an input for the person deciding, not legal advice.
data.model#Model:
The deployment’s general reasoning tier.
The events, amounts and deadlines are fixed arithmetic over cited records. No model computes them. The agent orders the events and phrases the next step; the server copies amounts and handoffs from the card and drops any step that names a card, action or approver it cannot stand behind.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It finds money your own records show is recoverable and has not been recovered, puts the most urgent first, and drafts the next step for the person who approves the recovery. Its jobs:
Losses never claimed. A shortage or damage on the receiving record with no claim and no dispute file for the shipment. Claims not served. A claim on file where the correspondence shows no written notice sent to the carrier, with the filing deadline from the delivery date. Credits not received. Service credits an SLA audit computed, or credits a counterparty promised, that the credits ledger shows received short or not at all. Short-pays not taken. An invoice the rate-confirmation audit found overbilled that accounts payable paid in full. Concealed-damage windows. Goods signed for subject to inspection with no inspection recorded, and the notice window your terms state. Each event points to the recovery card that already drafts the claim: the OS&D report, the notice of intent, the rate-confirmation audit or the SLA audit. The claim is approved there, in the existing claims recovery flow.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: A CLAIMS_LEAKAGE evidence document per event on Actionable Twins (claims play), with the evidence bundle of the recovery card it points to, the amount at stake computed from cited records, and the earliest deadline with the rule that set it. From ReviewClaimsLeakage: the events due within a horizon you choose (past-due first), the total the cards state, and, if you ask, a drafted next step per event. Each step uses one of five actions (open the recovery draft, follow up a credit, review a short-pay, schedule an inspection, escalate to a claims handler) and names its approver.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Receiving (OS&D) records, the claims feed, dispute correspondence, carrier invoices with their rate confirmations, SLA scorecards, and two ledgers you tag as evidence sources: accounts-payable payments and credits. Where the ledger an event rests on is not connected, that event is not reported: a record nobody looked for is not evidence that it does not exist.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane: Runink’s shared machines on Lite, your own cloud or servers on Dedicated and Enterprise. No outside AI service is called on any plan. Your records reach the model as fenced, untrusted data. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the claims agent (claims in ExecuteLoop), with the claims and recovery evidence documents.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: Never invents a figure. A missing rate or document is named as missing, and no amount is given in its place. Does not decide or score claims on the basis of a claimant’s name, demographics or location, and does not lowball settlements for particular areas. Does not fabricate weather events or disruptions to build a force majeure defence. Does not build defamatory profiles of carriers, and does not scrape partner portals or private systems without authorisation. Stays on claims and recovery work; warehouse routing and macro forecasting belong to other agents.
data.how-to-read-its-results#How to read its: It works from your records. Rates come from your contract file, and a rate that isn’t in it is reported as not stated. It doesn’t establish liability. A claim document assembles the file; the carrier, an adjuster or a court decides. A pattern that looks like return abuse is a lead for a person to check, not a finding of fraud. When a source could not be read, the document records the figure as absent with a reason, such as NO_BACKING_RECORD or NOT_STATED_ON_DOCUMENT.
data.human-oversight#Human oversight: A claims handler approves every claim letter, dispute and demand before it reaches a carrier. Approval seals the evidence document; rejection needs a reason. The agent never files a claim, contacts a carrier or withholds a payment on its own. A computed deadline is an input for the person deciding, not legal advice.
data.model#Model:
The deployment’s general reasoning tier.
The figures in the evidence documents (amounts, units, deadlines) are fixed arithmetic over cited records. No model computes them. A model may phrase the narrative only after they are set.
data.what-it-does#What it does:
It puts a freight claim together from your own shipping records and drafts the paperwork for a person to approve. Its jobs:
Shortage at delivery. Compares the manifest weight with the weighbridge reading and the counts received, and works out what is short and what it is worth. Over, short and damaged receipts. Compares the purchase order, the bill of lading and the receiving count, and prepares the OS&D report. Filing windows. Works out the notice and suit dates from the delivery date and the named regime, and orders open claims by the earliest deadline. Disputes and recovery. Prepares the notice of intent to claim, the statement of position and the subrogation demand. Recovery procedures. Ranks the recovery work with the most money at stake first, for example SLA breach refunds, accessorial and duplicate-charge disputes, and return patterns worth a closer look.
data.what-it-produces#What it produces: Evidence documents from the closed vocabulary: OSD_REPORT, NOTICE_OF_INTENT_TO_CLAIM, STATEMENT_OF_POSITION and SUBROGATION_DEMAND. Each figure cites the record it came from, and each deadline names the rule that set it. See Evidence documents. Action cards on Actionable Twins (claims play), each with one proposed next step, such as “send this claim letter to the carrier”. A short recovery plan: two or three procedures, ranked by money recovered, each tied to the records behind it.
data.what-it-reads#What it reads: Manifests, bills of lading, purchase orders, goods-received records, weighbridge events, carrier tracking milestones, SLA records, invoices and the business rules that Rules Recon found in your data. It can run read-only queries against the connection a run was started with. Other agents can hand it a sub-task with delegate_to_claims.
data.where-it-runs-and-data-handling#Where it: On the deployment’s own model plane: Runink’s shared machines on Lite, your own cloud or servers on Dedicated and Enterprise. No outside AI service is called on any plan. Your records reach the model as fenced, untrusted data. See Facts shared by every card.

data: Agent: the telemetry agent (telemetry in ExecuteLoop), with the TEMPERATURE_EXCURSION and CHAIN_OF_CUSTODY_AUDIT evidence documents.
data.guardrails#Guardrails: No stated band, no breach. FACE never assumes a threshold the source didn’t provide, and never borrows an industry norm. A missing reading is “not measured”, never zero. A gap in the log is reported as a gap. Refuses to alter, suppress or fabricate sensor, GPS, speed, fuel or driver records. Refuses to bypass hazardous-goods segregation rules or crane safety locks.
